Buttermilk Falls State Park in Ithaca: the Gorge Trail climbs about 600 feet past pools and several waterfalls to Pinnacle Rock, with many stone steps; the park is open dawn to dusk, so call the park office for current trail status
If time allows before heading home, Cornell Botanic Gardens' gardens and natural areas are free and open dawn to dusk year-round

title: Fort Worth Stockyards to Waco, Texas
best_time_description: Spring and fall keep the outdoor time in Cameron Park and along the river comfortable; Texas summers are hot.
description: A cowboy-district evening in Fort Worth, then a Waco weekend of Magnolia, the Brazos riverfront and an Ice Age dig site. Suits friends who like walkable stops and an easy pace.

days.title: Fort Worth Stockyards
activities: Fort Worth Herd cattle drive in the Stockyards, listed on the district's own site as running every day at 11:30 am and 4:00 pm
Walk the Stockyards National Historic District around Cowtown Coliseum
Check the Stockyards events page for rodeo dates at Cowtown Coliseum and concerts at Billy Bob's Texas

days.title: Waco: Magnolia and the Brazos Riverfront
activities: Magnolia Market at the Silos: the market and grounds (check Magnolia's Visit page for current hours, as Sunday and holiday hours can differ)
Waco Suspension Bridge, completed in 1870, between Indian Spring Park and Martin Luther King, Jr. Park
Branding the Brazos sculptures and the Riverwalk beside the Brazos River

days.title: Waco Mammoth and Cameron Park
activities: Waco Mammoth National Monument: open daily 9 am to 5 pm, closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day; Dig Shelter access is by ticket only, per the National Park Service
Cameron Park trails above the Brazos River; City of Waco lists park hours as 6 am to midnight
Drive home from Waco

title: Enchanted Rock & the Hill Country Backroads: Fredericksburg Long Weekend
best_time_description: Spring and fall suit the granite-dome hike and the backroads best; summer afternoons on exposed rock are hot, so go early if you travel then.
description: A weekend base in Fredericksburg for a granite-dome hike at Enchanted Rock, the dance hall at Luckenbach, and a presidential boyhood home in Johnson City. Suits friends who want fresh air and small-town stops more than wine tastings.

days.title: Fredericksburg: Main Street and the Pacific War
activities: National Museum of the Pacific War (open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Wednesday to Monday, closed Tuesdays; the Pacific Combat Zone closes at 3 p.m.)
Stroll Main Street's shops and galleries, noting that some close early in the evening
Visitor Center at 302 E. Austin St. for current events and maps

days.title: Enchanted Rock and Luckenbach
activities: Hike the granite dome at Enchanted Rock State Natural Area; TPWD says advance day-pass reservations are required on weekends, school breaks and holidays, and the park often fills to capacity
Luckenbach Texas: the general store, bar and dance hall (listed hours run daily, check the live-music calendar for the evening)

days.title: Johnson City and Pedernales Falls
activities: Lyndon B. Johnson National Historical Park in Johnson City: the Boyhood Home and the Johnson Settlement (check the park's page or call 830 868-7128 for current hours and tour rules)
Pedernales Falls State Park: view the falls (TPWD says swimming and wading are not allowed in the falls area) and reserve a day pass in advance, since the park often reaches capacity

title: Galena and the Mississippi Palisades, Illinois
best_time_description: Late spring for green bluffs and fall for color along the Mississippi bluffs; Grant Home tours are seasonal, so check the season before you pick your dates.
description: A historic river town and two bluff-and-canyon state parks in the Driftless corner of northwest Illinois. It suits friends who want an easy walkable town evening, one big hiking day and a history stop before heading home.

days.title: Galena: Main Street
activities: Settle into Galena and walk Main Street, the town's historic shopping street
Pick up a Galena Country Passport Trail (themed self-guided trails) from the visitor bureau to plan the weekend

days.title: Mississippi Palisades State Park
activities: Walk the short surfaced paths to Ozzie's Point, Louis' Point and Lookout Point for river overlooks
Hike the wider North System trails (High Point, Aspen); the narrow South System trails run close to the bluff and are hazardous when wet
Hiking trails and the day-use area close for the three-day firearm deer season, the weekend before Thanksgiving weekend, so avoid those dates

days.title: Grant Home and Apple River Canyon
activities: Interpreter-led tour of the Ulysses S. Grant Home State Historic Site, open Wednesday through Sunday with off-season tours by reservation only from November 1; confirm hours on granthome.org or 815-777-3310
Apple River Canyon State Park: pick a trail from Pine Ridge, Tower Rock, River Route, Sunset or the accessible Primrose Trail, and stay on the trail
Picnic at one of the four riverside picnic areas before the drive home

title: Galveston and the Upper Texas Coast Weekend
best_time_description: Spring and fall are the comfortable shoulders for paddling and birding on the coast; summer is hot and humid, and the ferry can have long waits at peak times.
description: A Gulf Coast island weekend for friends who want salt air, bay-side paddling, a pyramid-shaped aquarium and a free ferry ride to the quieter Bolivar Peninsula. Suits groups who like a mix of beach, birds and old-port streets.

days.title: Galveston Island State Park
activities: Arrive at Galveston Island State Park, which runs from the Gulf beach to the bay
Walk to the bay-side observation tower for water birds (the park's bay side is its birding area)
Check the park's page for its three bay-side paddling trails and ranger-led paddling tours

days.title: Moody Gardens and the Strand
activities: Moody Gardens: the Aquarium Pyramid and Rainforest Pyramid (the site says its attractions are open 365 days a year; check its daily hours page)
Galveston Railroad Museum in the old railroad depot, check the museum's own page for current days and hours
Evening walk through the Strand Historic District, the Victorian-era port district downtown

days.title: Ferry to Bolivar Peninsula
activities: Take the TxDOT Galveston-Port Bolivar ferry (toll-free, runs 24 hours; crossing about 20 minutes, waits can exceed two hours in busy seasons, and service can be reduced in severe weather)
Bolivar Flats Shorebird Sanctuary at the southern tip of the peninsula, a Houston Audubon sanctuary; confirm access and tide conditions with Houston Audubon first
Fort Travis Seashore Park near the ferry landing, a historic military site

title: Gettysburg Battlefield & Catoctin Foothills
best_time_description: Mid-October is the sweet spot for autumn color and the end of apple season, while April brings orchard blossom and May and September are mild for walking the battlefield.
description: A weekend of Civil War history on the Gettysburg battlefield, a slow detour through Adams County apple country, and a woodland finish in the Catoctin Mountains and Frederick. It suits friends who want a mix of history, easy walks and small-town wandering.

days.title: Gettysburg: Museum and Visitor Center
activities: Start at the National Park Service Museum and Visitor Center on Baltimore Pike; the building is free to enter, while the museum, the film and the Cyclorama painting of Pickett's Charge are ticketed (check opening hours with the park)
Drive the battlefield roads, which the park says are open daily from 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset

days.title: Little Round Top and Adams County apple country
activities: Walk Little Round Top, reopened by the park in June 2024 after a rehabilitation project with new trail alignments and signage
Pick a few stops on the battlefield auto tour, then spend the afternoon among the orchards around Biglerville
Visit the National Apple Museum at 154 West Hanover Street, Biglerville; in the 2026-27 off-season it is open by appointment only (call 717-677-4556) and admission is free

days.title: Catoctin Mountain: Cunningham Falls and the road home via Frederick
activities: Walk the half-mile Lower Trail to Cunningham Falls in Cunningham Falls State Park (William Houck Area, west of Thurmont); stay on marked trails and note that swimming at the falls is prohibited

Optional rock-outcrop hike at neighboring Catoctin Mountain Park, whose East Side trails reach Chimney Rock, Wolf Rock and Hog Rock (no dogs on the rock formations; check trail conditions with the park)
Finish in Frederick at the National Museum of Civil War Medicine, 48 East Patrick Street (Mon-Sat 10-5, Sun 11-5, last gallery entry 4 pm, closed some holidays), then stroll Carroll Creek Park

title: Hermann and the Missouri River Wine Country, Missouri
best_time_description: Fall for vineyard season and Hermann's month-long Oktoberfest, spring and early summer for easy days on the Katy Trail.
description: A weekend of hilltop wineries, the Katy Trail and German-settler history along the Missouri River, from Augusta to Hermann with a riverfront stop in Washington on the way home. It suits friends who like an easy pace, tasting rooms and a bit of cycling.

days.title: Augusta: Vineyards and the Katy Trail
activities: Walk or ride a stretch of the Katy Trail from the Augusta Trailhead (mile marker 66.3), with parking at the trailhead, Augusta Winery and Klondike Park
Klondike Park, a St. Charles County park with a fishing lake, a Missouri River boat ramp and white silica sand around the lake
Taste at the hilltop Montelle Winery or the historic Mount Pleasant Estates (established 1859); check each winery's own page for hours

days.title: Hermann: German Heritage and Cellars
activities: Deutschheim State Historic Site: guided tours at 10 a.m., 12:30 p.m. and 2:30 p.m. daily April 1 to October 31, Thursday to Sunday only November 1 to March 31 (closed on state holidays); grounds open sunrise to sunset
Hermannhof Winery, which describes ten stone cellars in a historic building; its own page lists tasting-room hours
Stone Hill Winery, known for the nation's largest series of cellars by its own account; its page lists daily winery hours
Cycle from town over the Missouri River Bridge bike lane to the McKittrick Katy Trail trailhead, about 2 miles north of Hermann according to Missouri State Parks

days.title: Hermann to Washington: Riverfront and Home
activities: Morning in Hermann: the Visitor Information Center in the Amtrak station at 301 Wharf Street (listed as open daily; check Visit Hermann) for a walk through the historic town
Washington's Riverfront Park on the Missouri River, with picnic pavilions and a 10-foot asphalt trail for walking or cycling
Lions Lake in Washington, with a 1-mile walking trail around the water

title: Hudson Valley: Beacon, Hyde Park and Olana
best_time_description: Late spring for green hillsides and early autumn into October for foliage; summer suits river paddling, and winter shortens daylight and park hours.
description: A river-valley long weekend for friends who like a good museum, an easy hill hike and a grand estate: Beacon's riverfront and Main Street, Mount Beacon, then Hyde Park and the Olana landscape above the Hudson.

days.title: Beacon: Long Dock Park and Main Street
activities: Walk the riverfront at Scenic Hudson's Long Dock Park (23 Long Dock Rd), open dawn to dusk, with a pavilion, viewing deck and train access
Stroll Main Street in the evening

days.title: Beacon: Dia and Mount Beacon
activities: Dia Beacon, the contemporary art museum at 3 Beekman Street: it keeps a limited weekly schedule with closed weekdays, so check the Dia calendar and plan this day around it

Mount Beacon Park, free and open year-round dawn to dusk: a steep climb up stairs along the course of the old Beacon Incline Railway, with switchbacks above, to a summit view and a 60-foot climb up the South Mount Beacon fire tower
Evening in Rhinebeck village

days.title: Hyde Park and Olana, then home
activities: Vanderbilt Mansion National Historic Site in Hyde Park (4097 Albany Post Road): no entrance fee, with terraced formal gardens and a Hudson River overlook; check the National Park Service tickets and tours page for mansion tour times
Olana State Historic Site near Hudson: the grounds are free and open daily from 8:00 AM to sunset, while house tour hours vary by season, so check olana.org or call 518-751-0344

title: Joshua Tree & Palm Springs, California
best_time_description: Cooler months. The National Park Service calls October through May the busy season at Joshua Tree and describes summer heat as a very serious safety risk, so autumn through spring suits both the boulder walks and the canyon hikes.
description: Two nights in the Mojave: Joshua Tree's boulder-strewn short trails and desert overlooks, then Palm Springs for a palm-oasis canyon and a cable-car ride up the mountain. Suits friends who want easy hikes, big views and a pool to come back to.

days.title: Joshua Tree: Hidden Valley and Keys View
activities: Hidden Valley Nature Trail, a 1-mile loop through a boulder-ringed valley (the NPS suggests arriving by 9 a.m. on busy weekends and holidays; little shade and no cell service)
Keys View, a 0.25-mile paved loop to an overlook (the upper path is steep; the park is open 24 hours a day)
Bring all water and food: the NPS says there are no grocery stores, restaurants or lodging inside the park

days.title: Joshua Tree: Barker Dam and Cholla Cactus Garden
activities: Barker Dam, an easy 1.1-mile loop past the historic dam (water depends on rainfall) with a rock art site to view from a distance
Skull Rock, a 1.7-mile loop on the NPS trail list
Cholla Cactus Garden, a 0.25-mile loop
Leave the park by the south entrance at Cottonwood toward Palm Springs

days.title: Palm Springs: Indian Canyons and the Aerial Tramway
activities: Indian Canyons (Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians): palm-lined Andreas and Palm Canyons; hours change by season, so check the Indian Canyons hours page and the last-vehicle entry time
Palm Springs Aerial Tramway up to the mountain station; check the operator's hours page for first and last tram and buy tickets in advance for busy days
If time is short, choose one: canyon walk in the morning or the tram, then head home

title: Pennsylvania Wilds: Cook Forest, Kinzua Bridge & Oil Creek
best_time_description: Late September through October for fall color along the Clarion River and Kinzua Gorge; early summer works for river tubing and the Sawmill Center season.
description: Old-growth pines, a railroad viaduct turned sky walk and the birthplace of the oil industry, all in the forested northwest of the state. Suits friends who would rather hike and wander small towns than chase a city.

days.title: Cook Forest State Park
activities: Forest Cathedral, old-growth white pines and hemlocks (a National Natural Landmark; the park is open daily, sunrise to sunset)
Walk the Clarion River shoreline, a 13-mile stretch through the park popular for canoeing, kayaking and tubing

days.title: Kinzua Bridge and the Allegheny National Forest
activities: Walk the Kinzua Bridge Sky Walk, 600 feet out on the remaining towers of the viaduct a 2003 tornado partly destroyed, with a partial glass platform at the end
Visitor center at Kinzua Bridge State Park with self-guided exhibits; the skywalk has been closed in stretches during a multi-year rehabilitation, so check the park's page for current dates
Hike the Tionesta Scenic Area, a Forest Service trail into old-growth hemlock and beech in the Allegheny National Forest

days.title: Titusville: Drake Well and Oil Creek
activities: Drake Well Museum and Park, the birthplace of the modern petroleum industry (ticketed; open Wednesday to Sunday April through October, Friday to Sunday November through March, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.)
Oil Creek State Park, where interpretation covers the oil boomtowns and early transportation (open daily, sunrise to sunset)
Head home to Pittsburgh

title: Madison, Baraboo & Devil's Lake, Wisconsin
best_time_description: Summer into early fall: Circus World runs its performance season in summer, the Crane Foundation's guided tours are daily in June to August, and Devil's Lake is busiest on summer and fall weekends, so go early.
description: A city-meets-nature long weekend: Frank Lloyd Wright's lakeside Monona Terrace in Madison, a full day on the quartzite bluffs of Devil's Lake, then cranes and circus history in Baraboo. It suits friends who want one big hike day between two easy, museum-style days.

days.title: Madison: Monona Terrace and Henry Vilas Zoo
activities: Monona Terrace Community and Convention Center, the lakeside building Frank Lloyd Wright first proposed in 1938 (building open daily 8 am to 5 pm except posted closure dates; check the public tour schedule)
Rooftop gardens at Monona Terrace (Sunday to Thursday 8 am to 10 pm, Friday and Saturday 8 am to midnight, closed in bad weather)
Henry Vilas Zoo, open daily 9:30 am to 5 pm per the zoo (hours may vary on holidays), if you arrive Saturday morning

days.title: Devil's Lake State Park
activities: Arrive early: the DNR says weekend parking lots from May to October often fill before 9 am, and a vehicle admission sticker is required (buy it ahead of time)
East Bluff Trail (1.7 miles, rated most difficult by the DNR) with the steep Balanced Rock trail and the short Devil's Doorway spur
Grottos Trail (0.7 miles, level gravel) and the Nature Center in the historic clubhouse
Parfrey's Glen State Natural Area: a 0.7-mile trail into a narrow gorge; stay on the trail, no food, drink or pets

days.title: Baraboo: Cranes and Circus World
activities: International Crane Foundation's Crane Discovery Center: open daily 9 am to 5 pm from May 1 to October 31, last entry 4:30 pm; guided tours daily June to August, weekends in May, September and October

Circus World, on the original Ringling Bros. Circus Winter Quarters (a National Historic Landmark): hours are seasonal and live performances run only in the summer season, so check the Wisconsin Historical Society's plan page for dates before you go

title: Mendocino Coast, California
best_time_description: Spring for headland wildflowers and winter for the gray whale migration, both noted by California State Parks; coastal weather changes quickly, so pack layers.
description: A north-coast weekend of a working lighthouse, river redwoods, cliff-top headlands and a glass-strewn beach. It suits friends who want sea air and short walks over a packed schedule.

days.title: Point Arena Lighthouse and Navarro River Redwoods
activities: Point Arena Lighthouse: tower tours run daily about every 20 minutes, with the last around 3 p.m. per the lighthouse's own site (an older page, so confirm hours before you go)
Navarro River Redwoods State Park on Highway 128, second-growth redwoods along the river, with the Navarro Visitor Center in the historic Captain Fletcher's Inn
Swim, kayak or just picnic at Navarro Beach where the river meets the Pacific (the park page lists it as open with restrictions, so check its alerts)

days.title: Mendocino Headlands and Russian Gulch
activities: Mendocino Headlands State Park: cliff-top trails past sea arches and grottos, plus the Ford House visitor center and Big River Beach (day use, free admission per the park page)
Russian Gulch State Park: the 0.75-mile Headlands Trail to the Devil's Punchbowl, a collapsed sea cave (day use 6 a.m. to sunset)
Fern Canyon Trail to the 36-foot waterfall, if open: the park page notes a closed portion of this trail, so check the alert first

days.title: Fort Bragg: Glass Beach and MacKerricher
activities: Glass Beach at the south end of MacKerricher State Park, once a municipal dump; look and photograph only, because State Parks forbids removing the glass
MacKerricher State Park (open 6 a.m. to sunset): free seal-watching stations and the Haul Road boardwalk, which the park lists as wheelchair accessible
Check the park's alerts before you go: Laguna Point parking is closed at times for road repair

title: Mississippi River Bluffs: Red Wing to Winona
best_time_description: Late spring and early autumn suit the bluff hikes and the Wabasha eagle center, whose listed schedule runs March through October; Frontenac's DNR page names spring and fall as its strongest birding.
description: Three days down the Mississippi bluff towns, from a Red Wing summit hike to the Lake Pepin overlooks, live eagles at Wabasha and Winona's river-bluff lookouts. It suits friends who want river views, short hikes and small-town stops instead of a big city.

days.title: Red Wing: Barn Bluff and Main Street
activities: Walk up He Mni Can (Barn Bluff) from the trailhead memorials at the base of the bluff; Visit Red Wing calls it one of the best-known natural features along the upper Mississippi
Visit the Red Wing Shoe Museum and the world's largest boot at the flagship store on Main Street (check the store's hours before you go)

days.title: Frontenac, Lake City and Wabasha along Lake Pepin
activities: Hike Frontenac State Park: the Bluff Side Trail drops by stairs and switchbacks to near water level and climbs back to the bluff top, and the picnic-area and Old Frontenac overlooks look out over Lake Pepin (the bluff trails are not for winter use)
Walk the River Walk and Ohuta Park in Lake City, where a statue honours water-skiing inventor Ralph Samuelson on the Lake Pepin shore

Meet the live eagles at the National Eagle Center in Wabasha: open daily 10am to 4pm on the March-October schedule, with live eagle programs at 11am and 1pm on Fridays and Saturdays; advance reservations are recommended because program tickets can sell out

days.title: Winona: Garvin Heights and Perrot State Park
activities: Watch the city, the Mississippi and the Wisconsin bluffs from the Garvin Heights Overlook in Winona
Minnesota Marine Art Museum on the Winona riverfront: open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm, closed Mondays and federal holidays
Cross into Wisconsin for Brady's Bluff at Perrot State Park: the east and west trails are narrow and steep, and the summit looks over the river valley (check the state park vehicle pass rules)

title: Mississippi Delta Blues & Faulkner's Oxford
best_time_description: Spring and fall suit a trip that mixes walking Clarksdale and Oxford with time outdoors; Delta summers are hot, and several stops close on Mondays or Sundays, so plan the order around the days they are open.
description: A Friday-to-Sunday run through the Mississippi Delta's blues towns, ending in William Faulkner's Oxford. It suits friends who care more about music, museums and literary history than about hiking.

days.title: Clarksdale: the Crossroads and live blues
activities: Visit the Crossroads in Clarksdale, the guitar-sculpture landmark on the town's tourism page; ask locally for the exact spot
Walk the Arts and Culture District downtown and its mural tour; Clarksdale's tourism office says live blues plays there every night of the year
Stop outside the Riverside Hotel to read its Mississippi Blues Trail marker (rededicated in October 2025) on the former Clarksdale Colored Hospital where Bessie Smith died

days.title: Clarksdale to Indianola: museums of the Delta
activities: Delta Blues Museum, Clarksdale: open Monday to Saturday 10 to 5 (last admission 4:30), with the remains of Muddy Waters's Stovall Farms cabin on display; check the museum before going for current exhibits
Riverside Hotel Interpretive Center (Living Blues and Civil Rights Museum), opened in 2025; hours and tour arrangements are not published on the pages checked, so contact the hotel first
B.B. King Museum, Indianola: open Tuesday to Saturday 10 to 5, closed Sunday and Monday, so Saturday is the day to go
Dockery Farms near Cleveland, a Delta plantation site with a free museum and restored gin and commissary buildings; visiting hours are not stated on the tourism page, so check before you detour

days.title: Oxford: Rowan Oak and the Square
activities: Rowan Oak, William Faulkner's home: open Sunday 1 to 4 and closed Mondays and major holidays; admission is cash only, and the grounds are open dawn to dusk
Courthouse Square, the historic center of Oxford, for a walk among its shops and restaurants
Square Books, an independent bookstore group founded in 1979 near the University of Mississippi; confirm store hours on its website

title: Olympic Peninsula: Port Townsend to Rialto Beach
best_time_description: Summer and early fall give the most open roads and facilities: Hurricane Ridge Road is open throughout the summer, but in winter it is scheduled for Friday through Sunday and holiday Mondays only, weather permitting. Check the park's road conditions before you go.
description: A ferry, a Victorian-era port town, a mountain ridge, a deep glacial lake and a driftwood beach on the Olympic Peninsula, for friends who want a lot of scenery without an overnight hike.

days.title: Seattle to Port Townsend by ferry
activities: Cross Puget Sound on a Washington State Ferries sailing (the Edmonds-Kingston route lists a crossing of about 30 minutes; WSF asks for a boarding pass on weekends, so check the ferry page before you leave)
Evening walk in Fort Worden Historical State Park: beaches and the historic gun batteries on Artillery Hill (state park day-use hours are 6:30 a.m. to dusk in summer, 8 a.m. to dusk in winter)
Stroll the Uptown and Downtown historic business districts of Port Townsend

days.title: Hurricane Ridge and Lake Crescent
activities: Hurricane Ridge: views of the Bailey Range and Mt. Olympus from the end of the road (the road may close any time for weather; winter access is Friday through Sunday and holiday Mondays only, and vehicles must carry tire chains in winter; there is no potable water on the Ridge)
Lake Crescent: the Marymere Falls hike via the Barnes Creek trail, or the Spruce Railroad trail along the north shore
Lake Crescent Lodge rents rowboats; the lodge is generally open late spring to early fall, so check its own dates

days.title: Rialto Beach and the way home
activities: Rialto Beach: sea stacks, giant drift logs and the Hole-in-the-Wall sea arch about 1.5 miles north of the beach (check the tide table first: the park warns parts of the coast become impassable at high tide)

Optional: the Hall of Mosses (0.8-mile loop) in the Hoh Rain Forest, which the park places within about an hour of Rialto (Hoh visitor center is open daily in summer, usually Friday through Sunday in spring and fall)
Head back toward Seattle by ferry (check State Route 104: the Hood Canal Bridge closes periodically for boat traffic)
days.drive_time: Forks is under 30 minutes by car from Rialto Beach (per NPS)

title: Mountain View Folk Country, Arkansas
best_time_description: April to May and October, when the Ozark Folk Center's Craft Village is open (mid-April to mid-November) and the Tyler Bend trails are comfortable for walking.
description: A quiet Ozarks weekend built on folk music and hand crafts in Mountain View, a spring-fed forest recreation area, and an easy walk beside the Buffalo National River. It suits friends who want porch-pace music and short hikes more than big adventures.

days.title: Mountain View: courthouse square
activities: Settle in and walk the courthouse square in Mountain View, which the city calls the Folk Music Capital of the World
Listen in on the free, open-to-all music sessions on the courthouse steps; the city's history page gives no day or time, so check the city calendar

days.title: Ozark Folk Center and Blanchard Springs
activities: Ozark Folk Center State Park Craft Village: working artisans and free music on the Blacksmith Stage, open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., in season (mid-April to mid-November, so check the park's season dates)
Heritage Herb Garden at the Folk Center
Blanchard Springs Recreation Area (Ozark National Forest, open year-round): paved trail to Blanchard Springs, trout fishing at Mirror Lake, swimming in North Sylamore Creek
Blanchard Springs Caverns tours end after the 2026 season for planned renovation, with a reopening anticipated in 2028 per Arkansas State Parks, so do not plan around them

days.title: Buffalo National River at Tyler Bend
activities: Sod Collier Homestead: an easy, flat 1/10-mile walk from its parking area
Riverview Trail overlooks above the Buffalo River (1.5 miles each way between the homestead parking area and the visitor center)
Tyler Bend Visitor Center and river access; the Park Service pages give conflicting hours, so check with the park before you go

title: Jupiter and the Treasure Coast, Florida
best_time_description: Winter and early spring bring the milder, drier stretch of the Florida year for walking and paddling; summer is hot, humid and stormy, and the lighthouse can delay or cancel tours in lightning and high wind.
description: A lighthouse climb, undeveloped Atlantic beach and Everglades edge country north of Palm Beach, easy to do from one base in Jupiter. It suits friends who want sand and wildlife instead of nightlife.

days.title: Jupiter: the Inlet Lighthouse
activities: Climb the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse (closed Mondays per the lighthouse's own hours page, last entry 4 pm; children need to be at least 48 inches tall to climb; tours can be cancelled for rain, lightning or high wind)
Walk the hardened trail and boardwalk of the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse Outstanding Natural Area (open dawn to dusk daily per BLM)

days.title: Hobe Sound and the Loxahatchee River
activities: Hobe Sound National Wildlife Refuge: 3.5 miles of undeveloped Atlantic beach and a visitor center with live reptiles, amphibians, fish and insects (entrance fee applies; pay in advance on Recreation.gov)
Jonathan Dickinson State Park on the Loxahatchee River: trails and paddling (check the park's own page for which tours and rentals are running that day)

days.title: Arthur R. Marshall Loxahatchee Refuge, then home
activities: Arthur R. Marshall Loxahatchee National Wildlife Refuge visitor center (open daily 9 am to 4 pm per the refuge page) and its Everglades trails, where alligators and snail kites are often seen
Check the refuge page before you go: some trails are muddy after impoundment work, the Cypress Swamp Boardwalk is closed until further notice, and Loxahatchee Road has a construction detour

title: Antelope Island to Bear Lake, Utah
best_time_description: Summer into early fall, when Bear Lake's beach areas and the cave and mountain-lake stops are open; check each stop's season before going.
description: Free-roaming bison on a Great Salt Lake island, a scenic byway up Logan Canyon, and the turquoise water of Bear Lake. A road weekend for friends who like easy hikes, swimming and wildlife over nightlife.

days.title: Antelope Island State Park
activities: Antelope Island State Park: park open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. year-round (closed Thanksgiving and Christmas); visitor center 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Look for the free-ranging bison, pronghorn and mule deer on the island roads
Fielding Garr Ranch historic ranch museum and exhibit, open daily 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Bridger Bay Beach for a float in the salty lake, with restrooms and showers

days.title: Logan Canyon to Bear Lake
activities: Logan Canyon National Scenic Byway (US-89), 41 miles winding from Cache Valley through the national forest to Bear Lake; the Forest Service says to allow about an hour of driving, so budget more for stops
Tony Grove Lake, a short detour off the byway with a boardwalk, picnic area and nature trail around the lake (day-use fee charged per vehicle; summer wildflowers peak in July and August)
Bear Lake State Park: Rendezvous Beach day-use beach, open from May 1 to about the third weekend of October
Garden City Marina on the north end of Garden City for the water and the lake views

days.title: Idaho side of Bear Lake and the way home
activities: Minnetonka Cave in Caribou-Targhee National Forest, Idaho: seasonal guided tours, tickets through Recreation.gov, a jacket needed (the cave stays about 40 degrees F) and 888 stairs; confirm this year's opening dates
Bear Lake National Wildlife Refuge near Montpelier, Idaho: free, open sunrise to sunset year-round, with a short auto tour for birding (best in the morning)
Return through Logan Canyon on the scenic byway, or the way you prefer

title: Santa Barbara, Ojai & the Channel Islands, California
best_time_description: Late winter for wildflowers on Anacapa, or autumn once the island's western gulls have finished nesting (April to mid-August, per the National Park Service). Island Packers boats are often full in summer.
description: A mellow loop for friends: an orchard-valley town, a Spanish-colonial coastal city, then a boat out to Anacapa, one of the Channel Islands. Suits a group that wants a little hiking, a little history and some time on the water.

days.title: Ojai: Libbey Park and the Valley Trail
activities: Stroll Libbey Park, the downtown park in the middle of Ojai, and the arcade shops beside it
Walk or cycle a stretch of the Ojai Valley Trail, a former rail line that starts one block east of the Arcade and runs about 10 miles toward the coast (open to bikes and horses)
Watch the evening light on the mountains; Ojai Visitors describes a sunset glow on the peaks each evening

days.title: Santa Barbara: Courthouse, Mission and Waterfront
activities: Santa Barbara County Courthouse: open 10 am to 5 pm on weekends (8 am to 5 pm weekdays), no entry after 4:30 pm, with security screening; check sbcourthouse.org for current access to the clock tower, as its pages disagree
Old Mission Santa Barbara self-guided tour: Monday to Saturday 9:30 am to 5 pm, Sunday 12:30 to 5 pm, last tour ticket 4 pm; on Saturdays the church and cemetery close to the tour after 3:15 pm
Santa Barbara Botanic Garden in Mission Canyon: open daily 10 am to 5 pm, reservations required (last reservation 4 pm)
Evening on the Santa Barbara waterfront and Stearns Wharf

days.title: Ventura Harbor: Anacapa Island
activities: Island Packers day trip from Ventura Harbor to East Anacapa: about one hour each way, year-round on a variable schedule, so book ahead; NPS says allow 6 to 8 hours for a full day, and non-landing trips also exist

On Anacapa, climb 157 stairs from the dock to the top, walk the roughly two miles of trails past the lighthouse overlooks and visit the small visitor center; bring all food and water, as the island has none
No boat? The Robert J. Lagomarsino Visitor Center at 1901 Spinnaker Drive is open daily 8:30 am to 5 pm (closed Thanksgiving and December 25) with exhibits and a park film, and does not need a boat
Mission San Buenaventura on Main Street, Ventura, with a daily gift shop and museum; check Mass times before visiting on a Sunday

title: Sarasota, Siesta Key & the Gulf Barrier Islands
best_time_description: Winter and spring, when Gulf beach days are comfortable and the museums and gardens are in full swing. Atlantic hurricane season runs June to November, so check park and beach status before you go; some local preserves have been closed for storm damage.
description: A beach-and-barrier-island weekend on Florida's Gulf Coast: Siesta Key's beach, a day on Longboat Key and Anna Maria Island, then Sarasota's aquarium and Ringling estate. It suits friends who want sand and sunsets with one or two good indoor stops.

days.title: Siesta Key: Siesta Beach
activities: Siesta Beach, a Sarasota County park with lifeguards, a picnic pavilion, concessions and a playground
Evening walk along the shoreline for sunset

days.title: Longboat Key and Anna Maria Island
activities: Quick Point Nature Preserve on Longboat Key: trails, boardwalks, tidal pools and a canoe launch (Town of Longboat Key; confirm it is open and check hours with the town)
Coquina Beach, a Manatee County beach on Anna Maria Island with lifeguards, picnic areas and a walking trail (sunrise to sunset unless posted)

Anna Maria Island Historical Society museum on Pine Avenue, open Tuesday to Saturday (shorter hours May to December, closed Sunday and Monday), with the outdoor Mangrove Walk and old City Jail from dawn to dusk

days.title: Sarasota: Mote Aquarium and the Ringling
activities: Mote Science Education Aquarium, open daily 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.; reserve tickets online in advance
The Ringling estate with the Museum of Art and Ca' d'Zan, open daily 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. (closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day); tickets are sold online

title: Amelia Island to St. Augustine: Florida's First Coast Forts
best_time_description: Spring and fall for comfortable days on the forts' open ramparts and the beach; summer is hot and prone to afternoon thunderstorms, which close the Castillo gun deck and Fort Matanzas.
description: A coastal run down Florida's northeast coast: historic Fernandina Beach on Amelia Island, Fort Clinch, a plantation in the Timucuan Preserve, then two national monument forts around St. Augustine. Suits history-minded friends who want beaches and old streets rather than theme parks.

days.title: Fernandina Beach: Centre Street
activities: Stop at the Amelia Island Welcome Center in the old train depot on Centre Street for the visitor guide
Stroll Centre Street and the harbor in Fernandina Beach's historic downtown
Settle in on Amelia Island for the night

days.title: Fort Clinch and Kingsley Plantation
activities: Fort Clinch State Park: walk the historic fort and the beach (check the state park page for current fort hours)
Kingsley Plantation (Timucuan Preserve, Jacksonville): the grounds are open Wednesday to Sunday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the planter's house opens on weekends only, in limited hours
Continue south and check in to St. Augustine for the night

days.title: Fort Matanzas, the Castillo and Anastasia
activities: Fort Matanzas National Monument: free ferry passes are handed out in person at the visitor center, first come first served, often gone before 11 a.m.; no ferry Tuesday or Wednesday and it stops in lightning or high wind
Castillo de San Marcos National Monument: open daily, first admission 9 a.m., last admission 5 p.m.; the gun deck closes in thunderstorms
Anastasia State Park: Atlantic beach and the Salt Run tidal marsh before the drive home

title: Saguaro Country and Bisbee, Arizona
best_time_description: Late fall through early spring suits desert hiking and a day of walking Bisbee's hillsides; summer is hot and Tombstone's courthouse keeps shorter hours then.
description: A saguaro-forest weekend that ends in a Cochise County copper town: both sides of Saguaro National Park, a stop at Tombstone's courthouse, then an underground mine tour in Bisbee. Suits friends who want easy desert walks and a bit of mining-and-Old-West history.

days.title: Tucson Mountain District, Saguaro National Park West
activities: Valley View Overlook Nature Trail, an easy 0.8 mile round trip to a ridge with benches (per NPS)
Signal Hill picnic area and the short walk up to the petroglyphs (NPS says it is not ADA accessible)
Bajada Loop Drive, a graded dirt road that NPS says does not need high clearance or four-wheel drive

days.title: Rincon Mountain District, then Tombstone to Bisbee
activities: Cactus Forest Scenic Loop Drive in the park's east district, about 8 miles, paved, narrow with tight turns and no parking for RVs (per NPS)

Tombstone Courthouse State Historic Park, a museum of Tombstone and Cochise County history, open daily, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. October to May and 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. June to September, closed Christmas Day (Arizona State Parks)
Evening arrival in Bisbee

days.title: Bisbee: Queen Mine and the museum
activities: Queen Mine Tour, an underground tour run by the City of Bisbee; reservations required, closed-toe shoes needed and the mine is cool, so bring a layer; check the booking page for departure times
Bisbee Mining and Historical Museum, a Smithsonian Affiliate, open daily 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day
Wander Bisbee's hillside streets before heading home

title: Death Valley from Las Vegas: Badlands, Salt Flats and Dunes
best_time_description: Late fall through spring, when the valley floor is walkable all day. The National Park Service says summer highs often top 120 F in the shade and advises against hiking at low elevations then, so go in the cooler months.
description: A desert weekend for friends who want sunsets over badlands, the lowest point in North America and sand dunes under a dark sky, with a ghost-town art stop on the way home. Built around the park's drive-up viewpoints and short walks.

days.title: Las Vegas to Furnace Creek: Zabriskie Point
activities: Drive west out of Las Vegas into Death Valley National Park and check the park's Alerts and Conditions page for road closures before you leave, since there is no cell service along most park roads
Zabriskie Point at sunset, a paved-grade viewpoint over the badlands that the park lists as a sunrise and sunset spot
Check in at Furnace Creek, where the park lists the Inn and the Ranch at Death Valley as open all year
days.drive_time: About 2.5 hours from Las Vegas to Furnace Creek (Death Valley National Park lodging page)

days.title: Dante's View, Badwater and Mesquite Flat Dunes
activities: Dante's View, a ridge viewpoint towering 5,575 ft above Badwater Basin, about a 45-minute drive from Furnace Creek and especially striking at sunrise or sunset
Badwater Basin, 282 ft below sea level, with a boardwalk and salt flat walk of about 1 mile round trip; the park says hiking is not advised after 10am in summer
Artists Drive, a one-way paved loop of about nine miles to Artists Palette, open in all seasons per the park (check the Alerts page for current road status and the 25 ft vehicle length limit)
Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes near Stovepipe Wells at sunset: no official trail, about 2 miles round trip to the tallest dune, and the park notes pets are not allowed on the dunes

days.title: Harmony Borax Works and Goldwell Open Air Museum
activities: Harmony Borax Works, 1 mile west of Furnace Creek: adobe ruins, a 20-Mule Team wagon and a 0.4 mile paved interpretive loop (about 30 minutes; hiking not advised after 10am in summer)
Golden Canyon, a 2 mile round trip hike from a trailhead on Badwater Road, with one rock scramble of about three feet and no restroom on the trail

Goldwell Open Air Museum near the ghost town of Rhyolite, on State Highway 374 west of Beatty, Nevada; the museum lists itself open 24 hours a day and its visitor center Monday to Saturday 10am to 4pm, closing earlier in summer
Drive home to Las Vegas

title: Wilmington and the Cape Fear Coast, North Carolina
best_time_description: Spring and early fall for comfortable beach and trail days. The Carolina Beach boardwalk amusement park only runs between Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends, and Atlantic hurricane season runs June through November.
description: A river-town-to-beach weekend on North Carolina's southern coast: a Riverwalk evening in Wilmington, Civil War history and open beach at Fort Fisher, then Venus flytrap country and a garden before the drive home. Suits friends who want a coastal weekend that is not the Outer Banks.

days.title: Wilmington: the Riverwalk
activities: Walk the Wilmington Riverwalk, a 1.75-mile path along the Cape Fear River from the foot of Nun Street to the Isabel Holmes Bridge (the city is replacing the decking in a multi-year project, so expect some sections to be under work)
Look across the river to Battleship NORTH CAROLINA; the ship welcomes visitors daily, so check its ticket page for current hours before planning a tour

days.title: Fort Fisher and Kure Beach
activities: Fort Fisher State Historic Site, the Civil War earthworks that kept Wilmington's port open to blockade-runners until January 1865 (open Tuesday to Saturday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed Sunday and Monday, so this is the day to do it)
Fort Fisher State Recreation Area: pedestrian beach open year-round, the Basin Trail through the salt marsh to an observation deck over Zeke's Island and the Cape Fear River
Kure Beach Fishing Pier, dating to 1923 and still family-owned

days.title: Carolina Beach State Park and Airlie Gardens
activities: Carolina Beach State Park, home of the Venus flytrap and the 50-foot Sugarloaf Dune, with about 9 miles of hiking trails (visitor center open daily, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.)
Airlie Gardens in Wilmington, open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with last admission at 4:30 p.m.

title: Berlin, Dresden + Munich, Germany
best_time_description: Late spring to early autumn (May to September) gives the longest days and open-air beer gardens in Munich, and Neuschwanstein's summer visiting hours run 9:00 to 18:00 (late March to mid-October; winter hours 10:00 to 16:00 from 16 October). Expect crowds at the Reichstag and Neuschwanstein in July and August.
description: Germany's classic first-timer arc: three days in Berlin for the Wall, Reichstag and Museum Island, a day trip to Dresden's rebuilt old town, the ICE south to Munich, and a day out to King Ludwig II's Neuschwanstein castle.

days.title: Arrive Berlin
activities: Settle in near Mitte or Prenzlauer Berg
Evening walk past the Brandenburg Gate and Unter den Linden
Dinner of currywurst or a doner kebab, both Berlin street-food staples

days.title: Berlin: Reichstag + Museum Island
activities: Reichstag dome: free, but you must register in advance on the Bundestag website (name and date of birth required; the dome is closed on some dates for maintenance, the roof terrace stays open)

Museum Island (a UNESCO site): the Pergamon Museum's main building is closed for refurbishment and is scheduled to reopen on 4 June 2027, so choose from the island's other museums and check smb.museum for opening hours and timed tickets
Afternoon walk along the Spree

days.title: Berlin: Wall history
activities: Berlin Wall Memorial on Bernauer Straße, an open-air memorial along a surviving stretch of the border strip
East Side Gallery, the longest preserved section of the Wall, now an open-air mural gallery
Evening in Kreuzberg for Turkish and international food

days.title: Day trip: Dresden
activities: Direct train from Berlin Hbf to Dresden Hbf, about 1 hour 35 minutes on the fastest Deutsche Bahn services (DB booking page, snapshot dated 16 October 2026); book a return the same evening
Frauenkirche, rebuilt church on the Neumarkt: the Open Church is free Monday to Friday 10:00-11:30 and 13:00-17:30, weekend times vary so check frauenkirche-dresden.de
Zwinger palace: the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister is open 10:00-17:00 and closed Mondays (skd.museum)
Walk the Brühl's Terrace above the Elbe, then return to Berlin

days.title: ICE to Munich
activities: Morning ICE from Berlin Hbf to München Hbf, about 4 hours (the fastest direct ICE is listed at 4 hours 6 minutes on bahn.de); reserve a seat if travelling at a weekend
Check in near Marienplatz or the Hauptbahnhof
Evening at a traditional beer garden: Bavarian beer gardens have long allowed guests to bring their own food, while drinks are bought on site

days.title: Munich old town
activities: Marienplatz and the Neues Rathaus town hall
Viktualienmarkt food market for a Bavarian lunch
Englischer Garten, one of Europe's largest city parks

days.title: Day trip: Neuschwanstein
activities: Regional train from München Hbf to Füssen, just under 2 hours; no direct long-distance link, so check bahn.de for the connection
Local bus 73 or 78 from Füssen station to Hohenschwangau, then a steep walk of about 15 minutes or the shuttle to the castle
Neuschwanstein is visited by guided tour only, at a set time on a set date: buy tickets online at hohenschwangau.de well in advance; the castle is closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January
Return to Munich by the same route

days.title: Depart Munich
activities: Morning at leisure: the Residenz or a last pretzel breakfast
Transfer to Munich Airport for departure

food_culture.name: Currywurst
food_culture.description: Pork sausage sliced under a curry-ketchup sauce, sold at Imbiss stands all over Berlin and treated as the city's signature fast food.

food_culture.name: Weißwurst breakfast
food_culture.description: Munich's white veal sausage, traditionally served in a bowl of hot water with sweet mustard and a soft pretzel and eaten in the morning rather than in the evening.

food_culture.name: Bavarian beer and the Reinheitsgebot
food_culture.description: Bavaria's 1516 purity law, which limited beer to water, barley and hops, is the origin of Germany's beer-purity tradition; Munich's beer halls and gardens serve the Helles lager the city is known for.

food_culture.name: The Biergarten
food_culture.description: Traditional Bavarian beer gardens let guests bring their own food and buy only the drinks, a custom rooted in a 19th-century Bavarian royal decree and still practised in Munich's shaded chestnut-tree gardens.

food_culture.name: Berlin Wall memory culture
food_culture.description: Berlin keeps the division of the city visible through the Berlin Wall Memorial, the East Side Gallery murals and the double line of cobblestones marking the Wall's path, and these sites are central to how the city tells its modern history.

title: Cologne, Heidelberg + Black Forest, Germany
best_time_description: May to October is the easiest window: long days for the Heidelberg Philosophenweg walk and Black Forest lake paths, and open-air cafes in Cologne and Freiburg. Spring brings blossom along the Neckar and September to October brings wine harvest season in Baden.
description: A west-to-south-west Germany route: Cologne's Gothic cathedral and Kölsch brewhouses, Heidelberg's ruined castle above the Neckar, then Freiburg and a day on the edge of the Black Forest at Titisee, all linked by fast Deutsche Bahn trains.

days.title: Arrive Cologne
activities: Check in near the Altstadt or the cathedral
Evening walk along the Rhine promenade past the Hohenzollern Bridge
First Kölsch at a traditional brewhouse in the Altstadt

days.title: Cologne cathedral + Altstadt
activities: Cologne Cathedral: since 1 July 2026 a ticket is required for tourist visits to the interior; tickets for the interior, tower and treasury are sold online at koelner-dom.de and at the Kurienhaus ticket office on Roncalliplatz
South Tower climb: 533 steps with no lift, allow 30 to 45 minutes; the tower is open 9:00-18:00 March to October (9:00-16:00 November to February) with last entry half an hour before closing
Walk the Altstadt and the Rhine embankment
Evening in a Kölsch brewhouse

days.title: Train to Heidelberg
activities: Morning train from Cologne Hbf to Heidelberg Hbf, about 1 hour 50 minutes with one change (fastest connection on bahn.de, example dated September 2026)
Walk the Hauptstraße through the Altstadt and cross the Alte Brücke (Old Bridge) over the Neckar
Late afternoon on the Philosophenweg across the river for the view of the castle and old town

days.title: Heidelberg Castle
activities: Heidelberg Castle: the official site lists daily 9:00-18:00 with last admission 17:30; the Schlossticket covers the funicular, courtyard, Great Barrel cellar and German Pharmacy Museum
Walk down through the Altstadt to the Marktplatz and the Church of the Holy Spirit
Stroll the Altstadt's lanes between the Marktplatz and the Neckar
Evening on the Neckar bank

days.title: ICE to Freiburg
activities: ICE from Heidelberg Hbf to Freiburg Hbf, about 1 hour 29 minutes on the fastest direct trains (bahn.de, snapshot October 2026)
Freiburg Münster and the Münsterplatz
Follow the Bächle, the narrow water channels running through the old town streets
Dinner of Flammkuchen or Baden wine at an Altstadt tavern

days.title: Black Forest: Titisee + Hinterzarten
activities: Regional S-Bahn (line S1) from Freiburg Hbf up the Höllentalbahn to Titisee, about 39 minutes on the 2026 timetable (departures roughly every 30 minutes on weekdays)
Walk the Titisee lakeside; the town centre is about 10 minutes on foot from Bahnhof Titisee
Short onward hop to Hinterzarten, about 6 minutes by train from Titisee, for forest walks
Try a slice of Black Forest cherry cake in the afternoon, then return to Freiburg by train

days.title: Freiburg and depart
activities: Climb Freiburg Münster's tower or wander the Schlossberg above the old town (check the Münster's visiting hours for the tower)
Late departure from Freiburg Hbf by train to the airport of your choice

food_culture.name: Kölsch
food_culture.description: Cologne's pale, top-fermented beer is brewed only in and around the city; it is served in thin 0.2 litre Stange glasses by waiters called Köbes, who keep refilling until you place a coaster on top of your glass.

food_culture.name: Cologne Carnival
food_culture.description: The Rhineland carnival season, known as the fifth season, opens on 11 November at 11:11 and peaks on Weiberfastnacht and Rosenmontag in February or March, with costume parades through the Altstadt.

food_culture.name: Black Forest cherry cake
food_culture.description: Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte layers chocolate sponge, whipped cream and cherries soaked in Kirschwasser, a cherry brandy made in the Black Forest region.

food_culture.name: Black Forest ham
food_culture.description: Schwarzwälder Schinken is a smoked ham with protected geographical indication status under EU rules, available at delis and Black Forest taverns around Titisee and Freiburg.

food_culture.name: Freiburg Bächle
food_culture.description: The narrow water channels that run along Freiburg's old town streets were once used to carry water for fire fighting and animals; local lore holds that stepping into one means you will marry a Freiburger.

title: Amsterdam, The Hague, Delft + Rotterdam, Netherlands
best_time_description: April to September gives the longest days and the most comfortable weather for walking, canal-side lunches and the Kinderdijk windmill walk. Amsterdam is busiest in summer and around King's Day (27 April), so book museum and Anne Frank House slots early. This is a plan for the Randstad (Amsterdam, The Hague, Delft, Rotterdam) and is easy by train.
description: The classic first-timer Netherlands loop: Amsterdam's canals and big museums, a Golden Age day in Haarlem, the Mauritshuis in The Hague, Delft's blue-and-white pottery and churches, then modern Rotterdam and the UNESCO windmills at Kinderdijk, all linked by short NS train rides.

days.title: Arrive Amsterdam
activities: NS train from Schiphol Airport to Amsterdam Centraal, about 14 to 16 minutes (9292 journey planner)
Check in, then an evening walk along the 17th-century canal ring (Herengracht, Keizersgracht and Prinsengracht)
Dinner of bitterballen and a local beer at a traditional brown cafe in the Jordaan
days.drive_time: NS train Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal, ~15 min
days.lodging_suggestion: Amsterdam (Centrum, Jordaan or near Amsterdam Centraal)

days.title: Rijksmuseum and Museumplein
activities: Rijksmuseum: tickets are sold online with a start time (the museum states everyone needs one); open daily 9:00 to 17:00. Rembrandt's The Night Watch is the headline work
Afternoon in Vondelpark, a short walk from Museumplein
Evening canal cruise from the centre of Amsterdam
days.lodging_suggestion: Amsterdam (Centrum, Jordaan or near Amsterdam Centraal)

days.title: Anne Frank House and the Jordaan
activities: Anne Frank House: tickets are sold online only for a specific time slot, never at the door, and each week's tickets are released on Tuesday at 10:00 CEST for a visit six weeks later, so book well ahead
Wander the Jordaan's narrow canals, galleries and small shops
Try poffertjes (mini pancakes) at a pancake house, and herring from a fish stall if you want the full local experience
days.lodging_suggestion: Amsterdam (Centrum, Jordaan or near Amsterdam Centraal)

days.title: Haarlem day trip
activities: NS train from Amsterdam Centraal to Haarlem, about 15 to 19 minutes (9292)
Grote Markt and the Grote Kerk (St Bavo); Sunday opening of the church differs between sources, so check before you go
Frans Hals Museum (Hof and Hal sites): open Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 17:00 and closed on Mondays
Train back to Amsterdam for the evening
days.drive_time: NS train Amsterdam to Haarlem, ~15-19 min each way
days.lodging_suggestion: Amsterdam (Centrum, Jordaan or near Amsterdam Centraal)

days.title: The Hague and on to Delft
activities: NS train from Amsterdam Centraal to Den Haag Centraal, about 50 minutes to 1 hour depending on the service (9292)
Mauritshuis for Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring: entry is by timed slot booked online; open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00 and Monday 13:00 to 18:00, last entry 30 minutes before closing
NS train from Den Haag Centraal to Delft, about 11 to 15 minutes (9292)
Evening stroll around Delft's Markt and canals
days.drive_time: NS train Amsterdam to The Hague ~50-60 min, then The Hague to Delft ~11-15 min

days.title: Delft to Rotterdam
activities: Oude Kerk and Nieuwe Kerk in Delft on one combined ticket; climbing the Nieuwe Kerk tower is a separate add-on bought at its counter and depends on the weather
Royal Delft museum on Rotterdamseweg, open every day, to see the blue-and-white Delftware tradition
NS train from Delft to Rotterdam Centraal, about 10 to 14 minutes (9292)

Markthal (Monday to Thursday 10:00 to 20:00, Friday 10:00 to 21:00, Saturday 10:00 to 20:00, Sunday 12:00 to 18:00 per its website) and the Cube Houses next door; only the Kijk-Kubus museum house can be entered and its hours differ between sources, so check kubuswoning.nl
days.drive_time: NS train Delft to Rotterdam Centraal, ~10-14 min

days.title: Kinderdijk windmills
activities: Reach Kinderdijk (UNESCO World Heritage site) from Rotterdam: Waterbus lists a direct WaterShuttle of about 30 minutes that runs on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays; Waterbus and Kinderdijk's own site name different departure stops, so confirm the stop. On other days use bus 489 from Rotterdam Kralingse Zoom, about 35 minutes to Kinderdijk Molenkade, or the Waterbus plus Driehoeksveer ferry
Choose a visit length on site: Kinderdijk offers a 1 hour route, a 2 to 3 hour route with audio tour, or a full-day route; tickets are ordered online
Return to Rotterdam and walk across the Erasmusbrug at sunset
days.drive_time: WaterShuttle ~30 min (Fri-Sun) or bus 489 ~35 min each way

days.title: Depart from Schiphol
activities: NS train from Rotterdam Centraal to Schiphol Airport, about 26 to 52 minutes depending on whether you catch an Intercity direct (9292)
Allow extra time at Schiphol for passport control and the EU Entry/Exit System registration for non-EU travellers
days.drive_time: NS train Rotterdam to Schiphol, ~26-52 min

food_culture.name: Bitterballen
food_culture.description: Deep-fried, crumb-coated balls of meat ragout served hot with mustard, the standard bar snack to order with a beer at a Dutch brown cafe, for example in Amsterdam's Jordaan.

food_culture.name: Haring (raw herring)
food_culture.description: Brined herring served at fish stalls, traditionally eaten with chopped onion and pickles; it is the most Dutch street snack you can try in Amsterdam, The Hague or Rotterdam.

food_culture.name: Poffertjes
food_culture.description: Small, puffy buckwheat-style pancakes served in a portion with butter and powdered sugar, a sweet stop on a canal-side afternoon.

food_culture.name: Jenever
food_culture.description: The juniper-flavoured Dutch spirit that gin descends from, poured in a small tulip-shaped glass filled to the brim and often paired with a beer at old tasting houses.

food_culture.name: King's Day (Koningsdag), 27 April
food_culture.description: The national holiday when much of the country dresses in orange and holds street markets; the Anne Frank House notes shortened hours on 27 April, a sign of how the day reshapes city opening times.

food_culture.name: Delftware
food_culture.description: Delft's blue-and-white pottery is still made and shown at Royal Delft on Rotterdamseweg, which runs a museum open every day alongside its working factory.

food_culture.name: Water management at Kinderdijk
food_culture.description: Kinderdijk's windmills and the Wisboom pumping station illustrate how the Dutch kept low-lying land dry; the site is one of the few UNESCO World Heritage sites in the Netherlands.

food_culture.name: Golden Age painting
food_culture.description: Rembrandt in the Rijksmuseum, Vermeer in the Mauritshuis and Frans Hals in Haarlem together give a three-city tour of 17th-century Dutch art.

title: Utrecht, Hoge Veluwe, Den Bosch + Maastricht, Netherlands
best_time_description: May to September suits the Hoge Veluwe's free White Bikes and long daylight, and the summer-only direct bus to the Kroller-Muller area; early autumn (September to October) is quieter and still good for cycling. Winter works for the cities but short days and seasonal bus changes make the park day harder.
description: A slower route away from the Amsterdam crowds: Utrecht's canals and Dom Tower, a day of free bikes and modern art in the Hoge Veluwe National Park, the Burgundian south in 's-Hertogenbosch (home of Hieronymus Bosch), then Maastricht on the Maas, linked by NS trains.

days.title: Arrive Utrecht
activities: NS train from Schiphol Airport to Utrecht Centraal, about 30 to 33 minutes on the fastest services and up to roughly 50 minutes on slower ones (9292)
Evening walk along the Oudegracht, whose canal-level wharf cellars hold cafes and restaurants
Dinner in the old centre
days.drive_time: NS train Schiphol to Utrecht Centraal, ~30-50 min

days.title: Utrecht: Dom Tower and canals
activities: Dom Tower: it can only be visited on a guided tour of about an hour, tickets are tied to a date and time, late arrivals forfeit their ticket and bags are not allowed (free lockers provided); tours run in Dutch and English
Explore Domplein and the Oudegracht at your own pace, then rest at a canal-side cafe
Optional: Museum Speelklok, a short walk away (the Dom Tower plus Speelklok combination ticket is not sold online)

days.title: Hoge Veluwe National Park and the Kroller-Muller
activities: NS train from Utrecht Centraal to Ede-Wageningen, about 22 to 27 minutes (9292)

Bus on to Otterlo: the park's FAQ says to choose the Ingang Otterlo stop in 9292 when travelling via Ede or Arnhem; the Kroller-Muller Museum says a direct bus 106 from Ede-Wageningen runs only in summer, so check the timetable for your date
Use the park's free White Bikes (they cannot be reserved and may run short on busy days)
Kroller-Muller Museum: open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00, closed Mondays except in the summer holidays and on listed holiday Mondays; its sculpture garden is part of the visit
Return to Utrecht by the same route
days.drive_time: NS train Utrecht to Ede-Wageningen ~22-27 min each way, plus bus to Otterlo

days.title: Utrecht to 's-Hertogenbosch
activities: NS train from Utrecht Centraal to 's-Hertogenbosch, about 27 to 28 minutes on most services (9292)
Sint-Janskathedraal (St John's Cathedral), which the cathedral's website lists as open daily with guided tours; check current hours before going
Binnendieze: take an open-boat trip through the old canals and fortifications beneath the city
Jheronimus Bosch Art Center, a former church about a 15-minute walk from the station, for the story of the painter Hieronymus Bosch
Order a Bossche bol, the chocolate-covered cream pastry the city is known for

days.title: Den Bosch to Maastricht
activities: NS train from 's-Hertogenbosch to Maastricht, about 1 hour 23 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes (9292)
Settle in and walk the old centre along the river Maas
Boekhandel Dominicanen, a bookshop in a restored 13th-century Gothic church with a cafe in the former chancel; Libris and Visit Maastricht list it open Monday 10:00 to 18:00
days.drive_time: NS train 's-Hertogenbosch to Maastricht ~1 h 23 min - 1 h 35 min

days.title: Maastricht
activities: Bonnefanten museum of art: open Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 17:00 and closed on Mondays; tickets are sold on its online ticket site, and the museum closes on Carnival Sunday, King's Day, Christmas Day and New Year's Day. Check its site for temporary closures between exhibitions
Lunch with a slice of Limburgse vlaai (fruit pie), the regional pastry
Afternoon wandering the squares and lanes of the old centre

days.title: Depart from Schiphol
activities: NS train from Maastricht to Schiphol Airport, about 2 hours 32 minutes to 2 hours 46 minutes (9292); leave early for a morning flight
Allow extra time at Schiphol for passport control and the EU Entry/Exit System registration for non-EU travellers
days.drive_time: NS train Maastricht to Schiphol, ~2 h 32 min - 2 h 46 min

food_culture.name: Bossche bol
food_culture.description: A large choux-pastry ball filled with whipped cream and coated in chocolate, the signature pastry of 's-Hertogenbosch; eat it with a fork or accept the mess.

food_culture.name: Limburgse vlaai
food_culture.description: The fruit pie of Limburg province, with a thin, soft pastry base and fruit filling, sold in wedges at bakeries and cafes in and around Maastricht.

food_culture.name: Stamppot
food_culture.description: Mashed potato mixed with a vegetable such as kale (boerenkool) and usually served with smoked rookworst sausage, a hearty cold-weather Dutch dish worth ordering on an autumn trip.

food_culture.name: Brown-cafe beer and jenever
food_culture.description: In Utrecht's old centre and on the Oudegracht cafe terraces, a local draught beer or a small glass of jenever is the standard evening drink.

food_culture.name: Carnival in the south
food_culture.description: Carnival in Limburg and North Brabant is a major social event in February; the Bonnefanten in Maastricht lists Carnival Sunday as a closed day, showing how it shapes the calendar there.

food_culture.name: White Bikes of the Hoge Veluwe
food_culture.description: The national park provides about 2,000 free White Bikes for visitors; they have no locks and cannot be reserved, and the park is where the Kroller-Muller Museum's sculpture garden sits.

food_culture.name: Hieronymus Bosch
food_culture.description: The late-medieval painter was from 's-Hertogenbosch, and the Jheronimus Bosch Art Center, set in a former church, tells his story through reproductions of his work.

food_culture.name: A bookshop in a church
food_culture.description: Boekhandel Dominicanen in Maastricht fills a restored 13th-century Gothic church, with a coffee cafe in the former chancel; it has been celebrated as one of the world's most beautiful bookshops.

title: Zurich, Lucerne, Interlaken + Zermatt, Switzerland
best_time_description: June to September gives the most reliable mountain views and has every lift, boat and waterfall in this route operating (the Trümmelbach Falls, for one, are open only from about April to early November, weather permitting). This is an editorial suggestion: the Jungfraujoch and Gornergrat run in winter too, but cloud can hide the views on any day, so check the operators' live webcams on the morning.
description: A first-timer's Swiss rail loop with no car: Zurich's old town, Lucerne's lake and covered bridge, the Bernese Oberland around Interlaken (the Jungfraujoch and the Lauterbrunnen valley), then car-free Zermatt below the Matterhorn and the Gornergrat railway.

days.title: Arrive Zurich
activities: Train from Zurich Airport to Zurich Hauptbahnhof, about 10 to 13 minutes on the SBB timetable (S-Bahn or IC)
Walk the Niederdorf old town and climb to the Lindenhof lookout above the Limmat
See Marc Chagall's stained-glass windows in the Fraumünster and the twin towers of the Grossmünster
Evening stroll on the Lake Zurich promenade
days.drive_time: Zurich Airport to Zurich HB, ~10-13 min by train
days.lodging_suggestion: Zurich old town or near Hauptbahnhof

days.title: Zurich to Lucerne
activities: Intercity train Zurich HB to Lucerne, about 41 to 50 minutes (SBB timetable)
Cross the Kapellbrücke, the covered wooden bridge, and see the Wasserturm (the water tower beside it)
Visit the Lion Monument and walk the medieval Museggmauer wall
Take a lake boat on Lake Lucerne at sunset (check the SGV Lake Lucerne timetable for the season)
days.drive_time: Zurich HB to Lucerne, ~41-50 min by train

days.title: Lucerne to Interlaken
activities: Luzern-Interlaken Express (zentralbahn) over the Brünig Pass, 1 hour 50 minutes; a seat reservation is optional (CHF 16 from 2 May to 1 November 2026 per zentralbahn), and the right-hand side in the direction of travel gives the best views
Walk the Höhematte meadow in Interlaken with the Jungfrau in view
Stroll along the Aare between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz
days.drive_time: Lucerne to Interlaken Ost, ~1 hr 50 min by train

days.title: Jungfraujoch, Top of Europe
activities: Interlaken Ost to Grindelwald Terminal, Eiger Express and Jungfrau Railway to the Jungfraujoch (3,454 m): Jungfrau Railways quotes 1 hour 30 minutes from Interlaken Ost on this route; the older route via Lauterbrunnen and Kleine Scheidegg takes about 2 hours on the SBB timetable
Jungfrau Railways recommends a paid seat reservation (CHF 10) in good weather to avoid queues; check the Jungfraujoch webcam in the morning, as cloud can cover the summit
Visit the Sphinx observation terrace, the Ice Palace and the 360-degree cinema (which does not depend on weather)
Return to Interlaken in the afternoon
days.drive_time: Interlaken Ost to Jungfraujoch, ~1 hr 30 min via Eiger Express each way

days.title: Lauterbrunnen Valley
activities: Train Interlaken Ost to Lauterbrunnen, about 22 minutes (SBB timetable)
See Staubbach Falls from the village

Visit the Trümmelbach Falls, ten glacier waterfalls inside the mountain reached by tunnel lift and stairs; open daily from about April to early November depending on weather, so check dates before going (usual hours 9:00 to 17:00, 8:30 to 18:00 in July and August)
Optional walk through the valley toward Stechelberg past the waterfalls, then return to Interlaken
days.drive_time: Interlaken Ost to Lauterbrunnen, ~22 min by train

days.title: Interlaken to Zermatt
activities: Train from Interlaken to Zermatt, about 2 hours 30 to 2 hours 45 with two changes (typically Spiez and Visp), per the SBB timetable; Visp to Zermatt alone is about 1 hour 6 minutes
Zermatt is a car-free village: you arrive by rail and move around on foot or by electric taxi
Walk Hinterdorf and the Kirchbrücke for a first view of the Matterhorn
days.drive_time: Interlaken to Zermatt, ~2 hr 30-2 hr 45 min by train, 2 changes

days.title: Gornergrat + depart
activities: Gornergrat cogwheel railway from Zermatt to 3,089 m, about 33 minutes up (Gornergrat Bahn), for views of the Matterhorn and the Gorner Glacier

Return to Zermatt and take the train to Zurich HB, about 3 hours 20 minutes with one change at Visp (SBB timetable), then Zurich HB to Zurich Airport in about 10 to 13 minutes; plan an evening flight, or add a night in Zurich
days.drive_time: Zermatt to Zurich HB, ~3 hr 20 min by train, 1 change

food_culture.name: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
food_culture.description: Zurich's signature dish: sliced veal in a cream and mushroom sauce, traditionally served with rösti. Look for it in the old-town restaurants.

food_culture.name: Cheese fondue
food_culture.description: Melted Swiss cheese in a shared pot, eaten with bread on long forks. A staple of mountain restaurants in the Bernese Oberland and Valais, typically ordered by the pot for two or more.

food_culture.name: Luzerner Chügelipastete
food_culture.description: Lucerne's classic vol-au-vent: a puff-pastry case filled with a creamy veal and mushroom ragout, found on the menus of traditional Lucerne restaurants.

food_culture.name: Raclette
food_culture.description: A Valais speciality: half a wheel of cheese is melted and scraped onto boiled potatoes with pickles and onions. Zermatt is in the canton of Valais, so it is on most menus in the village.

food_culture.name: Valais Fendant
food_culture.description: Fendant is the name for Chasselas wine in the Valais, the canton around Zermatt. It is a light white wine usually poured with raclette and fondue.

food_culture.name: Alpabzug (cattle descent from the alpine pastures)
food_culture.description: In early autumn, farmers bring their cows down from summer pastures in decorated processions with bells and flowers. The date varies by village and weather, so ask the local tourist office rather than planning around a fixed day.

food_culture.name: Matterhorn and the first ascent
food_culture.description: The Matterhorn (4,478 m) was first climbed in 1865, with a fatal descent that shaped Zermatt's mountaineering identity. The Matterhorn Museum Zermatlantis in the village tells that story.

food_culture.name: Sechseläuten, Zurich's spring festival
food_culture.description: Held in Zurich each April, the guild parade ends with the burning of the Böögg, a snowman figure on a pyre; the speed at which its head explodes is said to predict the summer weather.

title: Lake Geneva, Gruyères + Ticino Lakes, Switzerland
best_time_description: May to June and September to October suit lake and vineyard walking and Ticino's lakeside towns, with fewer crowds than July and August. This is an editorial suggestion. Some lifts (the Monte San Salvatore funicular, for example) close for maintenance in late autumn, so check dates for an October or November trip.
description: A west-to-south route by train and no car: Geneva and Lausanne, the Lavaux vineyard terraces, Montreux and Château de Chillon, a cheese-and-chocolate day trip to Gruyères, then through the Gotthard to Italian-speaking Ticino for Lugano, Bellinzona's castles and Locarno on Lake Maggiore.

days.title: Arrive Geneva
activities: Train from Geneva Airport to Geneva Cornavin, about 7 minutes (SBB timetable)
Walk the old town to the Cathédrale Saint-Pierre and climb its towers
See the Reformation Wall in Parc des Bastions
Evening walk along the lakefront of Lac Léman
days.drive_time: Geneva Airport to Geneva Cornavin, ~7 min by train
days.lodging_suggestion: Geneva old town or near Cornavin

days.title: Geneva to Lausanne + Lavaux
activities: Train Geneva to Lausanne, about 40 to 50 minutes (SBB timetable)
Visit Lausanne's Gothic cathedral and walk the old town

Regional train Lausanne to Cully, about 10 minutes (SBB timetable), then walk among the Lavaux vineyard terraces above the lake, a UNESCO World Heritage landscape, and taste local Chasselas white wine at a cave in Cully or Epesses
days.drive_time: Geneva to Lausanne, ~40-50 min; Lausanne to Cully, ~10 min by train

days.title: Lausanne to Montreux + Château de Chillon
activities: Train Lausanne to Montreux, about 20 minutes (SBB timetable)
Walk the Montreux lakeside promenade and see the Freddie Mercury statue
Bus 201 from Montreux to Château de Chillon, about 14 minutes (SBB timetable); the castle is open year-round except 1 January and 25 December, with hours that change by season, so check chillon.ch
days.drive_time: Lausanne to Montreux, ~20 min by train; Montreux to Chillon, ~14 min by bus

days.title: Day trip to Gruyères
activities: GoldenPass line train Montreux to Montbovon, then a regional train to Gruyères, about 1 hour 14 minutes in total (SBB timetable)
Walk the car-free medieval village and visit Gruyères Castle

See cheesemaking at La Maison du Gruyère in Pringy (production viewing is at set times in the morning and midday, so check the dairy's schedule before going) and try meringues with Gruyères double cream

Optional: Maison Cailler chocolate factory in nearby Broc; Switzerland Tourism recommends booking tickets online in advance (chocolate workshops need a reservation), so check availability and current hours before you go
Return to Montreux, about 1 hour 15 to 20 minutes (SBB timetable); check the last connection from Gruyères
days.drive_time: Montreux to Gruyères, ~1 hr 14 min by train via Montbovon

days.title: Montreux to Lugano
activities: Long rail day through the Gotthard: Montreux to Lugano takes about 4 hours 35 minutes to 4 hours 50 minutes on the SBB timetable, usually changing at Lausanne and Lucerne (example: 09:08 to 13:58)
Arrive in Lugano and walk the lakefront and Piazza della Riforma
Evening aperitivo by the lake
days.drive_time: Montreux to Lugano, ~4 hr 35-4 hr 50 min by train, 2 changes

days.title: Lugano + Monte San Salvatore
activities: Visit the LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura museum and walk the old town

Funicular to the summit of Monte San Salvatore, about 12 minutes in summer service, for views over Lake Lugano; the funicular closes for maintenance in late autumn (10 November to 5 December on the operator's page when checked) and runs a reduced winter timetable, so check montesansalvatore.ch
Optional lake boat trip on Lake Lugano
days.drive_time: Lugano city and funicular, on foot or local transit

days.title: Bellinzona + Locarno
activities: Train Lugano to Bellinzona, about 14 to 18 minutes (SBB timetable)

Visit Castelgrande and the other two castles of the UNESCO World Heritage fortifications, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro; check the castles' seasonal hours, and note the weekly market is held on Saturdays
Train Bellinzona to Locarno, about 23 to 26 minutes (SBB timetable)
Walk Piazza Grande and take the Locarno funicular to the Madonna del Sasso sanctuary above the town, with views over Lake Maggiore
Return to Lugano, about 32 minutes by regional express (SBB timetable)
days.drive_time: Lugano to Bellinzona, ~14-18 min; Bellinzona to Locarno, ~23-26 min; Locarno to Lugano, ~32 min by train

days.title: Depart from Zurich
activities: Train Lugano to Zurich HB, about 1 hour 53 minutes through the Gotthard Base Tunnel, then Zurich HB to Zurich Airport in about 9 to 13 minutes (SBB timetable); about 2 hours 10 minutes in total, so allow time for an airport check-in
days.drive_time: Lugano to Zurich Airport, ~2 hr 10 min by train, 1 change

food_culture.name: Papet vaudois
food_culture.description: A Vaud canton dish of leeks and potatoes slow-cooked together and served with saucisson vaudois, a smoked pork sausage. Found in traditional restaurants around Lausanne and Lavaux.

food_culture.name: Filets de perche
food_culture.description: Fried perch fillets from the lake are a regular on lakeside menus around Lake Geneva, usually served with fries or potatoes and a lemon wedge.

food_culture.name: Meringues with Gruyères double cream
food_culture.description: Gruyères is known for thick double cream served with meringues in a bowl. You can buy the cream and meringues at the dairy shop next to La Maison du Gruyère.

food_culture.name: Ticino risotto and polenta
food_culture.description: Ticino's cooking is closer to Lombardy than to German-speaking Switzerland: polenta, risotto, braised meats and cold cuts.

food_culture.name: Lavaux Chasselas
food_culture.description: Chasselas is the main white grape of the terraced Lavaux vineyards above Lake Geneva. Cellars in Cully and other villages offer tastings.

food_culture.name: Merlot del Ticino
food_culture.description: Merlot is the leading grape of Ticino, the Italian-speaking canton of this route, and appears as red or as a white-vinified wine (Merlot bianco) in many Lugano and Locarno restaurants.

food_culture.name: Grotto dining in Ticino
food_culture.description: A grotto is a rustic Ticino stone-cellar restaurant, traditionally serving cold cuts, polenta and wine in small ceramic cups (boccalini). The tradition grew from the cool natural cellars of the region.

food_culture.name: Fête des Vignerons, Vevey
