food_culture.description: Winegrowers' festival in Vevey held about once a generation, on the shores of Lake Geneva; it is listed by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage, and the last one took place in 2019.

food_culture.name: Swiss chocolate heritage at Maison Cailler
food_culture.description: Cailler, one of Switzerland's oldest chocolate brands, runs a visitor factory in Broc near Gruyères where the story of Swiss chocolate is told and chocolate is tasted.

title: Vienna, Salzburg + Hallstatt, Austria
best_time_description: Late spring (May to June) and early autumn (September to October) give comfortable walking weather in all three towns and fewer crowds than July and August. Hallstatt and the Salzkammergut are busiest in summer. Check ÖBB for rail works on the Hallstatt line, which run until 2 November 2026.
description: Austria's classic first-timer arc by rail: three days of imperial palaces, museums and coffee houses in Vienna, two in Mozart's Salzburg, then the lakeside village of Hallstatt in the Salzkammergut, joined by the Vienna to Salzburg Railjet and the Salzkammergutbahn.

days.title: Arrive Vienna
activities: ÖBB train from Flughafen Wien to Wien Hauptbahnhof takes about 14 minutes (6:34 to 6:48 in ÖBB's West line timetable); the Hauptbahnhof is also where the Salzburg trains leave on day 4
Walk the Innere Stadt to St. Stephen's Cathedral (Stephansdom) and the Graben
Dinner of Wiener Schnitzel or Tafelspitz at a traditional Viennese restaurant
days.lodging_suggestion: Innere Stadt (Vienna's first district) or near Wien Hauptbahnhof

days.title: Imperial Vienna: Schönbrunn + Naschmarkt
activities: Schönbrunn Palace, the Habsburgs' summer residence, and its gardens; check the palace website for timed-entry tickets and book ahead in high season
Walk or browse the stalls of the Naschmarkt
Coffee and cake in a traditional Viennese coffee house in the afternoon
days.lodging_suggestion: Innere Stadt (Vienna's first district) or near Wien Hauptbahnhof

days.title: Hofburg, Belvedere + a Heuriger evening
activities: Hofburg palace complex and the museums on the Ringstrasse; check each museum's weekly closing day, as several Vienna museums close one weekday
Belvedere palaces, home of Klimt's The Kiss in the Upper Belvedere; timed or advance tickets are sensible
Evening at a Heuriger (wine tavern) in a Vienna wine district such as Grinzing, reachable by city tram and bus
days.lodging_suggestion: Innere Stadt (Vienna's first district) or near Wien Hauptbahnhof

days.title: Vienna to Salzburg by Railjet
activities: ÖBB Railjet Xpress from Wien Hauptbahnhof to Salzburg Hauptbahnhof, about 2 hours 25 minutes (7:28 to 9:53 in the ÖBB West line timetable valid from 14 June 2026); ÖBB runs the route twice an hour with no change
Drop bags, then walk the Altstadt (Old Town) along the Salzach river, including Getreidegasse
Mozart's Birthplace museum on Getreidegasse; check opening hours
Evening stroll through the Mirabell Gardens

days.title: Salzburg: fortress + Mönchsberg
activities: Hohensalzburg Fortress above the Old Town, reached on foot or by the funicular from Kapitelplatz
Walk the Mönchsberg ridge for city views
Afternoon Salzburger Nockerl (sweet soufflé) and coffee in the Old Town

days.title: Salzburg to Hallstatt
activities: Train from Salzburg Hauptbahnhof to Attnang-Puchheim, about 50 minutes (ÖBB West line timetable), then Salzkammergutbahn regional train to Hallstatt station, about 1 hour 15 minutes (7:37 to 8:52 in ÖBB's line 170 timetable)
The station is on the opposite shore: the Hallstatt ferry crosses the lake to the village in about 15 minutes (hallstatt.net), running roughly hourly to meet trains

Rail works: ÖBB has announced rail replacement buses and changed timetables between Attnang-Puchheim and Bad Ischl/Stainach-Irdning from 10 October to 2 November 2026, so allow extra time and check oebb.at if travelling in that window
Wander the village's lakeside lanes and the Market Square in the evening, when day visitors have left

days.title: Hallstatt: salt mine + lake
activities: Salzwelten Hallstatt: the funicular climbs to the Hallstatt High Valley, then the salt mine tour; the site warns of delays at busy times and has no on-site visitor parking
Skywalk viewing platform over Lake Hallstatt, which sits before the mine descent on the Salzwelten visit
Lake ferry or lakeside walk, with a fish meal from the Hallstätter See

days.title: Depart via Salzburg
activities: Ferry to Hallstatt station, then regional train to Attnang-Puchheim and onward to Salzburg Hauptbahnhof (about 50 minutes from Attnang-Puchheim); the whole trip takes roughly 2.5 to 3 hours, so plan departures accordingly
Fly from Salzburg, or continue by Railjet to Vienna (about 2 hours 25 minutes from Salzburg)

food_culture.name: Wiener Schnitzel
food_culture.description: Wiener Schnitzel is a thin breaded and pan-fried veal cutlet; under Austrian food rules the name is reserved for veal, and pork versions are sold as Schnitzel Wiener Art. Served with potato salad and lemon in Viennese restaurants.

food_culture.name: Tafelspitz
food_culture.description: Boiled beef served in its broth with apple-horseradish and chive sauce, a classic Viennese dish long associated with the Habsburg court.

food_culture.name: Salzburger Nockerl
food_culture.description: A large sweet soufflé baked in the oven, traditionally shaped like the hills around Salzburg and served dusted with sugar; meant to be shared at the end of a meal.

food_culture.name: Heuriger wine and Gemischter Satz
food_culture.description: Vienna is one of the few capitals with its own vineyards. A Heuriger is a wine tavern selling the current year's wine, and Wiener Gemischter Satz (field blend) is the city's signature style.

food_culture.name: Viennese coffee house culture
food_culture.description: Vienna's coffee houses are places to linger for hours over one coffee and a newspaper, and the tradition is recognised on UNESCO's Austrian national inventory of intangible cultural heritage.

food_culture.name: Sachertorte and Apfelstrudel
food_culture.description: Chocolate Sachertorte, created in Vienna, and apple strudel are the two cakes most associated with the city's cafes and pastry shops.

food_culture.name: Reinanke from the Hallstätter See
food_culture.description: Whitefish from the Salzkammergut lakes is a regional speciality, often served pan-fried or grilled in lakeside Hallstatt restaurants.

food_culture.name: Salt and Hallstatt
food_culture.description: Hallstatt's name and wealth come from salt mining; the salt mine above the village is among the oldest known in the world, and the village and region are a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape.

title: Tyrol + Salzburgerland Alps: Innsbruck, Kitzbühel + Zell am See, Austria
best_time_description: June to September is the window for this route: the Grossglockner High Alpine Road runs only from early May to early November, with its longest opening hours from 1 June to 31 August, and the cable cars and lakes are at their best. Autumn (September to early October) is quieter.
description: An alpine route across western Austria by rail: Innsbruck below the Nordkette peaks, the Habsburg-era town of Hall in Tirol, the old town of Kitzbühel, then Zell am See on its lake as a base for the Grossglockner High Alpine Road, ending in Salzburg.

days.title: Arrive Innsbruck
activities: Reach Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof; ÖBB's fast Railjet Xpress runs hourly from Vienna to Innsbruck
Stroll the Old Town to the Goldenes Dachl (Golden Roof) and Maria-Theresien-Strasse
Dinner of Tiroler Gröstl or Kasspatzln in the Old Town

days.title: Innsbruck: up the Nordkette
activities: Nordkette cable cars: the Hungerburgbahn funicular runs from the Old Town to Hungerburg in about 8 minutes, then the Seegrubenbahn to Seegrube and the Hafelekarbahn to Hafelekar, the Top of Innsbruck (nordkette.com)
Check the Nordkette website for the current operating timetable before going; autumn maintenance dates were not listed
Hofburg and the Hofkirche in the Old Town in the afternoon; check opening days

days.title: Hall in Tirol + Schloss Ambras
activities: Regional train from Innsbruck Hbf to Hall in Tirol, about 10 minutes (ÖBB Innsbruck to Wörgl timetable valid from 14 June 2026)
Walk Hall's medieval Old Town and the Burg Hasegg mint complex; check opening days
Back to Innsbruck for Schloss Ambras, a Renaissance castle with a museum on the city's southern edge; check opening days

days.title: Innsbruck to Kitzbühel
activities: Train from Innsbruck Hbf to Wörgl takes about 30 to 45 minutes depending on the train (for example 8:20 to 8:51), then change to the Giselabahn regional train to Kitzbühel, about 38 minutes (8:22 to 9:00 or 8:51 onwards in the same pattern; ÖBB Giselabahn timetable valid from 14 June 2026); allow time for the change
Old town with its painted house fronts and the lanes around the Vorderstadt
Hahnenkammbahn cable car, whose station lies close to the Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm rail stop; check season dates before you go

days.title: Kitzbühel to Zell am See
activities: Giselabahn regional train from Kitzbühel to Saalfelden about 45 minutes (9:00 to 9:45), with Zell am See about 12 minutes further (ÖBB Giselabahn timetable valid from 14 June 2026)
Walk the Zell am See lakeside promenade and the old town centre
Evening lake views; book accommodation near the station for an early start on day 6

days.title: Grossglockner High Alpine Road
activities: Drive or join a tour on the Grossglockner High Alpine Road, Austria's highest paved mountain pass road; no train or public transport timings were verified, so arrange a rental car or an organised excursion in advance

The road is open only from early May to early November, from 5:30 to 21:00 between 1 June and 31 August, with the last entry 45 minutes before the night closure (grossglockner.at); a toll applies and the road can close in bad weather
Stop at the Edelweiss-Spitze and Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe viewpoints on the road

days.title: Zell am See to Salzburg
activities: Train from Zell am See to Salzburg Hauptbahnhof takes about 1 hour 35 to 40 minutes (ÖBB Giselabahn timetable valid from 14 June 2026); check the exact departure on oebb.at
Afternoon in Salzburg's Old Town, with Hohensalzburg Fortress above it
Evening Salzburger Nockerl in the Old Town

days.title: Depart from Salzburg
activities: Leave from Salzburg Hauptbahnhof or Salzburg Airport, or continue by Railjet to Vienna (about 2 hours 25 minutes)

food_culture.name: Tiroler Gröstl
food_culture.description: A pan-fried mix of potatoes, bacon or beef and onions topped with a fried egg, a Tyrolean mountain staple often served in huts and Old Town inns.

food_culture.name: Kasnocken and Kaspressknödel
food_culture.description: Tyrolean cheese dumplings and fried cheese-dumpling soup made from Alpine cheese and day-old bread, found in Tyrol and Salzburgerland mountain huts.

food_culture.name: Tiroler Speck
food_culture.description: Tiroler Speck is a smoked, cured ham with EU protected geographical indication status (PGI), sliced thin on a Brettljause cold-cuts board.

food_culture.name: Kaiserschmarrn
food_culture.description: A fluffy shredded pancake with raisins, served with plum compote or apple sauce and a favourite at alpine huts.

food_culture.name: Almabtrieb
food_culture.description: In early autumn, cattle are brought down from high summer pastures decorated with flowers and bells in village celebrations across Tyrol and Salzburgerland; dates vary by village.

food_culture.name: Yodelling and alpine folk music
food_culture.description: Yodelling and Volksmusik are part of Tyrolean and Salzburgerland tradition, performed at village festivals and in inns.

food_culture.name: Goldenes Dachl
food_culture.description: Innsbruck's Golden Roof, a balcony covered in gilded copper tiles on the Old Town, is linked to the Habsburg Emperor Maximilian I and is the city's best-known landmark.

title: Dublin, Cork + Killarney, Ireland
best_time_description: May to September has the longest days and the most reliable weather for Killarney National Park and the Ring of Kerry; Blarney Castle and Gardens keep shorter winter hours (9am to 5pm in November and December). Trains run year-round, so shoulder months work too if you pack for rain.
description: A rail-based first visit to Ireland: two days in Dublin, south by train to Cork for the English Market, Blarney and Cobh, then on to Killarney for the 179 km Ring of Kerry loop and the lakes of Killarney National Park, finishing with the train back to Dublin.

days.title: Arrive Dublin
activities: Settle into the city centre and walk St Stephen's Green and Grafton Street

Trinity College Dublin: the Book of Kells Experience and the Old Library's Long Room (entry is timed and Trinity strongly recommends booking online; Trinity says the Old Library and Long Room stay open to visitors until the end of 2027)
Evening in Temple Bar or a traditional music session in a pub

days.title: Dublin: Kilmainham Gaol + Guinness
activities: Kilmainham Gaol Museum: guided tours only, about one hour; tickets go on sale online 28 days ahead and sell out, so book early on the official site and arrive 15 minutes before your tour
Guinness Storehouse at St James's Gate (buy tickets on the official Guinness site)
Afternoon walk in Phoenix Park

days.title: Dublin to Cork + the English Market
activities: Irish Rail from Dublin Heuston to Cork Kent: the direct services on the timetable valid from 14 December 2025 take about 2 hours 30 to 2 hours 40 (for example 07:00 to 09:35 or 10:00 to 12:32, Monday to Saturday)
Cork's English Market: open Monday to Saturday (about 8am or 8:30am to 6pm per Cork City Council) and closed on Sundays and bank holidays

Afternoon bus to Blarney Castle and Gardens: Bus Eireann route 215 takes about 40 minutes according to Tourism Ireland and its timetable changes on 1 November 2026, so check it. October hours are 9am to 5:30pm (last admission 4:30pm), November and December 9am to 5pm; tickets are sold online or on arrival with no timed slots; kissing the Blarney Stone means climbing 128 steep, narrow steps
days.drive_time: Train, about 2 hrs 30 min to 2 hrs 40 min

days.title: Cobh + Cork city
activities: Train from Cork Kent to Cobh, about 25 minutes (Tourism Ireland)
Titanic Experience Cobh, about a 6 minute walk from Cobh station, and St Colman's Cathedral
Back in Cork, wander the Shandon area and the city's riverside streets

days.title: Cork to Killarney
activities: Irish Rail from Cork Kent to Killarney on the Tralee line: about 1 hour 20 minutes on the through train (for example 06:25 to 07:49, Monday to Saturday) to about 2 hours when you change at Mallow (for example 10:25 to 12:21)

Afternoon at Ross Castle on Lough Leane: the interior is by guided tour only, first come first served, 15 people per tour (Heritage Ireland lists the 2026 season as 5 March to 3 November, 09:30 to 17:00)
Evening in Killarney town
days.drive_time: Train, about 1 hr 20 min to 2 hrs

days.title: The Ring of Kerry
activities: Drive or take a guided day tour around the 179 km Ring of Kerry loop of the Iveragh Peninsula from Killarney via Moll's Gap, Kenmare, Waterville and Cahersiveen; Discover Ireland puts the driving at about 3.5 hours without stops, so plan a full day
Photo stops at Moll's Gap and Coomakista Pass between Waterville and Caherdaniel
Return to Killarney for the evening
days.drive_time: Loop, 179 km, about 3 hrs 30 min driving without stops

days.title: Killarney National Park
activities: Muckross House, Gardens and Traditional Farms: tickets are bought on arrival with no pre-booking; the gardens and the national park are free
Walk the marked trail to Torc Waterfall (uphill, seasonal opening hours apply)
Boat or walk around Lough Leane in the afternoon

days.title: Killarney to Dublin
activities: Irish Rail from Killarney to Dublin Heuston with a change at Mallow: about 3 hours 15 minutes to 3 hours 20 minutes on the timetable valid from 14 December 2025 (for example 09:41 to 12:58, Monday to Saturday)
Evening in Dublin before flying home, or fly from Dublin Airport the same night
days.drive_time: Train, about 3 hrs 15 min to 3 hrs 20 min

food_culture.name: Full Irish breakfast
food_culture.description: A cooked breakfast of bacon, sausage, egg, tomato, soda bread and black and white pudding, served in cafes and guesthouses across the country; a standard first meal in Dublin or Killarney.

food_culture.name: Drisheen
food_culture.description: A traditional Cork blood pudding, milder and softer than black pudding, historically sold in Cork's English Market; ask the market's butchers and traders if you want to try it.

food_culture.name: Irish soda bread
food_culture.description: A quick bread raised with bicarbonate of soda and buttermilk rather than yeast, served with soups, seafood and butter in most cafes and pubs.

food_culture.name: Irish stout
food_culture.description: Dublin is home to Guinness, while Cork has its own stouts, Murphy's and Beamish; pubs in both cities pour them, and the Guinness Storehouse in Dublin runs the brand's visitor experience.

food_culture.name: Traditional music session
food_culture.description: Informal sessions of fiddles, tin whistles and bodhran in pubs, common in Dublin, Cork and Killarney; sit quietly, buy a drink and listen rather than request songs.

food_culture.name: The Blarney Stone
food_culture.description: Kissing the stone at the top of Blarney Castle is said to give the gift of the gab; it is an optional climb of 128 steep, narrow steps.

title: Westport, Galway + the Aran Islands, Ireland
best_time_description: May to September gives the longest days for the Croagh Patrick climb, the Great Western Greenway and the Aran Islands crossing; Ireland.com notes April to September are the popular months to climb Croagh Patrick, and the last Sunday in July is the busy annual pilgrimage. Dun Aonghasa on Inis Mor has shorter hours from November (09:30 to 16:00).
description: A slower west-coast route by train and ferry: Dublin to Westport for Croagh Patrick and the Great Western Greenway on Clew Bay, across to Galway, then the ferry to Inis Mor and the cliff fort of Dun Aonghasa before the train back to Dublin.

days.title: Dublin to Westport
activities: Irish Rail from Dublin Heuston to Westport on the timetable valid from 14 December 2025: the 07:35 departure (Monday to Saturday) reaches Westport at 11:02, about 3 hours 25 minutes, via Athlone
Walk The Octagon, The Mall and Westport Quay
Evening traditional music at Matt Molloy's pub

days.title: Croagh Patrick
activities: Climb Croagh Patrick from the car park at Murrisk on the R335: the marked path is about 7 km and Ireland.com estimates 3 to 4 hours for the round trip over steep, rocky and sometimes muddy ground; start in the morning, wear hiking boots and carry layers
Without a car, the Bus Eireann route 450 stops at Murrisk about 15 minutes from Westport (Discover Ireland)
Rest and dinner in Westport

days.title: Great Western Greenway
activities: Hire a bike in Westport (Clew Bay Bike Hire and Westport Electric Bike Rental both operate there) and ride the traffic-free greenway to Newport, 12.5 km
Optional extension from Newport to Mulranny, another 18 km (Discover Ireland); one-way shuttle back to Westport is offered by hire companies and should be booked in advance in peak season
Evening in Westport

days.title: Westport to Galway
activities: Irish Rail from Westport to Athlone on the 09:45 departure (Monday to Saturday), arriving 11:33, about 1 hour 50 minutes; change at Athlone to the Dublin to Galway service that leaves Athlone at 12:50 and reaches Galway Ceannt at 13:51 (timetable valid from 14 December 2025; check the connection on irishrail.ie)
Evening in Galway's Latin Quarter and along Quay Street
Walk to the Spanish Arch at the mouth of the River Corrib
days.drive_time: Train with change at Athlone, about 4 hrs

days.title: Inis Mor + Dun Aonghasa
activities: Aran Island Ferries: shuttle bus from Victoria Place in Galway to Rossaveel, 37 km west of the city, then the ferry to Inis Mor, about 40 minutes; standard sailings leave Rossaveel at 10:30 and 18:00 (18:30 on Fridays), so book both legs online

Dun Aonghasa, the cliff-edge stone fort 7 km from Cill Ronain: open 09:30 to 18:00 April to October and 09:30 to 16:00 November to December, adult ticket 5 euro; there is no barrier at the cliff edge, a drop of 87 metres, and boots are recommended; closed 24 to 30 December
Cycle or walk the island's lanes and stone-walled fields
days.drive_time: Shuttle bus then ferry, ferry about 40 min

days.title: Galway city + Salthill
activities: Galway Cathedral and the Claddagh, the old fishing quarter by the Corrib
Seafood lunch in the Latin Quarter
Afternoon stroll along the Salthill promenade on Galway Bay

days.title: Galway to Dublin
activities: Irish Rail from Galway Ceannt to Dublin Heuston: services take about 2 hours 20 minutes to 2 hours 40 minutes on the timetable valid from 14 December 2025
Time in Dublin before your flight home
days.drive_time: Train, about 2 hrs 20 min to 2 hrs 40 min

food_culture.name: Seafood chowder
food_culture.description: A creamy chowder of fish and shellfish served with brown soda bread, a staple on menus in Galway and Westport.

food_culture.name: Galway Bay oysters
food_culture.description: Oysters from the bays around Galway, eaten raw with brown bread and a pint of stout; Galway holds an annual oyster and seafood festival.

food_culture.name: Boxty
food_culture.description: A traditional Irish potato pancake made from grated and mashed potato, found on pub and restaurant menus in the west of Ireland.

food_culture.name: Reek Sunday pilgrimage
food_culture.description: Pilgrims climb Croagh Patrick on the last Sunday in July each year, and the mountain is very busy that day (Ireland.com).

food_culture.name: Irish language on the Aran Islands
food_culture.description: Irish is widely spoken on Inis Mor and the other Aran Islands, which lie in the Gaeltacht; greeting people with a Gaelic hello is welcomed.

food_culture.name: Pub music in Westport and Galway
food_culture.description: Live traditional music is a fixture in pubs in both towns, for example at Matt Molloy's in Westport, and in the Latin Quarter in Galway.

title: Dubrovnik, Split + Hvar, Croatia
best_time_description: Late May to June and September are the sweet spot: warm enough to swim, with the seasonal Split-Hvar catamaran running its fuller timetable and less crowding than July and August. Jadrolinija publishes the Split-Hvar catamaran as a seasonal 2026 timetable, and winter sailings are much thinner, so avoid November to March for this route.
description: Croatia's classic Dalmatian coast in one line: Dubrovnik's walled Old Town and a day on Lokrum island, the 3 hour 55 minute bus up the coast to Diocletian's Palace in Split, then the catamaran across to Hvar for harbour evenings and the Pakleni islands.

days.title: Arrive Dubrovnik
activities: Settle into the Old Town or the Pile and Ploce area just outside the walls
Evening stroll along the Stradun, the limestone main street, and out to the Old Port

days.title: Dubrovnik city walls + Old Town
activities: Walk the city walls, a 1,940 m circuit with towers and fortresses; the Society that runs them says the ticket is valid for one tour only and re-entry is not possible, so buy it before you go up (shop.citywallsdubrovnik.hr)
Rector's Palace and the Franciscan monastery with its old pharmacy on the Stradun
Evening: sunset drink at a cliffside bar outside the Pile gate

days.title: Lokrum island
activities: Take the official boat from the Old Town harbour to Lokrum Nature Reserve; the reserve's own site sells a ticket from 30 EUR that covers reserve entry and the return boat, sold at the Luza sales point (the published timetable is a PDF on lokrum.hr, so check the sailing times and last return boat for your date)
Walk the island's paths and the Benedictine monastery ruins, and swim from the rocky shore
Late afternoon back in Dubrovnik; dinner of black risotto or grilled fish in the Old Town

days.title: Bus to Split + Diocletian's Palace
activities: FlixBus from Dubrovnik to Split: its route page says as fast as 3 hours 55 minutes, 8 buses a day, first at 03:30 and last at 21:00; book a seat in advance
Split bus station sits beside the ferry port, so you can walk to the Riva waterfront
Afternoon inside Diocletian's Palace: the Peristyle, the Cathedral of St Domnius bell tower and the underground cellars
Evening on the Riva promenade

days.title: Split morning, catamaran to Hvar
activities: Morning on Marjan hill for views over the harbour and the islands

Jadrolinija catamaran from the Split ferry port to Hvar town: the company says the crossing takes 1 hour 5 minutes on a seasonal 2026 timetable (departure times are in its PDF), and a catamaran ticket is tied to the departure time you choose, so book a sailing rather than turning up
Hvar town: St Stephen's Square (Pjaca), the Cathedral and the harbour
Sunset from the waterfront

days.title: Hvar fortress + Pakleni islands
activities: Walk up to the Spanjola (Fortica) fortress above the town for the view over the harbour and the Pakleni islands
Water taxi from Hvar harbour out to one of the Pakleni islands for a swim and a konoba lunch (taxi boats run to demand and in good weather; agree the return time with the skipper)
Evening seafood in Hvar town; try Hvar's gregada fish stew

days.title: Catamaran back + Salona
activities: Morning catamaran back to Split with Jadrolinija (1 hour 5 minutes; check the return timetable and keep the ticket's chosen departure)
Visit the Roman ruins of Salona at Solin on the edge of Split (the ancient capital of the province of Dalmatia)
Last evening in Split's old town

days.title: Departure
activities: Depart from Split Airport or take a bus or ferry onward; the Split bus station and ferry port are side by side in town

food_culture.name: Crni rizot (black risotto)
food_culture.description: Dalmatian cuttlefish risotto coloured with the ink; a staple on konoba and restaurant menus along the coast from Dubrovnik to Split.

food_culture.name: Peka
food_culture.description: Veal, lamb or octopus with potatoes cooked slowly under an iron bell (peka) covered with embers; a Dalmatian dish that usually has to be ordered a few hours ahead.

food_culture.name: Hvarska gregada
food_culture.description: A Hvar fish stew with potatoes, olive oil and white wine, served in the island's konobas and harbour restaurants.

food_culture.name: Rozata
food_culture.description: Dubrovnik's custard flan with a caramel top, flavoured with rose liqueur or lemon, found on Old Town dessert menus.

food_culture.name: Plavac mali wines from Peljesac and Hvar
food_culture.description: Dalmatia's main red grape; the Dingac and Postup wines come from the Peljesac peninsula north-west of Dubrovnik, and Hvar has its own wineries.

food_culture.name: Klapa singing
food_culture.description: Unaccompanied a cappella part-singing from Dalmatia, inscribed on UNESCO's intangible heritage list in 2012; you can hear it in Split and Dubrovnik in evening concerts and at konobas.

food_culture.name: Hvar lace
food_culture.description: The island's lace-making traditions (agave lace sewn by Benedictine nuns in Hvar town) are on UNESCO's intangible heritage list; lace is sold in Hvar town.

title: Zagreb, Plitvice Lakes + Istria, Croatia
best_time_description: Late April to May and September to October suit the inland-to-Istria arc: waterfalls at Plitvice are full in spring, autumn is the Istrian truffle and wine season, and temperatures are mild for walking. The Plitvice park is open 365 days a year but its own site says most hospitality facilities close in the colder part of the year, so winter is a poor fit.
description: Away from the beach: Zagreb's Upper Town and markets, a full day on the boardwalks of Plitvice Lakes National Park, Rijeka's Trsat hill, then Pula's Roman arena and a boat out to the Brijuni islands, with every leg on a named bus operator.

days.title: Arrive Zagreb
activities: Check in near the centre; walk Ban Jelacic Square and the cafe street Tkalciceva in the evening
Try strukli (baked cheese pastry) for dinner

days.title: Zagreb Upper Town + markets
activities: Dolac market and the Cathedral on Kaptol
Upper Town (Gornji grad): the Stone Gate, St Mark's Church with its tiled roof, and the Lotrscak Tower
Museum of Broken Relationships; check its current opening days before you go
Evening in Tkalciceva street; buy a licitar heart as a souvenir

days.title: Zagreb to Plitvice Lakes
activities: Take the first FlixBus from the Zagreb bus station (Avenija Marina Drzica 4); FlixBus lists 2 buses a day, the first at 06:45 and the last at 14:30, in as little as 1 hour 50 minutes

Plitvice Lakes National Park runs from Entrance 1 (Rastovaca) and Entrance 2 (Hladovina), both 07:00 to 18:00 on the park's hours page, with ticket sales until 15:00; check its seasonal hours and buy tickets through its ticketing site

Pick a route: the park lists Program B at 3 to 4 hours (electric boat on Kozjak and a panoramic vehicle) or Program C at 4 to 5 hours (8,000 m) from Entrance 1, or Program H at 4 to 6 hours from Entrance 2
Overnight near the park

days.title: Plitvice to Rijeka
activities: Optional early walk at Entrance 1 before the bus (the park is open 365 days a year)
FlixBus Plitvice Lakes to Rijeka: its route page lists 3 buses a day, first at 09:45 and last at 17:15, in as little as 5 hours 30 minutes; the long journey means the afternoon is mostly travel
Evening on Rijeka's Korzo promenade

days.title: Rijeka to Pula + the Arena
activities: Morning on Trsat hill above the city for the castle and views over the Kvarner bay
FlixBus Rijeka to Pula: its route page lists 4 buses a day, first at 03:40 and last at 22:20, in as little as 1 hour 25 minutes
Afternoon at Pula's Roman Arena, then the Temple of Augustus and the Arch of the Sergii in the old town

days.title: Brijuni National Park
activities: Go to the small town of Fažana: the Brijuni National Park site says the boat leaves from a jetty in the centre and tickets are bought at the park's Fažana office (Brionska 10) or online, and the sailing takes about 15 minutes to Veliki Brijun; its own pages give no bus time from Pula, so check a local bus or taxi in advance

The park's guided excursion takes around 4 hours with a tourist train around the island, the Safari Park and a museum exhibition; its FAQ says a ticket cannot be used at another time or refunded, so pick your date firmly
Back in Pula in the evening for dinner; try fuzi pasta with truffles

days.title: Pula to Zagreb + departure
activities: FlixBus Pula to Zagreb: its route page lists 6 buses a day, first at 02:00 and last at 20:30, in as little as 3 hours 45 minutes; or fly home from Pula airport instead
Allow buffer for Zagreb airport or the evening bus if you are flying out of Zagreb

food_culture.name: Strukli
food_culture.description: A Zagreb and Zagorje dish of dough filled with fresh cheese, baked or boiled; found in traditional restaurants around Upper Town.

food_culture.name: Fuzi with truffles
food_culture.description: Hand-rolled Istrian pasta often served with truffles or in a meat sauce; fuzi is a staple of Istrian konobas.

food_culture.name: Istrian prosciutto and cheese
food_culture.description: Air-dried Istrian pršut and local sheep and cow cheeses, traditionally eaten as a starter with olive oil.

food_culture.name: Malvazija Istarska and Teran
food_culture.description: Istria's signature white and red wines; Malvazija is the dry white most often served with seafood and pasta.

food_culture.name: Licitar hearts
food_culture.description: Painted gingerbread hearts from the Zagreb region that UNESCO added to its intangible heritage list in 2010; sold at Zagreb markets and souvenir stalls.

food_culture.name: Two-part singing in the Istrian scale
food_culture.description: A traditional Istrian folk singing style (UNESCO intangible heritage, 2009) that you may hear at village festivals and folk evenings across Istria.

title: Prague, Kutná Hora + Český Krumlov, Czechia
best_time_description: Late April to June and September to October give mild weather for walking Prague's hills and Český Krumlov's lanes and fewer crowds than July and August; December suits Christmas markets but is cold and short on daylight. Check seasonal opening dates for Český Krumlov's castle gardens before you go.
description: Czechia's classic first-timer route: three days in Prague's castle, bridges and Old Town, a day trip to the silver-mining town of Kutná Hora and its bone-filled Sedlec Ossuary, then a bus south to the riverside medieval town of Český Krumlov.

days.title: Arrive Prague
activities: Check in near the Old Town or Malá Strana
Evening walk across Charles Bridge and through Old Town Square
Dinner at a traditional pub (hospoda) serving svíčková or goulash with Czech lager

days.title: Prague Castle + Malá Strana
activities: Prague Castle complex, including St Vitus Cathedral (buy a castle circuit ticket; security queues form at the main gates, so go early)
Walk down through the castle's Golden Lane area and Malá Strana's lanes
Petřín Hill and its lookout tower for a view over the city
Evening beer at a pub in Malá Strana

days.title: Old Town + Jewish Quarter
activities: Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock, which performs on the hour
Jewish Museum in Prague (Maisel, Pinkas, Klausen and Spanish synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery); closed Saturdays and Jewish holidays, so plan this day around that
Wenceslas Square and the National Museum area
Optional riverside walk toward Vyšehrad fortress in the evening

days.title: Day trip to Kutná Hora
activities: Direct Vysočina fast train (R) from Prague main station (Praha hl.n.) to Kutná Hora hl.n., hourly; České dráhy lists about 1 hour including a change to the local train for Kutná Hora město
Sedlec Ossuary, a chapel decorated with the bones of tens of thousands of people; early arrival avoids tour groups
Cathedral of St Barbara, part of the UNESCO-listed Kutná Hora historic centre
Italian Court (Vlašský dvůr) and the old silver-mining town centre; return to Prague by train in the evening
days.drive_time: Train, about 1 hr each way (České dráhy)

days.title: Bus to Český Krumlov
activities: Direct bus (RegioJet or FlixBus) from Prague to Český Krumlov, about 3 hours; the town's tourist office says there are several a day and tickets are best booked online in advance
Settle in and wander the old town inside the Vltava river loop
Cloak Bridge and the Český Krumlov Castle exterior and courtyards
Dinner in a riverside restaurant

days.title: Český Krumlov Castle + river
activities: Český Krumlov Castle guided tour and Castle Tower views (reserve the tour times you want; some castle parts and the gardens are seasonal, so check dates for your month)
Egon Schiele Art Centrum, an art museum in a former brewery
Late afternoon beer at a pub tied to the town's Eggenberg brewery tradition
Optional paddle on the Vltava in the warm months (seasonal)

days.title: Return to Prague + depart
activities: Morning stroll through the old town before checking out
Bus back to Prague, about 3 hours (the tourist office also describes a train option via České Budějovice, also about 3 hours)
Allow buffer time before any evening flight from Václav Havel Airport Prague
days.lodging_suggestion: Prague (airport hotel or Old Town if overnighting)

food_culture.name: Svíčková na smetaně
food_culture.description: Marinated beef sirloin in a creamy root-vegetable sauce, served with bread dumplings, a dollop of cranberry sauce and whipped cream; a staple of traditional Czech pubs and restaurants.

food_culture.name: Vepřo-knedlo-zelo
food_culture.description: Roast pork with dumplings and sauerkraut, often described as a Czech national dish and found on hospoda menus across Prague and Český Krumlov.

food_culture.name: Smažený sýr
food_culture.description: A slice of breaded, fried cheese served with tartar sauce and fries, a common pub and street-food meal in Prague.

food_culture.name: Czech lager (pivo)
food_culture.description: Czechia's pale lager tradition shapes daily life; beer is served in half-litre glasses at pubs, and Pilsner-style lagers are the benchmark. Český Krumlov has its own Eggenberg brewery heritage.

food_culture.name: Hospoda culture
food_culture.description: The Czech pub is a neighbourhood social institution where tables are often shared and beer arrives without ordering again unless you place a coaster on your glass to say stop.

food_culture.name: Sedlec Ossuary
food_culture.description: A small chapel in Kutná Hora decorated with the bones of tens of thousands of people, including a chandelier said to contain every bone in the human body; part of the UNESCO-listed Kutná Hora site.

title: Brno, Lednice-Valtice + Olomouc, Moravia, Czechia
best_time_description: May to June and September to October suit Moravia: the Lednice-Valtice parks are at their best, wine cellars are open and the harvest season begins in autumn. Winter is cold and quiet, and some park attractions open seasonally, so check dates for your month.
description: A different side of Czechia in the east: Brno's functionalist architecture and hilltop fortress, a day in the wine country and UNESCO-listed castle landscape of Lednice-Valtice, then the baroque university city of Olomouc, with a fast train back to Prague.

days.title: Arrive Brno
activities: Reach Brno by train from Prague on the České dráhy railjet or EuroCity, about 2 hours 36 minutes (ČD lists 34 connections a day), or fly into Brno-Tuřany
Check in near the old town
Evening in the Zelný trh (Cabbage Market) square area
days.drive_time: Train from Prague, about 2 hrs 36 min (České dráhy railjet)

days.title: Brno old town + Špilberk
activities: Zelný trh (Cabbage Market), a produce market square with the Parnas fountain
Cathedral of St Peter and Paul on Petrov hill
Brno Astronomical Clock, a black glass column on Náměstí Svobody, which releases a glass ball daily at 11:00
Špilberk Castle, the hilltop fortress and city museum
Capuchin Crypt, a monastery crypt of mummified monks

days.title: Villa Tugendhat + functionalist Brno
activities: Villa Tugendhat, the UNESCO-listed modernist villa by Mies van der Rohe; closed Mondays and interior entry only with a ticket bought in advance, so book before you travel
Walk through Brno's other functionalist architecture
Evening wine bar or pub in the centre

days.title: Lednice-Valtice day trip
activities: Train from Brno to Břeclav, about 1 hour on the slower services, then a local bus to Lednice (bus time not confirmed from an official source; check IDOS for the day)
Lednice Château and its park, part of the UNESCO-listed Lednice-Valtice cultural landscape
Minaret in the Lednice park (seasonal)
Valtice and the National Wine Centre, with a tasting of Moravian wines at the Wine Salon of the Czech Republic
Return to Brno in the evening
days.drive_time: Train to Břeclav, about 1 hr, plus local bus

days.title: Brno to Olomouc
activities: Train from Brno to Olomouc, about 1 hour 30 minutes on the fastest direct ČD services (some stop more often and take longer)
Settle in and walk the Upper Square (Horní náměstí)
Holy Trinity Column, UNESCO-listed, and the Olomouc Astronomical Clock
Dinner of local specialties

days.title: Olomouc old town
activities: St Wenceslas Cathedral and the Premyslid Palace
Archdiocesan Museum Olomouc
Baroque fountains of the old town (six Baroque fountains in the centre)
Taste Olomoucké tvarůžky, the local aged cheese, at a restaurant in town

days.title: Return to Prague + depart
activities: Pendolino from Olomouc to Prague main station, about 2 hours 17 minutes (ČD lists 2 h 17 min Olomouc to Prague; EuroCity and InterCity take about 2 h 27 min)
Connect to Václav Havel Airport Prague or stay another night in the capital
days.drive_time: Train, about 2 hrs 17 min (SC Pendolino, České dráhy)

food_culture.name: Moravian wine
food_culture.description: South Moravia is Czechia's main wine region; the Lednice-Valtice area has cellars, and the National Wine Centre in Valtice runs tastings of Czech wines.

food_culture.name: Olomoucké tvarůžky
food_culture.description: A pungent aged cheese from the Olomouc region with a protected geographical status, eaten fried, in spreads or on bread with beer.

food_culture.name: Svíčková and Moravian roast meats
food_culture.description: Czech comfort food with regional variations; Moravian restaurants serve roast pork or duck with dumplings and cabbage alongside local wine.

food_culture.name: Zelný trh market
food_culture.description: Brno's Cabbage Market, one of the oldest city squares in Brno, is a working produce market where locals still buy vegetables, fruit and flowers.

food_culture.name: Holy Trinity Column, Olomouc
food_culture.description: A baroque plague column in Olomouc's Upper Square, UNESCO-listed, that reflects the city's Habsburg-era civic pride and is a meeting point for locals.

food_culture.name: Functionalist architecture
food_culture.description: Brno is known for interwar functionalism, including Villa Tugendhat, a modernist house and UNESCO site where light and open plan became a model for twentieth-century design.

title: Golden Circle + South Coast to Jokulsarlon, Iceland
best_time_description: June to early September is the easy window: every road on this route is paved Ring Road or main road, the South Coast waterfalls are fully accessible and daylight is long. The route is paved and open year-round (Visit Iceland says all of the Ring Road is paved and open throughout the year), but outside summer storms and ice can close sections at short notice, daylight is short, and trails at Gullfoss are sometimes closed by ice. Highland F-roads (e.g. F208 Fjallabak, Sprengisandur F26) are not used on this route: they are usually closed from about mid-September until June or July, and Vegagerdin's 2021-2025 opening table puts most openings between late May and mid-July, so a highland detour is only an option in July to early September with a suitable 4x4, after checking road.is (traffic service 1777, 24 hours).
description: Reykjavik, the three Golden Circle stops (Thingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss), then east along the paved Ring Road past Seljalandsfoss, Skogafoss and the black sand of Reynisfjara to Skaftafell and the glacier lagoon at Jokulsarlon, and back west. A first-timer's Iceland on paved roads only, so a standard rental car is enough in summer.

days.title: Arrive Reykjavik
activities: Collect the rental car at Keflavik Airport (headlights must be on at all times, all year, per safetravel.is)
Walk Reykjavik: Hallgrimskirkja church tower, Harpa concert hall and the Sun Voyager sculpture on the waterfront
Soak in a public geothermal swimming pool such as Laugardalslaug: shower without swimwear before you enter

days.title: Golden Circle: Thingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss
activities: Thingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site): walk the Almannagja canyon to Oxararfoss; parking costs 1,000 ISK per car per day at the park's own machines or Checkit.is per thingvellir.is, fees may have changed since
Silfra fissure: snorkelling or diving here needs a permit and is done through licensed operators, so reserve in advance if you want it
Geysir geothermal area: Strokkur erupts roughly every 8-10 minutes on the marked paths
Gullfoss waterfall (31 m, open year-round; in winter the trails to the lower viewing platforms are sometimes closed for ice and snow)
Optional on the way: Keri crater and the historic bishop's seat at Skalholt
days.drive_time: Whole Golden Circle is about 250 km round trip from Reykjavik (Visit Iceland); live times at road.is

days.title: Seljalandsfoss, Skogafoss + Vik
activities: Seljalandsfoss: you can usually walk behind the falls in summer only
Skogafoss: climb the staircase beside the falls to the viewing platform
Dyrholaey nature reserve: the upper lighthouse area is closed to traffic overnight and parts close each spring for nesting from roughly May to late June (dates shift, follow the signs)
Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vik: sneaker waves reach far up the sand even in calm weather, so stay well back from the water and read the warning signs
Lava Show in Vik is an indoor option on a rainy evening
days.drive_time: Reykjavik to Vik: about 2 hr 15 min without stops (Visit Iceland); this day starts at Selfoss and has several stops, so allow the whole day

days.title: Vik to Skaftafell + Jokulsarlon
activities: Drive the paved Ring Road east across the lava fields and glacial outwash plains toward Vatnajokull National Park; one-lane bridges have a 50 km/h limit (safetravel.is)
Skaftafell in Vatnajokull National Park: hike to Svartifoss waterfall
Jokulsarlon glacier lagoon and the Diamond Beach next to it; boat tours on the lagoon run seasonally, so check the operator's schedule
This is the longest day: I could not find an official drive time for Vik to Jokulsarlon, so check umferdin.is or road.is for live times and fuel up before leaving Vik

days.title: Diamond Beach + back west to Vik
activities: Early walk on Diamond Beach and the lagoon shore before tour buses arrive
Drive back west along the Ring Road with a stop at Skaftafell if you skipped it
Solheimajokull glacier outlet: walk toward the ice on your own, or take a guided glacier walk where the operator provides ice gear
Check weather and road conditions at safetravel.is and road.is in the morning, since conditions can change quickly outside summer
days.drive_time: No official time found for Jokulsarlon to Vik; check live times at road.is

days.title: Vik to Reykjavik
activities: Drive the Ring Road back to Reykjavik
Afternoon in Reykjavik: Perlan museum, the old harbour or the shops on Laugavegur
Try a pylsa (Icelandic hot dog) from Baejarins Beztu Pylsur by the harbour
days.drive_time: Vik to Reykjavik: about 2 hr 15 min without stops (Visit Iceland, Reykjavik to Vik figure)

days.title: Depart
activities: Return the car and fly out of Keflavik Airport; allow extra time at the border for Entry/Exit System checks if you are not a Schengen citizen
Selfoss to Keflavik is roughly an hour in normal conditions (south.is), so allow longer from Reykjavik if the weather is bad

food_culture.name: Kjotsupa (Icelandic lamb soup)
food_culture.description: A hearty soup of lamb, root vegetables and herbs served at cafes and roadside restaurants all along the South Coast, a standard warm stop after Gullfoss or the beaches.

food_culture.name: Skyr
food_culture.description: A thick, strained dairy product eaten with berries or on its own at breakfast; sold in every supermarket and served in most guesthouses.

food_culture.name: Pylsa (Icelandic hot dog)
food_culture.description: Lamb-based hot dog eaten 'with everything' (raw and fried onion, ketchup, sweet mustard, remoulade), a cheap harbour-side lunch in Reykjavik.

food_culture.name: Brennivin
food_culture.description: Caraway-flavoured schnapps traditionally served ice cold, often alongside fermented shark at midwinter feasts.

food_culture.name: Public geothermal swimming pools
food_culture.description: Nearly every town has a heated outdoor pool and hot pots; the custom is to shower thoroughly without swimwear before entering, and locals treat the pool as a social meeting place.

food_culture.name: Thingvellir and the Althing
food_culture.description: Thingvellir, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004, is Iceland's most significant historic and geological site, with the Almannagja canyon, Lake Thingvallavatn and Oxararfoss waterfall; the Althing is the name of Iceland's parliament and its historic assembly is tied to this place.

title: Snaefellsnes + West Iceland Loop, Iceland
best_time_description: May to September for the full peninsula: the 90 km Snaefellsnes peninsula is rated year-round by Visit Iceland and the main roads are paved, but road 570 up Snaefellsjokull is steep, unpaved and open summer only (4x4 needed), seabirds nest at Londrangar in summer, and winter daylight is short. Storms can close road sections at short notice outside summer (Visit Iceland names Holtavorduheidi on the Ring Road north of Borgarnes among passes that can close September to May), so check road.is. Highland F-roads (e.g. F208 Fjallabak, Sprengisandur F26) are not used on this route: they are usually closed from about mid-September until June or July, and Vegagerdin's 2021-2025 opening table puts most openings between late May and mid-July, so a highland detour is only an option in July to early September with a suitable 4x4, after checking road.is (traffic service 1777, 24 hours).
description: A compact western loop for a shorter trip: Hvalfjordur and Borgarfjordur's waterfalls, then a loop around the 90 km Snaefellsnes peninsula (Kirkjufell, Arnarstapi, Djupalonssandur, Snaefellsjokull National Park), returning to Reykjavik. Quieter than the South Coast and entirely on paved roads except the optional summer-only road 570.

days.title: Reykjavik to Borgarfjordur
activities: Pick up the car in Reykjavik and take Route 1 north through the Hvalfjordur tunnel toward Borgarnes
Borgarnes: stop at the Settlement Center museum or the shore walk by the fjord
Hraunfossar and Barnafoss in Borgarfjordur, a 40 km detour from the Ring Road per Visit Iceland (lava-spring waterfalls)
Deildartunguhver hot spring near Reykholt in Borgarfjordur (a roadside geothermal stop; check locally for access)
days.drive_time: Reykjavik to the start of Snaefellsnes is about 2 hours (Visit Iceland); Hraunfossar adds a 40 km detour from the Ring Road

days.title: Borgarnes to Stykkisholmur via Route 54
activities: Join Route 54 at the roundabout just past Borgarnes: the whole loop around the peninsula is about 260 km starting and ending in Borgarnes (Visit Iceland)
Eldborg crater, rising 60 m above the surrounding scrub, a short walk from the road
Gerduberg basalt column cliff, columns up to 14 m tall
Stykkisholmur: harbour, the Library of Water and the old town of painted wooden houses; a ferry runs from here to Flatey island if you want a half-day extension
days.drive_time: No official time found for Borgarnes to Stykkisholmur; check live times at road.is

days.title: Kirkjufell + the south coast of Snaefellsnes
activities: Kirkjufell mountain and Kirkjufellsfoss at Grundarfjordur
Djupalonssandur black pebble beach with the lifting stones, and the sea stacks of Londrangar (seabirds nest here in summer)
Arnarstapi to Hellnar 2.5 km coastal path
Vatnshellir lava tube: guided tours go 35 m below ground into an 8,000-year-old lava tube, so reserve ahead
days.drive_time: No official time found for individual legs on the peninsula; the full 260 km loop from Borgarnes is the figure Visit Iceland gives

days.title: Snaefellsjokull National Park, then back to Reykjavik
activities: Snaefellsjokull National Park, the only national park in Iceland that runs from glacier summit to the Atlantic shore; Malarrif visitor centre (no hours confirmed, ask locally)
Saxholl crater (a short climb up the staircase)
Optional: road 570 toward the glacier is steep, unpaved and open in summer only, 4x4 required (Visit Iceland); skip it if closed or in doubt
Drive back via Route 54 and Route 1 to Reykjavik; Visit Iceland says a one-day Snaefellsnes trip from Reykjavik is five to six hours of total driving
days.drive_time: About 2 hours between Reykjavik and the peninsula (Visit Iceland)

days.title: Reykjavik and departure
activities: Morning at the Reykjavik old harbour and the Perlan museum
Drive to Keflavik Airport; allow time for Entry/Exit System checks for non-Schengen passports
Selfoss to Keflavik is roughly an hour in normal conditions (south.is), so give Reykjavik to Keflavik a similar margin

food_culture.name: Plokkfiskur
food_culture.description: A comforting mash of boiled fish, potato and onion in a white sauce, eaten with dark rye bread at harbour cafes in Stykkisholmur and Borgarnes.

food_culture.name: Hardfiskur
food_culture.description: Wind-dried fish torn into strips and eaten with butter, a traditional Icelandic snack sold in supermarkets and harbour shops.

food_culture.name: Hverabraud (geothermal rye bread)
food_culture.description: Dense sweet rye bread traditionally baked slowly in the hot ground near geothermal areas; try it at Laugarvatn or in a bakery.

food_culture.name: Icelandic craft beer
food_culture.description: Small Icelandic breweries make lagers and ales that appear on bar menus around West Iceland; ask for a local tap rather than an imported one.

food_culture.name: Thorrablot midwinter feast
food_culture.description: A midwinter feast of preserved foods such as fermented shark, smoked lamb and pickled ram's testicles, usually washed down with brennivin; restaurants serve it in late winter.

food_culture.name: Sagas and the hidden people
food_culture.description: Snaefellsjokull and the farms of the peninsula feature in the Icelandic sagas, and many Icelanders still tell stories of elves and hidden people living in the lava rocks.

title: Singapore Classic: Marina Bay, Chinatown + Sentosa
best_time_description: Singapore is hot and humid all year. Smartraveller notes monsoon rain and strong winds from December to March and June to September, and regional smoke haze that can affect Singapore from June to October, so February to April is an editorial pick for fewer weather and haze risks rather than a met-service statistic. Check the National Environment Agency's air-quality and weather updates before you fly.
description: A first-timer's loop of Singapore's essentials: the Marina Bay skyline and Supertree Grove, the Civic District and Chinatown's temples and hawker food, a beach day on Sentosa, and Little India and Kampong Glam, all reachable on the MRT.

days.title: Arrive Changi, Jewel + Marina Bay
activities: Arrive at Changi Airport; LTA gives the current MRT journey from Changi Airport to Marina Bay as about 50 minutes, and Changi Airport's own guidance gives about 30 minutes by taxi to the city. The MRT route is Changi Airport (CG2) to Tanah Merah (EW4) to the East West Line, or Expo (CG1/DT35) to the Downtown Line.
If you land with time to spare, look at Jewel Changi Airport's Rain Vortex before leaving the airport area; check Jewel's website for show times and any closures
Gardens by the Bay: walk among the Supertrees at Supertree Grove (the outdoor gardens are the free part; the conservatories and elevated walkways are ticketed, so book those ahead if you want them)
Evening walk along the Marina Bay waterfront for the skyline view toward Marina Bay Sands
days.lodging_suggestion: Marina Bay or City Hall area

days.title: Civic District + Chinatown
activities: Merlion Park and the Esplanade waterfront, then the Civic District on foot: National Gallery Singapore and the Asian Civilisations Museum (ticketed; check each museum's website for opening days)
Chinatown: Sri Mariamman Temple, Singapore's oldest Hindu temple, and the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple and Museum on South Bridge Road (modest dress expected at both)

Dinner at Maxwell Food Centre in Chinatown, one of the hawker centres where Hainanese chicken rice is a standard order; hawker culture is on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (inscribed 16 December 2020)

days.title: Sentosa Beach Day
activities: MRT to HarbourFront (CC29/NE1), walk to VivoCity Level 3 and board the Sentosa Express monorail to the island (Sentosa's guidance lists service every 4 to 8 minutes, 7am to midnight; an entry fare applies on the way in)
Spend the day at Sentosa's beaches such as Siloso Beach and walk its seafront paths; Sentosa also has paid attractions, which you should book on their own sites if you want them
Return to VivoCity and MRT at HarbourFront for an evening in the city

days.title: Little India + Kampong Glam, depart
activities: Little India: Tekka Centre (hawker food and market) and the Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple (modest dress, shoes off at the temple entrance)
Kampong Glam: Sultan Mosque (visitors should dress modestly and check the mosque's visiting hours), Arab Street and Haji Lane
Head back to Changi Airport; allow the 50-minute MRT figure from Marina Bay's side as a guide, and more if you start from a different part of the city

food_culture.name: Hawker culture
food_culture.description: Singapore's hawker centres are open-air food courts where stalls sell inexpensive cooked dishes. UNESCO inscribed 'Hawker culture in Singapore, community dining and culinary practices in a multicultural urban context' on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on 16 December 2020. Many hawker centres close on a regular cleaning day, so check the centre's notice before a long trip.

food_culture.name: Hainanese chicken rice
food_culture.description: Poached chicken served over rice cooked in chicken stock, with chilli sauce and ginger paste; a staple order at hawker centres across the island.

food_culture.name: Chilli crab
food_culture.description: Crab cooked in a sweet, savoury and mildly spicy tomato-chilli sauce, eaten with fried or steamed buns to soak up the sauce; a long-standing Singapore seafood dish.

food_culture.name: Kopi and teh
food_culture.description: Singapore-style coffee and tea are sold in kopitiams and hawker centres with local ordering terms for sweetness and milk, such as 'kopi-o' for coffee with sugar and no milk; the stall will explain if you ask.

food_culture.name: Four-culture neighbourhoods
food_culture.description: Chinatown, Little India and Kampong Glam sit within a short ride of each other, reflecting Singapore's Chinese, Indian and Malay communities, each with its own temples or mosque, food and shops.

food_culture.name: Temple and mosque etiquette
food_culture.description: Sri Mariamman Temple, the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple and Sultan Mosque are active places of worship, where visitors are expected to dress modestly, remove shoes where asked and follow posted photography rules.

title: Singapore Hawker Food, Heritage + Green Escapes
best_time_description: Singapore is hot and humid all year. Smartraveller notes monsoon rain and strong winds from December to March and June to September, and regional smoke haze that can affect Singapore from June to October. This route is mostly outdoors (Pulau Ubin, the Southern Ridges), so February to April is an editorial pick for lower weather and haze risk, not a met-service statistic; check NEA before each outdoor day.
description: A slower, greener route: Peranakan Katong and hawker dining, a day among Pulau Ubin's trails, the UNESCO-listed Botanic Gardens and Tiong Bahru, the Southern Ridges canopy walk, and Little India to finish.

days.title: Arrive + Katong Peranakan Quarter
activities: Arrive at Changi Airport; Changi Airport's guidance gives about 30 minutes by taxi to the city, and LTA gives about 50 minutes by MRT from the airport to Marina Bay
Katong and Joo Chiat on the east side: walk the colourful Peranakan shophouses around Koon Seng Road
Dinner at a local kopitiam or hawker centre in the Katong area; laksa is the dish this neighbourhood is known for

days.title: Pulau Ubin Day Trip
activities: Getting there: MRT to Tanah Merah (EW4), bus 2 from Exit B to Changi Village (NParks also lists buses 29, 59 and 109), then walk to Changi Point Ferry Terminal at 51 Lorong Bekukong

Bumboat to Pulau Ubin: NParks says the crossing takes about 10 minutes and costs $4 per person each way plus $2 per bicycle; boats are privately run, usually operate on demand from 6am to 7pm and leave when 12 passengers are aboard, so plan to be back at the Ubin jetty well before 7pm

On the island, walk, cycle or hire a local van to explore the trails; Visit Singapore describes a roughly one-kilometre boardwalk at Chek Jawa Wetlands (confirm current access and tide notes with NParks)
If no bumboat is waiting at the Ubin jetty for the return, NParks lists a helpline at 1800-471 7300

days.title: Botanic Gardens + Tiong Bahru
activities: Singapore Botanic Gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2015: free entry, open 5am to midnight daily; the National Orchid Garden inside is ticketed (8.30am to 7pm, last entry 6pm)
Tiong Bahru: explore the neighbourhood's low-rise residential estate and its market and hawker centre for lunch
Dinner at Lau Pa Sat in the central business district, a historic market building now housing food stalls

days.title: Southern Ridges Canopy Walk
activities: Start at HarbourFront MRT (NE1/CC29), Exit D, near Marang Road, for the Southern Ridges trail

Walk Mount Faber Park, cross Henderson Waves (a 274-metre pedestrian bridge linking Mount Faber Park and Telok Blangah Hill Park), continue through HortPark and finish at Kent Ridge Park's Canopy Walk; NParks lists the full route as 10 km, moderate to challenging, 3 to 5 hours of walking
NParks has noted a footpath section of the Mount Faber Loop closed for maintenance since 14 January 2025; check NParks for the current status before going
Finish near Kent Ridge MRT or Pasir Panjang MRT (both Circle Line) for the ride back; carry water, as most of the route is outdoors

days.title: Little India + depart
activities: Little India: Tekka Centre for a hawker breakfast or lunch (roti prata and Indian dishes are the local draw) and the Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple (modest dress, shoes off at the entrance)
Kampong Glam if time allows: Sultan Mosque exterior and Arab Street
Return to Changi Airport; allow about 50 minutes by MRT from Marina Bay according to LTA, more from other starting points

food_culture.name: Hawker culture
food_culture.description: Singapore's hawker culture was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on 16 December 2020. UNESCO's committee described hawker centres as community dining rooms where people of different backgrounds eat together.

food_culture.name: Laksa
food_culture.description: A spicy noodle soup in a coconut-milk broth, associated in Singapore with the Katong area on the east side, where the Peranakan culture shaped the local cuisine.

food_culture.name: Roti prata
food_culture.description: A South Indian-style flatbread, pan-fried and eaten with curry, served at Indian stalls and eateries in Little India and across hawker centres.

food_culture.name: Satay
food_culture.description: Skewered, grilled meat served with peanut sauce, a hawker favourite eaten across Singapore.

food_culture.name: Peranakan heritage
food_culture.description: The Peranakan community blends Chinese and Malay heritage; its legacy shows in Katong and Joo Chiat's coloured shophouses and in dishes such as laksa.

food_culture.name: Pulau Ubin and Singapore's island life
food_culture.description: Pulau Ubin is reached by privately run bumboat from Changi Point, and NParks's visitor page describes it as a place to walk or cycle designated trails, a contrast with the city's high-rise districts.

title: Kuala Lumpur, Cameron Highlands + Malacca, Malaysia
best_time_description: Roughly June to August is usually the drier stretch for the west coast, but rain can fall in any month. Australia's Smartraveller notes the wet season is usually October to February, with flooding and landslides common, which matters most on the winding highland roads. Cameron Highlands is noticeably cooler than the lowlands, so pack a light jacket.
description: The classic first-timer arc of peninsular Malaysia: Kuala Lumpur's towers, Hindu cave temple and street food, two nights in the tea hills of Cameron Highlands, then the Portuguese, Dutch and Peranakan history of Malacca on the way out.

days.title: Arrive Kuala Lumpur
activities: Arrive at Kuala Lumpur International Airport and transfer to the city
Settle in around Bukit Bintang or KLCC
Evening street food along Jalan Alor

days.title: Kuala Lumpur: towers + Batu Caves
activities: Batu Caves: the Lord Murugan statue and the stairs up to the Temple Cave, reached by KTM Komuter from KL Sentral (check the current Batu Caves line timetable at ktmb.com.my)

PETRONAS Twin Towers: the Skybridge and Observation Deck use time-ticketing, so book a slot on the official PETRONAS Twin Towers site in advance; official pages differ on which Mondays it is closed, so confirm before you go
Walk KLCC Park beneath the towers in the evening

days.title: Kuala Lumpur to Cameron Highlands
activities: Travel from Kuala Lumpur to Cameron Highlands, about 2 to 3 hours by road according to Tourism Malaysia; buses run from the TBS bus terminal in Kuala Lumpur to Tanah Rata
Check in around Tanah Rata, the main highland town
Evening stroll in Tanah Rata and a steamboat dinner

days.title: Cameron Highlands: tea + cloud forest
activities: Visit a tea plantation and its tea centre, such as BOH's Sungei Palas estate, for the tea terraces and a cup with a view; check the estate's current opening days before you go
Walk or drive up toward Gunung Brinchang and the Mossy Forest boardwalk; check current access rules at the entrance
Strawberry farms around Brinchang (check which are open when you visit)

days.title: Back to Kuala Lumpur
activities: Travel from Cameron Highlands back to Kuala Lumpur, about 2 to 3 hours by road (Tourism Malaysia); buses serve TBS
Afternoon in Chinatown (Petaling Street) and the Central Market area
Evening rooftop or tower views over the city

days.title: Kuala Lumpur to Malacca
activities: Take a bus from the TBS bus terminal to Melaka Sentral, about 3 hours according to Tourism Malaysia; check schedules on Easybook or Redbus, as Tourism Malaysia suggests
Afternoon at the Stadthuys, Christ Church and the A Famosa gateway at the foot of St Paul's Hill
Evening along the Malacca River; Jonker Street night market (check which nights it runs)
days.drive_time: Bus from TBS, about 3 hours (Tourism Malaysia)

days.title: Malacca + departure
activities: Baba & Nyonya Heritage Museum guided visit and Peranakan lunch (asam pedas, chicken rice balls)
Malacca River cruise
Return by bus to the TBS terminal in Kuala Lumpur, about 3 hours (Tourism Malaysia), for onward travel; leave time before an evening flight
days.drive_time: Bus to Kuala Lumpur, about 3 hours (Tourism Malaysia)

food_culture.name: Nasi lemak
food_culture.description: Rice cooked in coconut milk with sambal, fried anchovies, peanuts, cucumber and egg; widely eaten at breakfast across Kuala Lumpur and the rest of Malaysia.

food_culture.name: Chicken rice balls
food_culture.description: A Malacca specialty: Hainanese-style chicken served with rice pressed into golf-ball-sized rounds, a staple of the town's Chinese eateries around Jonker Street.

food_culture.name: Asam pedas
food_culture.description: A sour and spicy tamarind fish stew that is a signature of Malacca's Malay and Peranakan cooking.

food_culture.name: Teh tarik
food_culture.description: Strong black tea with condensed milk, 'pulled' between two vessels until frothy; found at every kopitiam and mamak stall.

food_culture.name: Highland tea
food_culture.description: Cameron Highlands is Malaysia's tea-growing hill region; estates such as BOH serve freshly brewed tea with views over the terraces.

food_culture.name: Baba-Nyonya (Peranakan) heritage
food_culture.description: Malacca is the heartland of the Peranakan Chinese, descendants of Chinese traders who married local Malays; their cuisine, beadwork and shophouse architecture are visible around Jonker Street.

food_culture.name: Thaipusam at Batu Caves
food_culture.description: Hindu festival honouring Lord Murugan, held in the Tamil month of Thai (usually January or February), when devotees climb the steps to the Batu Caves temple; the caves are far busier than usual on festival days.

title: Kuching, Bako + Mulu Caves, Sarawak, Borneo
best_time_description: Sarawak is rainy for much of the year; Australia's Smartraveller says flooding and landslides are common in the wet season, usually October to February. Mulu's park site says it can be visited year-round, mornings are usually clear and rain typically falls between 13:00 and 17:00, and June to September and holiday periods are busier so accommodation and guides must be booked. Heavy rain can cancel flights into Mulu, so leave a buffer day before an international departure.
description: A rainforest week in Malaysian Borneo: Kuching's riverfront and Sarawak food, proboscis monkeys and sea cliffs at Bako, semi-wild orangutans at Semenggoh, then a short flight to the limestone caves and canopy of Gunung Mulu National Park.

days.title: Arrive Kuching
activities: Arrive at Kuching International Airport. Sarawak and Sabah have their own entry pass issued on arrival (the German Foreign Office says it is usually valid 90 days), so keep your passport and MDAC confirmation handy
Evening on the Kuching Waterfront and the Main Bazaar old shophouses
Dinner of Sarawak laksa or kolo mee

days.title: Bako National Park
activities: Public bus No. 1 from central Kuching to Bako Market takes roughly 45 to 60 minutes according to tourism sources; minivans and taxis are faster

Register, buy the park ticket and a boat ticket at Bako Market, then take the boat of about 20 minutes to the park headquarters (park and jetty counter reported open 8:00 to 17:00 daily; confirm locally)
Walk a coastal trail for proboscis monkeys, bearded pigs and sea-stack views, then boat back and return to Kuching
days.drive_time: Bus about 45-60 min + boat about 20 min each way

days.title: Semenggoh + Kuching
activities: Visit Semenggoh Wildlife Centre in the morning to watch semi-wild orangutans at the feeding session; sightings are not guaranteed, and published feeding and counter hours differ between sources, so confirm the current schedule with Sarawak Forestry first
Afternoon in Kuching: the Main Bazaar, and a stroll along the waterfront
Sunset river view from the Waterfront

days.title: Fly Kuching to Mulu
activities: Fly Kuching to Mulu with MASwings (AirBorneo), about 1 hour 20 minutes per the official Mulu park site; Mulu has no road access and heavy rain can cancel flights
Buy the Mulu 5-day park pass (RM 30 for foreigners at the time of checking); book accommodation and guides ahead, as the park site says bookings are essential
Afternoon rain is typical from 13:00 to 17:00; use the evening for the rainforest boardwalks near Park HQ
days.drive_time: Flight about 1 hour 20 minutes (Mulu park site)

days.title: Mulu caves + canopy
activities: Guided visit to the show caves with a park guide, arranged at Park HQ; the cave and Canopy Skywalk visits are guided and subject to the day's conditions
Join the evening bat exodus viewing if it is running that day (confirm with the park)
Mornings are usually clear, so schedule the longest walks early

days.title: Fly Mulu to Kuching + departure
activities: Fly Mulu to Kuching, about 1 hour 20 minutes (confirm the timetable with AirBorneo)
Keep a buffer before any international flight: weather can delay Mulu flights
Last Sarawak layered cake (kek lapis) and souvenir shopping before departure
days.drive_time: Flight about 1 hour 20 minutes (Mulu park site)

food_culture.name: Sarawak laksa
food_culture.description: Rice vermicelli in a spiced paste and coconut-milk broth with prawns, chicken and omelette strips; considered a Kuching breakfast signature.

food_culture.name: Kolo mee
food_culture.description: Springy egg noodles tossed in a light pork or vegetable dressing with minced meat and char siu, a Kuching staple at kopitiams.

food_culture.name: Midin
food_culture.description: A wild jungle fern from Sarawak, typically stir-fried with garlic or belacan, found on menus in Kuching.

food_culture.name: Sarawak layer cake (kek lapis)
food_culture.description: Brightly patterned, intricately layered cakes that are a popular edible souvenir from Kuching.

food_culture.name: Gawai Dayak
food_culture.description: A harvest festival of the Iban and Bidayuh peoples, celebrated at the start of June and a public holiday in Sarawak; expect busy flights and closed shops around the date.

food_culture.name: Iban and Orang Ulu longhouse culture
food_culture.description: Sarawak's Indigenous communities traditionally live in longhouses, and their weaving, beadwork and music are presented at museums and cultural venues around Kuching.

title: Taipei, Jiufen + Sun Moon Lake, Taiwan
best_time_description: Late autumn to early winter (November to December) and spring (March to April) are the easier windows for city sightseeing plus a lake stay; October still falls in typhoon season, so keep flexibility and check forecasts.
description: Taipei's temples, night markets and museums, a day up in the old gold-mining hills at Jiufen and Jinguashi, then the high-speed train to Taichung and a two-night stay at Sun Moon Lake, Taiwan's largest lake. Every leg is by metro, bus or the THSR high-speed train.

days.title: Arrive Taipei
activities: Arrive at Taoyuan International Airport (TPE) and head into Taipei by the airport metro or an airport bus
Check in, then an easy first evening at a night market such as Shilin Night Market
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Taipei Main Station or Zhongshan

days.title: Old Taipei: Longshan Temple + Dihua Street
activities: Longshan Temple in Wanhua, one of Taipei's oldest temples, with morning worship under way
Dihua Street's old trading shops (dried goods, tea, textiles)
Taipei 101 observation deck in the late afternoon; buy tickets in advance for sunset slots
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Taipei Main Station or Zhongshan

days.title: National Palace Museum + Shilin
activities: National Palace Museum, home to the imperial collection brought from the mainland; allow most of the morning
Shilin Night Market for the evening, a short metro ride away
Check the museum's website for the opening day and any closure before you go
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Taipei Main Station or Zhongshan

days.title: Jiufen + Jinguashi
activities: From Exit 1 of MRT Zhongxiao Fuxing station take Keelung Bus 1061 or 1062 to Ruifang Train Station (per the Northeast and Yilan Coast National Scenic Area site; check the Keelung Bus timetable for departure times)
From Ruifang take the Gold Fulong Shuttle Bus 856 to Jiufen Old Street (stop 3 of its route), with teahouses and snack stalls
Continue on the 856 to Jinguashi (Gold Ecological Park), the former gold-mining site
Return to Taipei the same way in the evening
days.drive_time: Keelung Bus 1061/1062 Taipei to Ruifang, then Gold Fulong Shuttle Bus 856 to Jiufen and Jinguashi (operator timetables apply)

days.title: Taipei to Sun Moon Lake
activities: Take the THSR high-speed train from Taipei to Taichung: about 50 minutes on the fastest trains (for example train 203 leaves Taipei 06:30, arrives Taichung 07:20 in the timetable effective 2 February 2026)

At THSR Taichung Station take the escalator at Exit 5 to the first-floor bus terminal and board the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Sun Moon Lake route at Bus Platform 3 (check the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle site for the day's departures)
Afternoon walk at Shuishe, the lakeside shopping area, and sunset on the lake
days.drive_time: THSR about 50 min Taipei-Taichung, then the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle to Sun Moon Lake (official page gives no minutes; check the timetable). A direct Kuo-Kuang 1833 bus from Taipei is listed at approx. 4 hours
days.lodging_suggestion: Sun Moon Lake (Shuishe or Yuchi side)

days.title: Sun Moon Lake
activities: Xiangshan Visitor Center on the lake's southwest shore
Sun Moon Lake Wenwu Temple above the north shore
Sun Moon Lake Ropeway, or cycle part of the lakeside bikeway
Try the lake's black tea at a tea shop in Shuishe

days.title: Back to Taichung
activities: Take the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle from Sun Moon Lake back to THSR Taichung Station (confirm last departures on the day)
Miyahara in central Taichung, a dessert shop in a former eye hospital building
Rainbow Village, a small village repainted with murals by a former resident
Fengjia Night Market in the evening
days.drive_time: Taiwan Tourist Shuttle back to THSR Taichung (check the timetable)

days.title: Return to Taipei + departure
activities: THSR Taichung to Taipei in about 49 minutes on the fastest trains (for example train 204 leaves Taichung 07:48, arrives Taipei 08:37 in the timetable effective 2 February 2026)
Airport transfer for the flight home from Taoyuan (TPE)

food_culture.name: Beef noodle soup
food_culture.description: Taipei's best-known bowl: braised or stewed beef shank in a rich broth over wheat noodles, served at shops across the city and the subject of an annual local competition.

food_culture.name: Night markets
food_culture.description: Taiwan's evening street markets are a daily social ritual: stalls of grilled, fried and steamed snacks plus games. Shilin in Taipei and Fengjia in Taichung are two of the largest.

food_culture.name: Bubble tea
food_culture.description: Milk tea with tapioca pearls is a Taiwanese invention, and both Taichung and Tainan tea shops claim to have created it first. Order it sweetness-adjusted and iced from a street shop.

food_culture.name: Teahouse culture in Jiufen
food_culture.description: Jiufen's hillside teahouses serve oolong in the gongfu style with small cups; many are set in former mining-era buildings with sea views.

food_culture.name: Sun Moon Lake black tea
food_culture.description: The hills around Sun Moon Lake grow black tea, including the Assam-type leaf sold across Shuishe; tasting rooms and tea farms offer cups and packs.

food_culture.name: Thao people of Sun Moon Lake
food_culture.description: The lake is the homeland of the Thao, one of Taiwan's recognised Indigenous peoples, whose culture appears in local crafts, food and festivals around Ita Thao village.

title: Tainan, Kaohsiung + Alishan, Taiwan
best_time_description: November to April is cooler and drier in the south, which suits long days of walking in Tainan and Kaohsiung; Alishan is much cooler than the plains year-round, so pack layers. Summer brings heat and typhoon risk.
description: Taiwan's old southern capital, Tainan, then the harbour city of Kaohsiung, and up into the mountain forests of Alishan, all linked by the THSR high-speed train. A slower, food-led route that is easy to combine with Itinerary 1 for a longer stay.

days.title: Arrive Taipei to Tainan
activities: Arrive at Taoyuan International Airport (TPE) and reach THSR Taoyuan or Taipei station

THSR south to Tainan in about 1 hour 27 minutes on the fastest trains (for example train 205 leaves Taipei 07:51, arrives Tainan 09:18 in the timetable effective 2 February 2026); other trains take about 1 hour 33 minutes
THSR Tainan Station is outside the old city, so allow time for the onward bus or local train into central Tainan
Evening street-food walk

days.title: Old Tainan: temples + forts
activities: Chihkan Tower (Fort Provintia), a Dutch-era site later rebuilt
Tainan Confucius Temple, the oldest Confucian temple in Taiwan
Shennong Street's old shophouses, lively in the evening
Check opening days of museums and monuments the day before

days.title: Anping + Tainan food
activities: Anping Fort (Fort Zeelandia), the 17th-century Dutch fort
Anping Old Street and the Anping Tree House, a warehouse overrun by banyan roots
Dinner on Tainan snacks such as danzai noodles and milkfish

days.title: Tainan to Kaohsiung
activities: Morning in Tainan, then THSR from Tainan to Zuoying: 12 minutes (Tainan 08:03 to Zuoying 08:15 on train 203, for example)
