MRT from Zuoying into central Kaohsiung
Pier-2 Art Center on the harbour, then the Lotus Pond with the Dragon and Tiger Pagodas
Liuhe Night Market for dinner
days.lodging_suggestion: Kaohsiung, near Formosa Boulevard or Pier-2

days.title: Kaohsiung to Chiayi
activities: Optional morning at Fo Guang Shan Buddha Memorial Center, a large Buddhist monastery complex outside the city (check its opening times and getting there)
THSR from Zuoying to Chiayi: about 32 minutes on the fastest trains (for example train 1202 leaves Zuoying 06:25, arrives Chiayi 06:57; train 802 takes 33 minutes)
Chiayi city: Chiayi Hinoki Village and the Wenhua Road night market
Reserve Alishan transport and any Alishan Forest Railway tickets before arriving (online booking at afrts.forest.gov.tw)

days.title: Chiayi to Alishan
activities: From THSR Chiayi Station take the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Alishan route (the Alishan National Scenic Area site names routes 7329 and 7329A via Fenqihu); Chiayi County Bus 7322 also runs Chiayi to Alishan. Check current timetables, since the official page gives no minutes

Optional: the Alishan Forest Railway Main Line from Chiayi, which its site lists as operating normally; the timetable applicable from 10 January 2025 shows the 10:00 train arriving at Alishan at 14:56 (4 h 56 min), so check the current timetable and reserve
Walk the Alishan National Forest Recreation Area's giant-tree trails in the late afternoon; pack layers, it is much cooler than the plains
days.drive_time: Taiwan Tourist Shuttle 7329 or Chiayi County Bus 7322; Forest Railway 4 h 56 min on the 10:00 train per the January 2025 timetable

days.title: Alishan sunrise to Taipei
activities: Early-morning sunrise viewing; the Zhushan line sunrise train is booked through afrts.forest.gov.tw, and its departure time varies by day, so check the notice on the Forest Railway site
Descend to Chiayi by bus (check the timetable)

THSR Chiayi to Taipei in about 1 hour 28 minutes on the fastest trains (for example train 1302 leaves Chiayi 07:19, arrives Taipei 08:47; train 606 takes 1 h 30 min); the Alishan site gives approx. 1.5 hours between Taipei and Chiayi THSR
Evening in Taipei at a night market

days.title: Departure
activities: Airport transfer from Taipei to Taoyuan International Airport (TPE) for the flight home
Pack extra time if the previous day ran late

food_culture.name: Danzai noodles
food_culture.description: Tainan's signature small bowl: wheat noodles in a shrimp-and-pork broth topped with minced pork and a shrimp, traditionally eaten as a snack between meals.

food_culture.name: Milkfish soup
food_culture.description: Milkfish is farmed in the coastal ponds near Tainan, and the fish is served as a clear breakfast soup, often with ginger and sometimes with the belly or fish balls.

food_culture.name: Chiayi turkey rice
food_culture.description: Chiayi's emblem dish: shredded turkey meat over rice with a savory sauce and fried shallots, found at roadside shops and the Wenhua Road night market.

food_culture.name: Alishan high-mountain oolong
food_culture.description: Tea is grown at high elevation around Alishan, and the cool, misty conditions are associated with sweet, floral oolongs sold in tea shops in the village.

food_culture.name: Temple culture in Tainan
food_culture.description: Tainan has some of Taiwan's oldest Taoist and Buddhist temples, many dedicated to the sea goddess Mazu; incense and offerings are part of daily life and are respected by visitors.

food_culture.name: Kaohsiung harbour arts
food_culture.description: The old harbour warehouses at Pier-2 now host art installations, galleries and design shops, showing the port city's shift from shipping to culture.

food_culture.name: Alishan Forest Railway heritage
food_culture.description: The narrow-gauge railway was built to haul timber from the Alishan forests and is now a heritage line, run by the Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office.

title: Delhi, Agra, Jaipur + Rajasthan's Lake and Fort Cities, India
best_time_description: October to March is the cooler, drier window for Delhi, Agra and Rajasthan, which is when the Golden Triangle and the desert forts are comfortable to walk; April to June is very hot in all five cities.
description: India's classic first-timer circuit (Delhi, Agra's Taj Mahal, pink Jaipur) extended through holy Pushkar and blue-walled Jodhpur to lake-side Udaipur, with a nonstop flight back to Delhi at the end.

days.title: Arrive Delhi
activities: Arrive at Indira Gandhi International Airport and transfer to your hotel
Easy evening walk around Connaught Place or Hauz Khas, and an early night to recover from the flight

days.title: Old and New Delhi
activities: Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Old Delhi (check the Red Fort's weekly closing day before you go)
Chandni Chowk food walk including the parathas of Paranthe Wali Gali
Humayun's Tomb and Qutb Minar in the afternoon

days.title: Delhi to Agra by Gatimaan Express
activities: Gatimaan Express from Hazrat Nizamuddin at 08:10, reaching Agra Cantt about 09:50 (about 1 hour 40 minutes; listings show it does not run on Fridays, so check the day you travel)

Taj Mahal in the afternoon: open from about half an hour before sunrise to half an hour before sunset and closed on Fridays; buy tickets on the ASI site (asi.payumoney.com) or at the window; no tripods without ASI permission, no drones, no food inside
Mehtab Bagh or the Yamuna riverfront for sunset views back across to the Taj
days.drive_time: Gatimaan Express, about 1 hr 40 min (Nizamuddin to Agra Cantt, 188 km)

days.title: Agra Fort and on to Jaipur
activities: Agra Fort in the morning
Stop at Fatehpur Sikri on the road to Jaipur, the Mughal capital abandoned in the 16th century
Continue by road to Jaipur: Rajasthan Tourism lists Jaipur to Agra as 250 km, about 5 hours

days.title: Pink City of Jaipur
activities: Amber Fort on its hilltop above the town
City Palace and the Jantar Mantar observatory
Hawa Mahal facade and an evening of bazaar shopping for block prints and jewellery

days.title: Jaipur to Pushkar
activities: Drive to Pushkar: Rajasthan Tourism lists Jaipur to Pushkar as 140 km, about 3 hours
Walk the ghats of the sacred Pushkar Lake and visit the Brahma Temple
Sunset over the lake and the old-town bazaar

days.title: Pushkar to Jodhpur
activities: Drive to Jodhpur via Nimaj: Rajasthan Tourism lists Pushkar to Jodhpur via Nimaj as 190 km, about 4 hours
Mehrangarh Fort above the city
Evening wander in the Sardar Market near the Clock Tower
days.drive_time: Road via Nimaj, about 190 km / 4 hrs (Rajasthan Tourism)

days.title: Jodhpur to Udaipur
activities: Morning at the blue-washed old city streets below the fort
Drive to Udaipur: Rajasthan Tourism lists Jodhpur to Udaipur as 260 km, about 5 hours
Sunset boat or lakeside walk on Lake Pichola

days.title: Udaipur
activities: City Palace complex on the shore of Lake Pichola
Jagdish Temple and a walk through the old town lanes
Evening cultural dance show or rooftop dinner facing the lake

days.title: Fly Udaipur to Delhi
activities: Nonstop flight from Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur) to Delhi: IndiGo and Air India list direct flights of about 1 hour 15 to 20 minutes (check the current timetable with the airline)
Connect to your international flight home; leave a buffer for the transfer if you hold separate tickets

food_culture.name: Paranthe Wali Gali parathas
food_culture.description: Old Delhi's Chandni Chowk lane of stuffed fried flatbreads, eaten with pickles and chutneys, is the traditional first meal for a Delhi food walk.

food_culture.name: Agra petha
food_culture.description: A translucent sweet made from ash gourd and sugar syrup, sold across Agra and the classic thing to carry away from the Taj.

food_culture.name: Dal baati churma
food_culture.description: Rajasthan's signature meal: baked wheat balls (baati) with lentils (dal) and a sweet crumbled wheat dish (churma), found across Jaipur and Udaipur.

food_culture.name: Laal maas
food_culture.description: A fiery Rajasthani mutton curry coloured and heated with Mathania red chillies, associated with Marwari and Rajput kitchens and common in Jodhpur.

food_culture.name: Mirchi bada and pyaaz kachori
food_culture.description: Jodhpur's street snacks: a large green chilli stuffed with spiced potato and fried in gram-flour batter, and the onion kachori, both best eaten fresh from the stall.

food_culture.name: Masala chai and lassi
food_culture.description: Milky spiced tea served in small clay or glass cups at roadside stalls, and thick curd lassi in terracotta, are everyday drinks across the whole north Indian route.

food_culture.name: Pushkar Lake ghats
food_culture.description: Pushkar is a Hindu pilgrimage town around a sacred lake with ghats where visitors are asked to remove shoes and follow priests' guidance; be wary of anyone who pressures you into a paid offering.

food_culture.name: Mughal architecture and pietra dura
food_culture.description: The Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri show Mughal inlay, marble and red-sandstone building; the Taj's custodian is the Archaeological Survey of India.

food_culture.name: Rajput forts and palaces
food_culture.description: Amber, Mehrangarh and the Udaipur City Palace are royal Rajput residences built on hills and lakes; many are now museums, with hotel wings in some palaces.

title: Kerala Backwaters + Tamil Nadu Temple Towns, India
best_time_description: November to February is the cooler, drier window for Kerala's backwaters and the Tamil Nadu plains; the monsoon (June to September in Kerala) brings heavy rain, which also is when Alappuzha's snake-boat racing season runs.
description: Fly into Kochi, cruise the backwaters of Alappuzha, climb into the tea and spice hills of Periyar at Thekkady, then cross into Tamil Nadu for the Meenakshi temple in Madurai and the Chola-era Brihadisvara temple in Thanjavur.

days.title: Arrive Kochi
activities: Arrive at Cochin International Airport and transfer into Fort Kochi (Kerala Tourism lists Cochin airport about 85 km from Alappuzha town; allow time for the airport transfer)
Evening walk along the Chinese fishing nets and the Fort Kochi waterfront

days.title: Fort Kochi and Mattancherry
activities: Mattancherry Palace and Jew Town's antique and spice shops
St. Francis Church and Santa Cruz Basilica
Evening Kathakali dance performance (book a seat in advance)

days.title: Kochi to Alappuzha backwaters
activities: Kerala Tourism lists Fort Kochi at 53 km from Alappuzha; go by road or take the Alappuzha-Kochi backwater cruise listed by Kerala Tourism, or a train from Ernakulam Junction to Alappuzha (about 1 hour 10 minutes to 1 hour 40 minutes depending on the train)
Overnight houseboat cruise through the Kuttanad canals, or a day cruise with a lakeside stay
Village walk and a Kerala fish-and-rice meal on board or at a homestay
days.drive_time: Road/train, about 53 km; train 1 hr 10 min to 1 hr 40 min

days.title: Alappuzha to Thekkady
activities: Road to Thekkady: Kerala Tourism lists Alappuzha at 164 km, about 5 hours, from Thekkady
Spice plantation visit in Kumily on arrival
Optional evening cultural show or an ayurvedic massage

days.title: Periyar Tiger Reserve
activities: Early boat trip or guided nature walk in Periyar Tiger Reserve; book through the forest department and check the current ticket and trek rules in advance
Spice or tea estate visit near Thekkady
Free afternoon in Kumily's spice market

days.title: Thekkady to Madurai
activities: Cross into Tamil Nadu by road: Kerala Tourism lists Madurai about 140 km from the Periyar sanctuary
Afternoon at the Meenakshi Amman Temple complex, one of India's largest temples, with 14 gopurams of 45 to 50 m (check the temple's current dress and phone rules)
Evening temple lanes and late-night food streets

days.title: Madurai to Thanjavur
activities: Morning at Thirumalai Nayak Palace and the Teppakulam tank
Bus or car to Thanjavur: about 3 to 4.5 hours depending on stops and vehicle
Brihadisvara (Big Temple), the 11th-century Chola temple and UNESCO World Heritage site, and Thanjavur Palace in the late afternoon
days.drive_time: Bus or car, about 3 to 4.5 hrs

days.title: Thanjavur and departure
activities: Thanjavur Art Gallery and the town's Thanjavur painting craft shops
Depart through Tiruchirappalli International Airport, which Incredible India lists as one of Thanjavur's two nearest airports, or go on to Chennai (about 350 km from Thanjavur, per Incredible India)

food_culture.name: Kerala sadya
food_culture.description: A vegetarian feast served on a banana leaf with rice, sambar, avial, thoran, pickles and payasam, central to Onam and available at restaurants through the year.

food_culture.name: Karimeen pollichathu
food_culture.description: Pearl spot fish marinated in spices, wrapped in banana leaf and pan-fried, a dish served at backwater homestays around Alappuzha.

food_culture.name: Appam with stew
food_culture.description: Lacy fermented rice pancakes with a mild coconut milk vegetable or meat stew, a standard Kerala breakfast.

food_culture.name: Ashoka halwa
food_culture.description: A wheat and ghee sweet from the Thanjavur region, named in Incredible India's Thanjavur food trail.

food_culture.name: Jigarthanda
food_culture.description: Madurai's cold milk, almond-gum and ice cream drink, sold at dedicated shops in the city.

food_culture.name: Alappuzha snake-boat races
food_culture.description: Long snake boats with large crews race on Alappuzha's backwaters in the monsoon season; check the year's race calendar if you want to see one.

food_culture.name: Kathakali
food_culture.description: Kerala's classical dance-drama with elaborate face-painted makeup and costumes, performed for visitors at venues in Fort Kochi.

food_culture.name: Great Living Chola Temples
food_culture.description: Thanjavur's Brihadisvara Temple, built by Rajaraja Chola I in the 11th century and dedicated to Shiva, is a UNESCO World Heritage site with one of India's largest Nandi statues carved from a single granite rock.

food_culture.name: Thanjavur painting
food_culture.description: A local panel-painting craft associated with the Thanjavur region and shown at the town's art gallery.

title: Beijing, Xi'an + Shanghai by High-Speed Rail, China
best_time_description: Spring (April to May) and autumn (September to October) are the comfortable windows for walking the Forbidden City, the Great Wall and Xi'an's city wall; summer is hot and humid in Shanghai and Xi'an, and winter is cold in Beijing and Xi'an. Public-holiday weeks (around 1 October and Chinese New Year) are extremely crowded and trains and timed tickets sell out first.
description: China's classic first-timer arc: Beijing's imperial palaces and the Great Wall, the Terracotta Warriors and walled city of Xi'an, and Shanghai's river skyline, linked by China Railway high-speed G-trains. Several headline sights need a real-name, passport-based reservation, so book them before you land.

days.title: Arrive Beijing
activities: Arrive at Beijing Capital or Daxing airport and transfer to the Dongcheng hutong area
Complete China's arrival card online before travel (NIA website, NIA 12367 app or WeChat/Alipay mini-program) or at the immigration hall by QR code, kiosk or paper card
Evening stroll through the Nanluoguxiang and Shichahai hutong lanes

days.title: Forbidden City + Jingshan Park
activities: The Palace Museum (Forbidden City): tickets must be reserved in advance on the museum's official website or WeChat mini-program; foreign visitors can book with a passport on the English site (intl.dpm.org.cn); no same-day tickets; closed Mondays except statutory holidays; bring the passport used for the booking to the Meridian Gate
Walk the central axis from the Meridian Gate to the Gate of Divine Might
Jingshan Park hill for the view back over the palace roofs

days.title: Mutianyu Great Wall
activities: Mutianyu Great Wall: real-name online reservation is required through the official Mutianyu ticketing site (passport details; one ticket per ID per day); foreign visitors can enter with the original reservation and passport
Walk the restored watchtower sections along the ridge; check the official site for the cable car and what is running that day
Return to Beijing for a Peking duck dinner

days.title: Temple of Heaven, then train to Xi'an
activities: Temple of Heaven park and the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests; check the official channels for whether a timed ticket is needed on your date

Afternoon China Railway G-train from Beijing to Xi'an (arrives at Xi'an North or Xi'an East); journey time not verified from an official source here, so read it off the live 12306 timetable when you book
Dinner on Beiyuanmen street in the Muslim Quarter
days.lodging_suggestion: Near the Xi'an Bell Tower inside the city wall

days.title: Terracotta Warriors
activities: Museum of the Qin Terracotta Army: real-name online reservation is required for all visitors including foreigners, through the museum's official website or WeChat accounts, with an English platform for overseas visitors; bring the passport used for booking
Pits 1, 2 and 3 and the bronze chariot exhibition
Evening on the Bell and Drum Towers square
days.lodging_suggestion: Near the Xi'an Bell Tower inside the city wall

days.title: Xi'an city wall + museums
activities: Walk or cycle the top of the Xi'an city wall
Shaanxi History Museum (check its official channels for reservation rules and closing days before you go)
Big Wild Goose Pagoda in the evening
days.lodging_suggestion: Near the Xi'an Bell Tower inside the city wall

days.title: Train to Shanghai
activities: G-train from Xi'an (Xi'an North or Xi'an East) to Shanghai Hongqiao; journey time not verified from an official source here, so read it off the live 12306 timetable and allow most of the day
Evening walk on the Bund
days.lodging_suggestion: Near People's Square or the former French Concession

days.title: Shanghai highlights
activities: Yu Garden and the old city bazaar
Former French Concession streets
Pudong skyline from the Bund waterfront at night
days.lodging_suggestion: Near People's Square or the former French Concession

days.title: Depart Shanghai
activities: Transfer to Pudong or Hongqiao airport for your flight out

food_culture.name: Peking duck
food_culture.description: Beijing's signature roast duck, carved at the table and eaten in thin pancakes with sweet bean sauce, spring onion and cucumber; the dish is tied to the capital's imperial-era kitchens.

food_culture.name: Biangbiang noodles and roujiamo
food_culture.description: Xi'an's wide hand-pulled noodles with chilli oil and vinegar, and roujiamo, a flatbread stuffed with chopped braised meat, are staples of Shaanxi wheat-based cooking.

food_culture.name: Xiaolongbao
food_culture.description: Shanghai-area soup dumplings with a thin wrapper and a pocket of broth; eat them by nibbling the skin and sipping the soup first.

food_culture.name: Hutong courtyard life
food_culture.description: Beijing's hutong are narrow lanes lined with traditional courtyard homes, many near the Forbidden City, and remain living neighbourhoods with small shops, tea houses and cafes.

food_culture.name: Xi'an's Hui Muslim Quarter
food_culture.description: Around the Great Mosque, Xi'an's Hui community has lived for centuries and its street food, from lamb skewers to persimmon cakes, reflects Silk Road trading heritage.

food_culture.name: Chinese tea culture
food_culture.description: Tea houses across all three cities serve green, jasmine and oolong teas; ordering a pot and sitting is a normal way to rest between sights.

title: Chengdu, Chongqing + Zhangjiajie, China
best_time_description: April to May and September to October bring the mildest weather and clearer views in the Zhangjiajie mountains; Chengdu and Chongqing are hot and humid in summer, and Chongqing, Sichuan and Hunan are often overcast in winter. Avoid the first week of October and Chinese New Year, when the parks and trains are packed.
description: A south-west China loop for food, pandas and mountains: Chengdu's teahouses and giant pandas, Chongqing's hillside river city, then the sandstone pillars of Wulingyuan at Zhangjiajie, linked by high-speed rail. Chongqing East to Zhangjiajie West takes about two hours on the fastest train.

days.title: Arrive Chengdu
activities: Arrive at Chengdu Tianfu or Shuangliu airport and transfer to the city centre
Complete China's arrival card online before travel (NIA website, NIA 12367 app or WeChat/Alipay mini-program) or at the immigration hall by QR code, kiosk or paper card
Evening walk around Kuanzhai Alley
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Chunxi Road or Kuanzhai Alley

days.title: Giant pandas + teahouse
activities: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding: book tickets through its official channels in advance and go early in the day
Afternoon tea at a teahouse in People's Park
Evening Sichuan hotpot or a Sichuan opera show
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Chunxi Road or Kuanzhai Alley

days.title: Dujiangyan + Mount Qingcheng
activities: Dujiangyan Irrigation System, the UNESCO-listed water-control works begun in the 3rd century BC
Mount Qingcheng, a Taoist mountain and UNESCO site, for temples and forest paths
Return to Chengdu for the evening
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Chunxi Road or Kuanzhai Alley

days.title: Train to Chongqing
activities: G-train Chengdu to Chongqing; the fastest Fuxing service is reported at about 62 minutes (CGTN, December 2020), so check the train you book on 12306 for its actual time and Chongqing station
Evening at Hongya Cave and the Jiefangbei district
Night views of the Jialing and Yangtze rivers

days.title: Chongqing city
activities: Liziba station, where the Line 2 monorail runs through a residential building
Ciqikou Ancient Town
Chongqing hotpot for dinner

days.title: Train to Zhangjiajie
activities: G-train from Chongqing East to Zhangjiajie West: the fastest run is 2 hours 2 minutes (Hunan Today, April 2026); other trains are slower, so choose the Chongqing East departure when booking on 12306
Transfer to the Wulingyuan area
Evening walk in Wulingyuan town
days.lodging_suggestion: Wulingyuan, near the Zhangjiajie National Forest Park entrance

days.title: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
activities: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in the Wulingyuan UNESCO site: the sandstone pillar area including the Hallelujah Mountains
Check the park's official ticketing for entry rules and whether advance booking is needed on your date
Bring your passport in case it is needed for ticket or ID checks
days.lodging_suggestion: Wulingyuan, near the Zhangjiajie National Forest Park entrance

days.title: Tianmen Mountain
activities: Tianmen Mountain National Forest Park by cable car, the cliff-edge walkway and the 99-bend road
Check the official ticketing for any reservation requirement and weather closures before you go
Evening in Zhangjiajie city

days.title: Depart Zhangjiajie
activities: Transfer to Zhangjiajie Hehua airport or Zhangjiajie West station for onward travel

food_culture.name: Sichuan hotpot
food_culture.description: Chengdu and Chongqing both claim the numbing-and-spicy hotpot, simmered in a broth of chilli and Sichuan pepper; Chongqing's version is known for beef tallow in the broth.

food_culture.name: Mapo tofu and dan dan noodles
food_culture.description: Classic Sichuan dishes built on doubanjiang chilli bean paste and Sichuan pepper, found across Chengdu from street stalls to formal restaurants.

food_culture.name: Xiangxi smoked pork and sour fish
food_culture.description: Zhangjiajie sits in the Tujia and Miao region of western Hunan, where cured, smoked pork and hot-and-sour dishes are everyday cooking.

food_culture.name: Chengdu teahouse culture
food_culture.description: Chengdu's teahouses, with bamboo chairs and covered bowls of jasmine tea, are meeting places where people sit for hours; People's Park is the best known.

food_culture.name: Sichuan opera face-changing
food_culture.description: Sichuan opera is known for bianlian, the rapid change of painted masks on stage, shown in Chengdu theatres and teahouses.

food_culture.name: Tujia and Miao heritage
food_culture.description: Western Hunan around Zhangjiajie is home to the Tujia and Miao peoples, whose song, dress and stilted-house traditions are presented in the Wulingyuan area.

title: Kathmandu, Pokhara + Chitwan, Nepal
best_time_description: October and November (after the monsoon) and February and March are the comfortable windows for city sightseeing, Pokhara's mountain views and the Chitwan lowlands. The monsoon runs June to September, when flooding and landslides can block roads and disrupt flights (Global Affairs Canada). Nepal Tourism Board lists March to May and September to November as the best season for the Annapurna region that Pokhara looks onto. Chitwan is sub-tropical, hot and humid in summer with mild winters (Nepal Tourism Board).
description: Nepal's classic first-timer arc without a single day of trekking: the Newar temple squares and stupas of Kathmandu, a lakeside break in Pokhara under the Annapurna range, then Chitwan National Park in the Terai lowlands for jungle walks, canoes and Tharu culture. Every leg between cities is a short domestic flight on Buddha Air, so the days go to sightseeing instead of the road.

days.title: Arrive Kathmandu
activities: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Nepal's only international airport. Most nationalities buy a tourist visa on arrival at the counters (15 days USD 30, 30 days USD 50, 90 days USD 125 per the Department of Immigration); Indian citizens need no visa and show a passport or Voter ID. Have a machine-readable passport.
Transfer to Thamel, the main visitor district, and walk its lanes
Early night: tomorrow starts with a full day of temple squares
days.drive_time: Airport to Thamel by taxi or pre-booked hotel pickup, arranged on arrival (no fixed time verified)

days.title: Kathmandu Durbar Square and Swayambhu
activities: Kathmandu Durbar Square (the fee includes the Tribhuvan Museum; Nepal Tourism Board lists NPR 1,000 for foreign nationals, free under 10)
Swayambhu Stupa on its hilltop, the temple known to visitors as the Monkey Temple (Nepal Tourism Board lists NPR 200 for foreign nationals)
Evening in Thamel for a first Nepali meal
days.drive_time: Thamel to Durbar Square and on to Swayambhu by taxi or on foot; Swayambhu is on the western edge of the city

days.title: Pashupatinath, Boudhanath and Patan
activities: Pashupatinath Temple on the Bagmati River; Nepal Tourism Board lists NPR 1,000 per day per entry for foreign nationals and notes that tourists can view the temple from the back premises
Boudha Stupa (Boudhanath), one of the large stupas of the valley (Nepal Tourism Board lists NPR 400 for foreign nationals, free under 10)
Afternoon at Patan Durbar Square including the Patan Museum (Nepal Tourism Board lists NPR 1,000 for foreign nationals)
days.drive_time: Taxi between sites; all three are inside the Kathmandu Valley

days.title: Fly to Pokhara
activities: Buddha Air flight Kathmandu to Pokhara, 25 minutes, more than 17 flights a day per Buddha Air's route page. Flights can be delayed or cancelled by weather; Global Affairs Canada notes the June to September monsoon can disrupt flights and flood or block roads, and mountain weather can change suddenly. Buddha Air's route pages say schedules are subject to change, so check the flight status page.
Walk Lakeside, Pokhara's waterfront strip on Phewa Lake

Rent a rowing boat on Phewa Lake in the late afternoon for the Machhapuchhre ('Fish Tail') peak reflected in the water, which Nepal Tourism Board says many visitors find their most lasting impression of Nepal
days.drive_time: Flight, 25 minutes (Buddha Air); allow time for airport transfers either end

days.title: Sarangkot sunrise and Pokhara sights
activities: Sunrise from the Sarangkot view tower, 11.3 km from Lakeside, a maximum 30 minutes by road according to Nepal Tourism Board; views run from Dhaulagiri to Machhapuchhre and Annapurna II
World Peace Pagoda above Phewa Lake
Davis Falls and Gupteshwar Cave, Mahendra Cave and the Old Bazaar with Bindyabasini temple (all listed by Nepal Tourism Board as places to see in Pokhara)
Optional: tandem paragliding from Sarangkot (Nepal Tourism Board lists it as a major activity; book through a licensed operator)
days.drive_time: Lakeside to Sarangkot, up to 30 minutes by road (Nepal Tourism Board)

days.title: Fly to Bharatpur and Chitwan
activities: Buddha Air flight Pokhara to Bharatpur, 20 minutes. Buddha Air runs one flight a day on this route, so book ahead and keep the time flexible; Buddha Air also says Chitwan National Park is about a 30-minute drive from Bharatpur Airport. If it is cancelled, tourist buses also serve Pokhara and Chitwan (Nepal Tourism Board) but published journey times vary widely, so confirm departure and duration with the operator. Flights can be delayed or cancelled by weather; Global Affairs Canada notes the June to September monsoon can disrupt flights and flood or block roads, and mountain weather can change suddenly. Buddha Air's route pages say schedules are subject to change, so check the flight status page.
Transfer to a lodge near the park (the park headquarters at Kasara is 21 km from Bharatpur per Nepal Tourism Board; resorts are outside the park)
Evening Tharu cultural programme with the stick dance, which Nepal Tourism Board describes for Chitwan
days.drive_time: Flight 20 minutes, then about 30 minutes by road from Bharatpur Airport to the Chitwan National Park area (Buddha Air)
days.lodging_suggestion: Sauraha or another lodge outside Chitwan National Park

days.title: Chitwan National Park
activities: Park entry permit, paid at the Tourist Service Center in Kathmandu or at the park entry point: NPR 2,000 per person per entry for foreigners, free under 10 (Nepal Tourism Board). A news report dated 24 May 2026 (Onlinekhabar) puts the jeep fee at NPR 5,000 per vehicle; confirm at the gate.

Morning jeep safari or guided jungle walk, with canoe and bird-watching options; Nepal Tourism Board describes tigers, leopards and rhinos in the park and gharial and marsh mugger crocodiles along the rivers
Visit the Elephant Breeding Camp and the Tharu Cultural Museum (both on Nepal Tourism Board's Chitwan fee list) and a Tharu village
days.drive_time: Local transfers between the lodge, park entrance and Kasara headquarters (21 km from Bharatpur per Nepal Tourism Board)
days.lodging_suggestion: Sauraha or another lodge outside Chitwan National Park

days.title: Fly to Kathmandu and depart
activities: Buddha Air flight Bharatpur to Kathmandu, 25 minutes; Buddha Air lists 9 daily flights on this route. Book a morning flight and leave a long buffer before any international departure, since weather delays are possible. Flights can be delayed or cancelled by weather; Global Affairs Canada notes the June to September monsoon can disrupt flights and flood or block roads, and mountain weather can change suddenly. Buddha Air's route pages say schedules are subject to change, so check the flight status page.
Spare time in Kathmandu for last shopping in Thamel, or a late international flight home
days.drive_time: Flight, 25 minutes (Buddha Air), plus about 30 minutes by road from the lodge area to Bharatpur Airport
days.lodging_suggestion: Kathmandu near the airport if departing next morning

food_culture.name: Dal bhat
food_culture.description: Lentil soup with rice and vegetable curries, the everyday Nepali meal, served in Kathmandu restaurants, Pokhara lodges and the lodges around Chitwan.

food_culture.name: Momo
food_culture.description: Steamed or fried dumplings found across Kathmandu and Pokhara, a standard order for a first Nepali meal around Thamel and Lakeside.

food_culture.name: Newar temple squares of the Kathmandu Valley
food_culture.description: Nepal Tourism Board describes Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur as ancient cities once ruled by the Malla kings, with seven shrines listed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the Newars as the valley's original inhabitants whose craft skills built them.

food_culture.name: Pashupatinath on the Bagmati
food_culture.description: A major Hindu temple on the Bagmati River where, per Nepal Tourism Board, tourists can view the temple from the back premises rather than entering the main shrine.

food_culture.name: Tharu stick dance
food_culture.description: Nepal Tourism Board describes ending a Chitwan day by a campfire watching the Tharu stick dance and listening to Tharu folk songs; the Tharu are the indigenous people of the Terai who built the traditional mud houses visitors can enter.

food_culture.name: Gurung and Magar Pokhara
food_culture.description: Nepal Tourism Board says Gurungs and Magars predominate around Pokhara, known worldwide as Gurkha soldiers, and that Thakalis run many of the tea houses along Annapurna trails.

title: Poon Hill + Annapurna Foothills Trek, Nepal
best_time_description: Nepal Tourism Board lists March to May and September to November as the best season for the Annapurna region. Early spring (March, April) and the post-monsoon weeks of October and November are the usual windows for clear sunrise views from Poon Hill; Nepal Tourism Board describes the Ghorepani Poon Hill trek as one of the most popular short treks in Nepal, suitable for beginners and families. June to September is monsoon, with flooding and landslides that can block hill roads and disrupt flights (Global Affairs Canada).
description: A lower-altitude teahouse trek through the Annapurna Conservation Area: two days in Kathmandu and a day in Pokhara to set up permits, then Nayapul to Ghorepani for sunrise from Poon Hill (3,210 m), down through Tadapani to the Gurung village of Ghandruk. The highest point is Poon Hill, so this is the gentler end of Nepal trekking, but it still crosses the 2,500 m line where altitude sickness guidance applies.

days.title: Arrive Kathmandu
activities: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport. Most nationalities buy a tourist visa on arrival (15 days USD 30, 30 days USD 50, 90 days USD 125 per the Department of Immigration); Indian citizens need no visa and show a passport or Voter ID. Choose a visa length that covers the whole trip, including any buffer days.
Transfer to Thamel and confirm your trek booking with a government-registered trekking agency (Nepal Tourism Board says to use one for guide and TIMS card)
Buy any missing gear in Thamel
days.drive_time: Airport to Thamel by taxi or hotel pickup, arranged on arrival (no fixed time verified)

days.title: Bhaktapur and Changunarayan
activities: Bhaktapur Durbar Square (Nepal Tourism Board lists US$ 18 or NPR 1,800 for foreign nationals, free under 10); the National Art Museum there is closed on Tuesdays
Changunarayan Temple (Nepal Tourism Board lists NPR 300 for foreign nationals)
Back in Thamel, pack a small daypack for the trek and leave the rest at your hotel
days.drive_time: Taxi or hired car across the Kathmandu Valley; confirm travel time locally as traffic varies

days.title: Fly to Pokhara and sort permits
activities: Buddha Air flight Kathmandu to Pokhara, 25 minutes. Flights can be delayed or cancelled by weather; Global Affairs Canada notes the June to September monsoon can disrupt flights and flood or block roads, and mountain weather can change suddenly. Buddha Air's route pages say schedules are subject to change, so check the flight status page.

Annapurna Conservation Area entry permit: NPR 3,000 for foreigners per Nepal Tourism Board's park fee page and the NTNC ePermit portal (online payment adds a 2.9% gateway charge; permits issued at check-posts cost double). Carry it for the whole trek. The Nepal Tourism Board Annapurna page still shows NPR 2,000; the NTNC portal is the current figure.

TIMS card: Nepal Tourism Board says that since 31 March 2023 trekking guide plus an agency-issued TIMS card is mandatory on listed routes, including the Poon Hill-ABC trek, at NPR 2,000 for non-SAARC visitors. The page does not name the short Ghorepani Poon Hill loop on its own, so book a licensed guide and TIMS through your agency to be safe.
Evening boat on Phewa Lake

days.title: Pokhara to Nayapul, trek to Tikhedhunga
activities: Road transfer from Pokhara to the Nayapul trailhead arranged by your agency (operator pages quote about 1.5 hours; confirm with your agency)
Start walking from Nayapul toward Tikhedhunga, the first overnight stop; the route and village order follow the Government of Nepal's own outline of the Poon Hill trek
Overnight in a teahouse; dal bhat is the standard trail meal
days.drive_time: About 1.5 hours by road to Nayapul per trekking operators; walking times vary, ask your guide

days.title: Tikhedhunga, Ulleri and Banthanti
activities: Cross a stream by suspension bridge and climb to Ulleri, a Magar village
Above Ulleri the trail climbs gently through cultivated fields and rhododendron and oak forest; lunch at Nangethanti, then walk on through forest to Banthanti
Overnight in a teahouse; your guide sets the pace, and walking hours are not stated in the official outline
days.drive_time: On foot all day; the Government of Nepal outline gives no hours for this section

days.title: Banthanti to Ghorepani
activities: Hike on to Ghorepani, the village below Poon Hill and the base for the sunrise climb

Ghorepani lies inside the Annapurna Conservation Area, which Nepal Tourism Board says starts at 790 m and reaches 8,091 m at Annapurna I; carry your permit and register at check-posts along the route, as the NTNC portal asks
Early dinner and sleep: tomorrow's climb starts before dawn
days.drive_time: On foot; the Government of Nepal outline gives no hours for this section

days.title: Poon Hill sunrise to Tadapani
activities: Pre-dawn hike of about one hour (Government of Nepal outline) to Poon Hill, 3,210 m, for sunrise on Annapurna and Dhaulagiri per Nepal Tourism Board. Poon Hill is above 2,500 m, where Nepal Tourism Board says any headache, nausea, dizziness or unusual fatigue may be altitude sickness until proven otherwise: do not go higher, rest, and descend if symptoms worsen.
Walk back down to Ghorepani for breakfast
Continue to Tadapani by way of Deurali: the trail climbs along ridges through pine and rhododendron forest, then descends
days.drive_time: On foot; about one hour up to Poon Hill (Government of Nepal outline), other sections unstated

days.title: Tadapani to Ghandruk and back to Pokhara
activities: Trek about four hours (Government of Nepal outline) to Ghandruk, a Gurung village with close views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre
Lunch in Ghandruk, then drive via Nayapul back to Pokhara
Hot shower and a lakeside dinner
days.drive_time: About four hours on foot to Ghandruk; road return to Pokhara via Nayapul (operators quote about 1.5 hours from Nayapul)

days.title: Pokhara buffer day
activities: Keep one day free: weather can delay or cancel flights and block hill roads, and a trek can run late
Sunrise at Sarangkot (11.3 km from Lakeside, a maximum 30 minutes by road per Nepal Tourism Board) or the World Peace Pagoda
Rest your legs on Phewa Lake or in the Old Bazaar
days.drive_time: Sarangkot, up to 30 minutes by road from Lakeside (Nepal Tourism Board)

days.title: Fly to Kathmandu and depart
activities: Buddha Air flight Pokhara to Kathmandu, 25 minutes, more than 16 flights a day per Buddha Air's route page. Flights can be delayed or cancelled by weather; Global Affairs Canada notes the June to September monsoon can disrupt flights and flood or block roads, and mountain weather can change suddenly. Buddha Air's route pages say schedules are subject to change, so check the flight status page.
Connect to your onward international flight or spend the day in Thamel; allow a generous buffer before an international departure
days.lodging_suggestion: Kathmandu near the airport if departing next morning

food_culture.name: Dal bhat on the trail
food_culture.description: Rice with lentil soup and vegetable curry is the standard teahouse meal on the Poon Hill trail, served in the villages of Tikhedhunga, Ghorepani and Tadapani.

food_culture.name: Thakali teahouse cooking
food_culture.description: Nepal Tourism Board says the Thakalis run many of the tea houses along Annapurna region trails and that their home cooking is relished by tourists and Nepalis alike.

food_culture.name: Gurung village of Ghandruk
food_culture.description: A Gurung village the Government of Nepal describes as famous for its Gorkha soldiers; Nepal Tourism Board names the Gurungs and Magars as the main communities around Pokhara.

food_culture.name: Poon Hill sunrise
food_culture.description: Trekkers rise before dawn from Ghorepani for the hour's hike up to Poon Hill to watch the sunrise on Annapurna and Dhaulagiri, the trek's defining moment in Nepal Tourism Board's description.

food_culture.name: Nepali milk tea at the teahouse
food_culture.description: Teahouses along the trail serve hot milk tea alongside meals, a staple that gets you through the pre-dawn start to Poon Hill.

food_culture.name: Newar craft cities of Bhaktapur
food_culture.description: Nepal Tourism Board names Newars as the original inhabitants of the Kathmandu Valley whose skills were championed by the Malla kings; Bhaktapur Durbar Square and its museums show that craft heritage.

title: Siem Reap, Angkor + Phnom Penh, Cambodia
best_time_description: November to February is Cambodia's cool dry season (Ministry of Tourism's tourism site gives 17-27 C for November to February), the most comfortable time for walking temple complexes; it is also the busiest. March to May is hot and dry (29-38 C on the same source), and the rains run roughly June to October, when roads and temple paths can be muddy but crowds are smaller. Phnom Penh's Water Festival (Bon Om Touk) in November packs the capital.
description: The classic first-timer arc: three days among the Angkor temples from Siem Reap (Angkor Wat, Angkor Thom and the Bayon, Ta Prohm, Banteay Srei and Kbal Spean), then a morning bus to Phnom Penh for the Royal Palace, the National Museum and the Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek memorials. Entry is a tourist visa (e-Visa online or on arrival) plus the free e-Arrival Card; Angkor needs its own pass.

days.title: Arrive Siem Reap
activities: Land at Siem Reap Angkor International Airport. Before flying, complete the free Cambodia e-Arrival Card online (arrival.gov.kh) within 7 days before arrival, and have a tourist visa (e-Visa from evisa.gov.kh, USD 30, or on arrival; Singapore passports are visa-free)
Stroll the Old Market (Psar Chas) area and the Siem Reap River
Early night: Angkor opens at 5:00 AM
days.lodging_suggestion: Siem Reap (Old Market or Wat Bo area)

days.title: Angkor Wat + the small circuit
activities: Buy your Angkor pass first. Angkor Enterprise (the only valid seller) quotes USD 37 for a 1-day pass, USD 62 for a 3-day pass (use within 7 days of purchase) and USD 72 for a 7-day pass (use within 30 days). 3-day and 7-day passes need a photo; the 1-day does not. Buy online or at the ticket office on Road 60, 4 km from the centre, open 5:30 AM to 5 PM. Entry is 5:00 AM to 6:30 PM
Angkor Wat at opening time; children under 12 do not need a ticket, but the Upper Tower is for ages 12 and up
Bakheng temple (Phnom Bakheng) for the late-afternoon views
Dress modestly for the temples and follow the Apsara Authority code of conduct
days.lodging_suggestion: Siem Reap (Old Market or Wat Bo area)

days.title: Angkor Thom, Bayon + Preah Khan
activities: Bayon and the walled city of Angkor Thom
Baphuon temple
Preah Khan temple, on the Angkor Enterprise highlights list, and Ta Prohm
Return to Siem Reap for an Apsara dance dinner show
days.lodging_suggestion: Siem Reap (Old Market or Wat Bo area)

days.title: Banteay Srei + Kbal Spean
activities: Banteay Srei, the 10th-century Shiva temple about 25 km north-east of the main Angkor group
Kbal Spean has its own ticket (Angkor Enterprise lists USD 5, open 6:00 AM to 6:30 PM), separate from the Angkor pass
Use the third pass day to revisit a temple, or pay Angkor Enterprise's separate Beng Mealea ticket (USD 10, 6:00 AM to 6:30 PM)
days.lodging_suggestion: Siem Reap (Old Market or Wat Bo area)

days.title: Bus to Phnom Penh
activities: Giant Ibis bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh: departures at 8:45 AM, 9:45 AM and 12:30 PM per its schedule; the operator says the 320 km journey takes about 6 hours depending on traffic
Evening along the Phnom Penh riverfront (Sisowath Quay)
If you arrive during the Water Festival in November, expect crowds and book accommodation early

days.title: Royal Palace, National Museum + memorials
activities: Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (dress covering shoulders and knees; check the current opening hours before you go)
National Museum of Cambodia
Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21) and Choeung Ek Killing Fields: a sombre but central part of understanding modern Cambodia
Lunch of fish amok or kuy teav

days.title: Markets + departure
activities: Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) for souvenirs and street food
Depart Phnom Penh by air. Cambodia lists Techo International Airport as an e-Visa airport; check which airport your flight uses

food_culture.name: Fish amok
food_culture.description: Cambodia's best-known curry-style dish: fish steamed in a banana-leaf or coconut-milk custard flavoured with kroeung, a lemongrass-and-galangal paste. Restaurants in Siem Reap and Phnom Penh serve it, often in a banana-leaf cup.

food_culture.name: Beef lok lak
food_culture.description: Stir-fried marinated beef cubes served on lettuce and tomato with a lime-and-black-pepper dipping sauce; a staple on Khmer menus in both cities.

food_culture.name: Kuy teav
food_culture.description: A pork-bone broth noodle soup eaten for breakfast across Cambodia, topped with herbs, fried garlic and lime; Phnom Penh has many street and market stalls for it.

food_culture.name: Num banh chok
food_culture.description: Fresh rice noodles topped with a cold green fish-based curry and raw vegetables and herbs; a Khmer morning dish sold at markets, with a variant often called Khmer noodles.

food_culture.name: Fresh sugarcane juice
food_culture.description: Pressed to order at roadside stalls and markets, usually served over ice with a squeeze of lime; a popular cooler between temples.

food_culture.name: Apsara dance
food_culture.description: Classical Khmer dance whose costumed dancers are modelled on the celestial apsara figures carved on the walls of Angkor Wat. Dinner-show venues in Siem Reap and cultural performances in Phnom Penh feature it.

food_culture.name: Pchum Ben
food_culture.description: A Buddhist festival in September or early October in which families visit pagodas to make offerings for ancestors; many Cambodians travel home for it, so buses and guesthouses can be busy.

food_culture.name: Bon Om Touk (Water Festival)
food_culture.description: Held around the November full moon at Phnom Penh's riverfront with boat races on the Tonle Sap river, it marks the reversal of the Tonle Sap's flow; the city is crowded and accommodation books out.

title: Phnom Penh, Kampot, Kep + Koh Rong, Cambodia
best_time_description: November to February is the cool dry season on the Ministry of Tourism's site (17-27 C), best for Bokor, pepper farms and the island beaches; March to May is hot and dry, June to October is the rainy season with the heaviest rain in Phnom Penh in September and October. Boats to the islands depend on the sea state, and Khmer New Year in mid-April fills the coast with domestic travellers.
description: The southern coast at an unhurried pace: Phnom Penh's sights, then Giant Ibis buses to Kampot (river town, Bokor Hill Station and Kampot pepper farms) and Kep (crabs, Rabbit Island), back through the capital to Sihanoukville and a speedboat to Koh Rong. Stays well away from the Thai border provinces that Australia's Smartraveller advises against, and avoids Koh Kong province.

days.title: Arrive Phnom Penh
activities: Arrive after completing the free Cambodia e-Arrival Card (arrival.gov.kh) within 7 days before travel; get a tourist visa online from evisa.gov.kh (USD 30) or on arrival (Singapore passports are visa-free for up to 30 days)
Walk the riverfront on Sisowath Quay at dusk

days.title: Phnom Penh sights
activities: Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (dress covering shoulders and knees; check current opening hours)
National Museum of Cambodia
Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) in the afternoon

days.title: Bus to Kampot
activities: Giant Ibis bus Phnom Penh to Kampot at 8:00 AM or 2:45 PM; the operator says National Road 3 is in poor condition and the 150 km trip takes about 4 hours plus or minus 15 minutes
Evening on Kampot's riverfront

days.title: Bokor + pepper farms
activities: Bokor National Park and the Bokor Hill Station, one of the province's two highest points at 1,027 m (check road and weather conditions locally)
Afternoon visit to a Kampot pepper plantation: the Ministry of Tourism's site lists pepper plantations as a Kampot attraction
Tuk Chhou waterfalls, about 10 km from Kampot, if time allows

days.title: Kep and Rabbit Island
activities: Travel the 15 km paved road from Kampot to Kep (the Ministry of Tourism's site describes it as a popular day trip from Kampot)
Seafood lunch at the Kep waterfront; Kep is known for its crabs
Boat to Rabbit Island (Koh Thonsay), about half an hour away per the Ministry of Tourism's site
Overnight in Kep

days.title: Kep back to Phnom Penh
activities: Giant Ibis bus Kep to Phnom Penh at 7:30 AM or 1:45 PM; the operator says National Road 3 makes the 167 km trip take about 4 hours plus or minus 15 minutes
Afternoon in Phnom Penh at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum or Choeung Ek (if you took the morning bus)

days.title: Bus to Sihanoukville
activities: Giant Ibis bus Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville at 7:45 AM; the operator says the expressway journey takes about 4 hours plus or minus 30 minutes for 240 km
Afternoon on the Sihanoukville beaches; this coastal city is the departure point for the islands

days.title: Koh Rong
activities: Speedboat from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong; Buva Sea Cambodia lists services to Koh Rong, and other operators also run; confirm the day's timetable and your return slot with the operator because the operator pages did not publish times
Beach time, snorkelling and swimming; sea conditions can cancel sailings

days.title: Return and depart
activities: Morning boat back to Sihanoukville
Depart from Sihanoukville airport, or take the Giant Ibis bus back to Phnom Penh at 1:30 PM or 7:00 PM (about 4 hours plus or minus 30 minutes)

food_culture.name: Kampot pepper crab
food_culture.description: Crab stir-fried with fresh green Kampot pepper corns; the Ministry of Tourism's site notes that seafood in Kep is cheap, plentiful and that its crabs are particularly famous. Kampot pepper is among the best-known peppers in the world.

food_culture.name: Fish amok
food_culture.description: Fish steamed in a coconut-milk custard flavoured with kroeung paste, Cambodia's best-known dish; menus in Phnom Penh and Kampot carry it.

food_culture.name: Grilled seafood and squid
food_culture.description: Along the Kep waterfront and Sihanoukville's beaches, grilled fish, prawns and squid are served with lime-pepper dipping sauce.

food_culture.name: Kuy teav
food_culture.description: Pork-bone broth noodle soup eaten for breakfast; Phnom Penh markets have stalls for it from early morning.

food_culture.name: Fresh coconut and sugarcane juice
food_culture.description: Sold at roadside stalls and beach shacks; a cheap way to cool down on the coast.

food_culture.name: Pepper plantations of Kampot
food_culture.description: Pepper plantations are listed by the Ministry of Tourism's site among Kampot's attractions; farms around town offer visits and tasting of black, red and white pepper.

food_culture.name: Kep's abandoned French colonial villas
food_culture.description: Kep was a seaside resort in the French colonial era; the Ministry of Tourism's site mentions its abandoned villas and unfurnished royal palace overlooking the Gulf of Thailand.

food_culture.name: Khmer New Year (Chaul Chnam Thmey)
food_culture.description: Celebrated in mid-April with temple visits, water splashing and family gatherings; towns and beaches get crowded with domestic travellers and prices rise.

title: Auckland, Rotorua + Wellington, North Island, New Zealand
best_time_description: Summer (December to March) is the settled, warm window for Auckland's harbour and Wellington's waterfront, and November and April work with fewer visitors. Rotorua's geothermal parks run year-round, so the route does not depend on one season, but this is a self-drive route with no mountain passes, so winter weather matters less here than on the South Island.
description: A one-way North Island route from the big harbour city to the geothermal heartland and on to the capital: Auckland's volcanic cones and museum, Rotorua's steaming valleys and living Maori culture, then Wellington's national museum and waterfront. Fly in to Auckland, out of Wellington.

days.title: Arrive Auckland
activities: Land at Auckland Airport, collect a rental car for day 3 or use airport transfers for the city days
Check in near the Viaduct Harbour or Britomart and walk the waterfront
Early night to recover from the flight

days.title: Auckland: museum, volcano and harbour
activities: Auckland War Memorial Museum in the Domain, with its Maori and Pacific collections
Climb the Mount Eden (Maungawhau) volcanic cone for a view over the city
Sky Tower observation deck, then dinner around the Viaduct or Wynyard Quarter

days.title: Auckland to Rotorua
activities: Drive Auckland to Rotorua, about 3 hours (Rotorua tourism board's figure for the drive from Auckland); stop for lunch on the way
Arrive in Rotorua and walk by the lakefront and Government Gardens
Evening walk through Kuirau Park, a thermal park in the town centre

days.title: Rotorua: geothermal valley and Maori culture
activities: Morning in a geothermal park such as Te Puia (Whakarewarewa), with its geysers and Maori Arts and Crafts Institute, or Waimangu Volcanic Valley; check each operator's opening hours and ticket booking before you go
Walk or ride in The Redwoods (Whakarewarewa Forest) in the afternoon
Evening Maori cultural performance and hangi meal; these sell out in peak season, so book ahead with the venue

days.title: Rotorua to Wellington
activities: Drive Rotorua to Wellington, about 5 hours 30 minutes (Rotorua and Wellington tourism boards both give this figure); leave early and break the drive in Taupo, which is about 1 hour from Rotorua
Alternative: Air New Zealand flies Rotorua Airport to Wellington (Rotorua tourism board lists Wellington among its direct destinations); check the airline's schedule for the flight time
Arrive Wellington and walk the waterfront in the evening

days.title: Wellington: Te Papa and the waterfront
activities: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa on the waterfront, including the Maori exhibitions
Wellington Cable Car to the Botanic Garden, then walk down through the garden
Cuba Street for coffee and dinner

days.title: Wellington: wildlife sanctuary and the Beehive
activities: Zealandia Te Mara a Tane, a fenced wildlife sanctuary valley in the city, for native birds; check the sanctuary for day and night tour booking
Parliament buildings and the Beehive: check the New Zealand Parliament website for tour availability and booking
Mount Victoria lookout at sunset

days.title: Depart Wellington
activities: Breakfast on the waterfront
Fly out of Wellington Airport; leave the rental car at the airport depot
Optional extension: the Cook Strait ferry to Picton takes about 3 hours 30 minutes (Wellington tourism board and Interislander) and leads into the South Island itinerary

food_culture.name: Hangi
food_culture.description: Food slow-cooked in an earth oven heated with hot stones, a traditional Maori method. In Rotorua it is served at cultural evenings, and at Whakarewarewa the geothermal heat is used for cooking in steam boxes.

food_culture.name: Kumara
food_culture.description: The Maori sweet potato, grown in New Zealand for centuries and a staple on a hangi plate; look for it roasted, as chips or in salads.

food_culture.name: Hokey pokey ice cream
food_culture.description: A vanilla ice cream with crunchy honeycomb toffee pieces, sold in scoop shops across the North Island and a common sweet treat in New Zealand.

food_culture.name: Flat white
food_culture.description: A smooth espresso drink with microfoam milk that is standard in Auckland and Wellington cafes; Wellington's Cuba Street and surrounding lanes have a dense independent coffee scene.

food_culture.name: Hongi and pōwhiri
food_culture.description: The hongi is the traditional Maori greeting of pressing noses and foreheads, and the pōwhiri is the formal welcome onto a marae. Visitors to a cultural experience in Rotorua are often welcomed with an adapted pōwhiri; follow the host's lead on when to speak and when to stay quiet.

food_culture.name: Kapa haka and Te Reo Maori
food_culture.description: Kapa haka is Maori performing arts including song, haka and poi, seen at Rotorua's cultural evenings and at Te Papa. Te Reo Maori is an official language of New Zealand, so you will see dual Maori and English names on signs and in museums.

title: Christchurch, Aoraki/Mt Cook, Queenstown + Milford Sound, South Island, New Zealand
best_time_description: December to March gives the longest days and the most open roads. The Milford Road's avalanche season typically runs from June to November (NZTA), so early summer and autumn are safer for a road trip to Milford Sound. The DOC Great Walk season for the Milford and Routeburn tracks runs from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027, which is when their huts operate.
description: A South Island road trip from the garden city to the Southern Alps and Fiordland: whale watching on the Kaikoura coast, Aoraki/Mt Cook's glacial valley, Queenstown, then the Milford Road to Milford Sound. Fly into Christchurch, out of Queenstown.

days.title: Arrive Christchurch
activities: Land in Christchurch and collect a rental car
Christchurch Botanic Gardens and a walk along the Avon River
Christchurch Art Gallery Toi o Waiwhetu in the city centre

days.title: Christchurch to Kaikoura
activities: Drive Christchurch to Kaikoura, about 2 hours 30 minutes and 180 km on SH1 (Destination Kaikoura; Tourism New Zealand pages give 2 h 30 min to 2 h 45 min)
Alternative: the Coastal Pacific train runs seasonally between Picton and Christchurch from late September to the end of April; check the schedule at Great Journeys New Zealand
Walk the Kaikoura Peninsula and look out over the coast; the name Kaikoura means a meal of crayfish in Maori

days.title: Kaikoura whales and back to Christchurch
activities: Morning whale watching or another marine wildlife trip from Kaikoura; trips are with private operators, so book ahead and check the weather policy, because sea conditions can cancel sailings
Return drive Kaikoura to Christchurch, about 2 hours 30 minutes (Destination Kaikoura)
Evening in the city; early night before the long drive to Mt Cook

days.title: Christchurch to Aoraki/Mt Cook
activities: Drive Christchurch to Aoraki/Mt Cook Village, about 4 hours 10 minutes and 332 km via SH1 and SH8 (Tourism New Zealand route page, listed from the Mt Cook end); stop on the way at Lake Tekapo
Check road conditions on the NZTA highway page before you leave; snow can close SH80 to Aoraki/Mt Cook (DOC)
Arrive in the village and settle in for sunset views of the mountains

days.title: Hooker Valley Track and the stars
activities: Hooker Valley Track from the White Horse Hill car park, about 5 km one way: DOC lists the sections at 15, 30 and 45 minutes, about 1 hour 30 minutes each way and roughly 10 km return, to a glacial lake. No booking is listed on DOC's page; check DOC for current track status, as a new second swing bridge opened in July 2026
DOC warns that weather changes fast, the lakes are around 3 degrees Celsius, and shaded sections can be icy in winter
Stargaze in the evening: Aoraki Mackenzie is an International Dark Sky Reserve

days.title: Aoraki/Mt Cook to Queenstown
activities: Drive Aoraki/Mt Cook to Queenstown, about 3 hours 15 minutes and 264 km via SH6 and SH8 (Tourism New Zealand route page)
Queenstown Gardens and lakefront walk on arrival
Skyline Queenstown gondola for the view over Lake Wakatipu at sunset

days.title: Queenstown to Milford Sound
activities: Drive Queenstown to Milford Sound, 287 km via SH6 and SH94, listed by Tourism New Zealand at 3 hours 45 minutes to 4 hours 30 minutes each way; DOC says to allow about 2 hours for the whole Milford Road between Te Anau and Milford Sound without stops

Milford Road status: NZTA says the road closes about 8 days a year on average, mostly in winter, and avalanche season is typically June to November, when a high hazard means the road is shut; check the NZTA SH94 Milford Road status page or call 0800 44 44 49 before you leave, and carry chains if signs require them. Only stop in the signposted safe areas (The Chasm and Monkey Creek) in the avalanche zone

Take a Milford Sound cruise to see Mitre Peak (1,692 m, DOC) and the waterfalls; book the cruise ahead with an operator, and note DOC warns that a big earthquake could trigger a large tsunami in Piopiotahi Milford Sound, with a Know before you go section on its page

Great Walk note: the Milford Track and Routeburn Track huts and campsites must be booked through DOC for the Great Walks season (1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027); this route does not walk them, so no DOC booking is needed for the road trip itself. Overnight in Te Anau or Milford Sound, and book lodging ahead, because it fills in summer

days.title: Milford Sound back to Queenstown
activities: Drive Milford Sound back to Queenstown, the same 287 km route and about 3 hours 45 minutes to 4 hours 30 minutes (Tourism New Zealand); check the Milford Road status again before leaving, as closures can be at short notice when avalanche hazard is moderate
Arrowtown or a lake walk in Queenstown for a slow afternoon
Dinner in Queenstown town centre

days.title: Depart Queenstown
activities: Fly out of Queenstown Airport (for scale, the Wellington tourism board gives about 1 hour 30 minutes by air between Queenstown and Wellington)
Return the rental car at the airport

food_culture.name: Kaikoura crayfish (koura)
food_culture.description: The town's Maori name means a meal (kai) of crayfish (koura), and rock lobster is the local specialty at restaurants and roadside caravans around town; ask about the catch and its price per kilo.

food_culture.name: High-country salmon
food_culture.description: Look for farmed salmon from the Mackenzie Country on menus around Twizel and Lake Tekapo, on the drive between Christchurch and Mt Cook.

food_culture.name: Fergburger
food_culture.description: A Queenstown institution on Shotover Street, known for its big burgers and queues; expect a wait at peak hours and order ahead if you are short of time.

food_culture.name: Central Otago pinot noir
food_culture.description: Queenstown sits at the edge of Central Otago, one of the world's southernmost wine regions, and its pinot noir is the signature red; cellar doors and tastings are an easy afternoon from Queenstown or Arrowtown.

food_culture.name: Ngai Tahu and the Aoraki story
food_culture.description: Aoraki is named for an ancestor in the traditions of Ngai Tahu, the South Island's principal iwi, and the mountain's official name reflects both Maori and English names.

food_culture.name: Leave no trace and the Great Walks
food_culture.description: New Zealand's backcountry runs on DOC's hut and track system. Great Walk huts must be booked in season, and DOC's advice at Aoraki/Mt Cook includes keeping to the track and staying out of the cold glacial lakes.

title: Rio de Janeiro + Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil
best_time_description: Rio and Iguaçu sit in different climates, so there is no perfect month for both. The months chosen (May to September) are an editorial pick for the cooler, drier half of the year in south-east Brazil and were not checked against INMET monthly normals; see the Brazil country guide's climate table for figures. The Iguaçu River's level matters at the falls: the national park's own site reported a flood-safety protocol during high water on 13 October, with walkway railings removed and some trails temporarily closed, so check the park's notices before booking a fixed date.
description: A classic first-timer arc: four days in Rio de Janeiro for Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf, the beaches and the old centre, then a domestic flight to Foz do Iguaçu for the Brazilian side of the Iguaçu Falls.

days.title: Arrive Rio de Janeiro
activities: Arrive at Rio de Janeiro international airport (Galeão, GIG) and transfer to Copacabana, Ipanema or Leblon
Walk the Copacabana and Ipanema beachfront at the end of the day
Dinner in Ipanema; try a caipirinha (cachaça, lime and sugar)

days.title: Christ the Redeemer + Santa Teresa
activities: Christ the Redeemer sits inside Tijuca National Park (managed by ICMBio); buy your transport and entry ahead online with the operator and check the current ticketing arrangement before you go
Afternoon in Santa Teresa: the hilltop neighbourhood's old houses and viewpoints
Evening around the Lapa Arches and the Selarón Steps

days.title: Sugarloaf + Botanical Garden
activities: Sugarloaf cable car between Praia Vermelha, Urca Hill and Sugarloaf Mountain; the operator's site lists 8:30-21:00 Monday to Friday and 7:30-21:00 on weekends, last boarding 19:30 (as read in October 2026, so check before you go); tickets are bought on the operator's site
Time the upper station for late afternoon light over Guanabara Bay
Morning option: the Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro

days.title: Historic centre + samba in Lapa
activities: Praça Mauá, the Museu do Amanhã and the Museu de Arte do Rio on the revitalised waterfront
Lunch around Centro: a feijoada, the black-bean and pork stew eaten across Brazil
Evening live samba in Lapa

days.title: Fly to Foz do Iguaçu
activities: Domestic flight from Rio de Janeiro to Foz do Iguaçu (IGU); check on the airlines' sites whether your date has a nonstop, as the flight time depends on that
Check in and keep the afternoon light: the falls are the next day
Evening meal in Foz do Iguaçu

days.title: Iguaçu Falls, Brazilian side
activities: Iguaçu National Park (BR-469, km 18): open every day, 9:00-16:00 Monday to Friday and 8:30-16:00 on weekends per the park's site (October 2026); buy a time-slot ticket online at tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br
Take the park's panoramic bus to the Visitor Center, then walk the Trilha das Cataratas (about 1.5 km) to the walkway over the falls and the Garganta do Diabo viewpoint
Check the park's notices first: during high water it removes walkway railings and closes some trails

days.title: Depart Foz do Iguaçu
activities: Optional: the Argentine side of the falls is a separate national park in another country; check Argentina's entry rules for your passport before planning it
Fly home or onward from Foz do Iguaçu (IGU)

food_culture.name: Feijoada
food_culture.description: A stew of black beans with pork cuts, served with rice, farofa (toasted cassava flour), shredded greens and orange slices; long a weekend lunch in Rio's restaurants and one of Brazil's best-known dishes.

food_culture.name: Caipirinha
food_culture.description: Brazil's signature cocktail of cachaça (a spirit distilled from sugarcane juice), lime and sugar, served over ice at beach kiosks and bars across Rio.

food_culture.name: Pão de queijo
food_culture.description: Small chewy cheese breads made with cassava starch, sold at bakeries and lanchonetes for breakfast and snacks; originally from Minas Gerais and found in every Rio bakery.

food_culture.name: Samba rodas in Lapa
food_culture.description: Live samba is a part of Rio's nightlife, especially around Lapa, where bars and casas de samba host bands playing the genre that grew out of Rio's Afro-Brazilian communities.

food_culture.name: Rio's UNESCO cultural landscape
food_culture.description: UNESCO inscribed 'Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea' as a World Heritage cultural site in 2012; it covers areas such as Tijuca National Park, Sugarloaf, the Botanical Garden and the Copacabana seafront.

title: Salvador + Lençóis Maranhenses, Brazil
best_time_description: Salvador's old town is a year-round destination, but the Lençóis lagoons are rain-fed: ICMBio says they appear and disappear with rain, wind and moving dunes and that the park is open all year. ICMBio's management plan reports the heaviest rain in March and April, flooded access trails in the rainy period and dunes migrating as the water table falls in the dry period, with visitor peaks in January and July (school holidays). July to September is therefore an editorial pick for the weeks after the rains; the park's pages publish no lagoon calendar, so ask an ICMBio-accredited operator in Barreirinhas what the lagoons look like on your dates.
description: Afro-Brazilian Salvador, with its UNESCO-listed old town, then a flight north to São Luís and a road trip to Barreirinhas for the white dunes and rain-filled lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park.

days.title: Arrive Salvador
activities: Arrive at Salvador airport (SSA) and transfer to the city
Evening walk in the Pelourinho historic centre, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1985
Dinner of moqueca baiana, a fish or shrimp stew with coconut milk and dendê (palm) oil

days.title: Pelourinho + Cidade Baixa
activities: Terreiro de Jesus and the Igreja e Convento de São Francisco with its interior gilded carving
Largo do Pelourinho and the surrounding colonial streets
Elevador Lacerda down to the lower city and the Mercado Modelo craft market
Sunset at Farol da Barra

days.title: Bonfim + Afro-Bahian culture
activities: Igreja do Senhor do Bonfim, the pilgrimage church whose wish ribbons (fitas) are sold on the steps
Eat acarajé from a baiana de acarajé, a street-food craft protected as national heritage
Evening capoeira or samba de roda show in the old town

days.title: Fly Salvador to São Luís
activities: Morning flight from Salvador (SSA) to São Luís (SLZ); Salvador airport's destination list includes São Luís, but check on airline sites whether your date has a nonstop
Afternoon in São Luís historic centre (UNESCO World Heritage since 1997): Praça Dom Pedro II and the tiled colonial facades
Dinner of arroz de cuxá, the Maranhão rice dish made with vinagreira (hibiscus) leaves, and a glass of Guaraná Jesus

days.title: São Luís to Barreirinhas
activities: Road transfer from São Luís to Barreirinhas, about 260 km by BR-135 then MA-402, roughly 3 hours according to ICMBio's park management plan (a private car, shuttle or tour operator; check current road conditions locally)
Settle in Barreirinhas, the main gateway to the park, and book tours with ICMBio-accredited operators: only accredited vehicles, drivers and guides may take visitors into the park

days.title: Lagoa Azul + Lagoa Bonita
activities: Half-day 4x4 tour to the Lagoa Azul circuit; lagoons here appear and disappear with rain, wind and moving dunes, so ask your operator which are full
Lagoa Bonita route: 4x4 on sand roads, then a wooden staircase up to the dunes, with stops at Lagoa do Clone and Lagoa do Descanso
Park rules: no alcohol in the park, no private vehicles carrying visitors, no fires; ICMBio charges no park entry fee but operators charge for tours

days.title: Rio Preguiças + Atins
activities: Boat trip down the Rio Preguiças to Atins, the village opposite the river mouth just outside the park (confirm boat times with your operator)
Atins is known for kitesurfing, windsurfing, kayaking and horse riding
Optional beach route to the Foz do Rio Negro and Lagoa Verde, which ICMBio says starts in Atins; ask whether it is feasible on your date

days.title: Back to São Luís
activities: Road transfer from Barreirinhas to São Luís, about 260 km and roughly 3 hours per ICMBio's management plan
Evening in the São Luís historic centre
Try torta de camarão or a seafood dinner at a restaurant in the old town

days.title: Depart São Luís
activities: Fly home or onward from São Luís airport (SLZ)
Leave a buffer for the road transfer if you are returning from Barreirinhas the same morning

food_culture.name: Acarajé
food_culture.description: Deep-fried black-eyed-pea fritters split and filled with vatapá, caruru and shrimp, sold by baianas in white dress on Salvador's streets; the baiana de acarajé trade was registered as national heritage by IPHAN in 2005.

food_culture.name: Moqueca baiana
food_culture.description: Bahia's stew of fish or shrimp cooked with coconut milk, peppers, tomato and dendê (palm) oil, usually served with rice and farofa.

food_culture.name: Arroz de cuxá
food_culture.description: A Maranhão dish of rice with vinagreira (hibiscus sabdariffa) leaves, sesame and dried shrimp, a staple of São Luís home cooking and restaurants.

food_culture.name: Guaraná Jesus
food_culture.description: A pink guaraná soft drink from Maranhão, sold throughout São Luís and the state and rarely found in the rest of Brazil.

food_culture.name: Capoeira in Salvador
food_culture.description: Capoeira, the Afro-Brazilian martial art and dance, is practised in roda circles around Salvador's old town; the roda de capoeira is on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (2014).

food_culture.name: Bumba-meu-boi do Maranhão
food_culture.description: Maranhão's folk drama of the ox, with song, dance and costume, is held mainly around the June festivals of São João; UNESCO listed the Bumba-meu-boi complex of Maranhão as intangible cultural heritage in 2019.

food_culture.name: Lençóis Maranhenses World Heritage Site
food_culture.description: The park's dune field and lagoons are on the UNESCO World Heritage list (ICMBio links the UNESCO listing from the park's page); ICMBio-accredited guides and vehicles are the only way in.

title: Buenos Aires, Iguazu Falls + Mendoza, Argentina
best_time_description: Autumn (March to May) and spring (October to November) are the comfortable windows for all three stops: Buenos Aires and Mendoza are mild, and Iguazu avoids the peak summer heat. Iguazu's Garganta del Diablo walkway is closed as a precaution when the river rises, so check its status on the park concessionaire's site before you go. Mendoza's high-mountain road to Puente del Inca can be affected by winter snow, so check road status in July and August.
description: Argentina's classic first-timer arc: three days of Buenos Aires cafes, theatres and tango, a short flight north to the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls, then back via Buenos Aires to Mendoza for Malbec vineyards under the Andes and a day in the high mountains near Aconcagua. The legs are linked by domestic flights from Buenos Aires.

days.title: Arrive Buenos Aires
activities: Arrive at Ezeiza (EZE) or Aeroparque (AEP) and transfer into the city
Evening stroll around Plaza de Mayo and Avenida de Mayo
Dinner at a parrilla (grill house) in Palermo or San Telmo
days.lodging_suggestion: Palermo, Recoleta or San Telmo, Buenos Aires

days.title: Historic centre + Teatro Colon
activities: Plaza de Mayo, the Cabildo and the exterior of the Casa Rosada

Guided tour of the Teatro Colon (about 50 minutes, tours daily from 10:00 to 16:45 except 1 May, 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January; English tours at 11:00, 12:00, 13:00 and 15:00; buy tickets online or at the box office on Tucuman 1171; the box office takes pesos or cards, not foreign currency)
Cafe stop at a historic cafe on Avenida de Mayo or in San Telmo
days.lodging_suggestion: Palermo, Recoleta or San Telmo, Buenos Aires

days.title: Recoleta, Palermo + tango
activities: Recoleta Cemetery and the neighbourhood's plazas and cafes
Walk through Palermo's parks and the Plaza Serrano area
On Sundays the San Telmo street fair runs along Calle Defensa; otherwise book a tango show or a milonga (social dance night) for the evening
days.lodging_suggestion: Palermo, Recoleta or San Telmo, Buenos Aires

days.title: Fly to Iguazu
activities: Domestic flight from Buenos Aires (Aeroparque or Ezeiza) to Cataratas del Iguazu airport (IGR); flight times vary by airline and schedule, so check when booking
Transfer to Puerto Iguazu town (the park gate is on Ruta 101, Km 142)
Evening at the Hito Tres Fronteras viewpoint where the Iguazu and Parana rivers meet Brazil and Paraguay

days.title: Iguazu Falls, Argentine side
activities: Park (Area Cataratas) opens every day of the year from 8:00 to 18:00, last entry 16:00; the circuits close at 16:45; tickets are for a selected date and time and can be bought online from 30 days ahead

Take the Tren Ecologico de la Selva (included in the entry ticket; first departure 8:20, last departure to Garganta station 15:30, last return 17:30) to the Garganta del Diablo walkway (2.2 km round trip). It closes as a precaution when the river rises, so confirm its status on the day
Upper Circuit (3.7 km round trip, about 90 minutes, wheelchair accessible) and Lower Circuit (2.9 km round trip, about 90 minutes, steep stairs on part of it)
Showing your day-one ticket at the ticket office gives 50 percent off a second day, per the park concessionaire

days.title: Macuco trail + return to Buenos Aires
activities: Sendero Macuco jungle trail to the 23 m Salto Arrechea (7.6 km round trip, about 3 hours; opens 8:00 and rangers close it in bad weather)
Optionally use the second-day half-price entry for a slower pass along the Upper Circuit
Afternoon or evening flight from Iguazu (IGR) back to Buenos Aires
days.lodging_suggestion: Near Aeroparque or Palermo, Buenos Aires

days.title: Fly to Mendoza
activities: Domestic flight from Buenos Aires to Mendoza (MDZ); flight times vary by airline and schedule
Plaza Independencia and the tree-lined boulevards of Mendoza city
Dinner of grilled meats and local wine in the city centre

days.title: Luján de Cuyo wine day
activities: Visit two or three Malbec wineries in Luján de Cuyo; tastings are usually by reservation, so book ahead
Lunch at a winery restaurant
Return to Mendoza city for an evening walk through Parque General San Martin

days.title: High mountains: Uspallata, Puente del Inca + Aconcagua
activities: Ruta 7 west toward the Chilean border through the Uspallata valley, with stops at Puente del Inca's natural stone bridge
Aconcagua Provincial Park viewpoints and the short walk toward Laguna de los Horcones; the road and park can close for snow in winter, so check road status the day before
Return to Mendoza for a last evening in the city

days.title: Depart Mendoza
activities: Morning free for the Mercado Central and cafes
Fly Mendoza (MDZ) to Buenos Aires for your onward international flight, leaving a generous gap between flights as Aeroparque and Ezeiza are different airports

food_culture.name: Asado and parrilla
food_culture.description: Argentina's grilled-meat tradition is cooked over embers on a parrilla, and a mixed grill typically brings beef cuts, chorizo and morcilla to a shared table; it anchors Sunday family meals as well as restaurant menus in Buenos Aires and Mendoza.

food_culture.name: Mendoza Malbec
