food_culture.description: The Andean foothills around Mendoza are Argentina's main wine region, and Malbec is its signature red; Luján de Cuyo is one of the best-known areas for winery tastings.

food_culture.name: Mate
food_culture.description: Mate is a bitter herbal infusion of yerba mate drunk from a gourd through a metal straw (bombilla) and passed around a group; sharing it is an everyday social ritual across the country.

food_culture.name: Cafe culture and medialunas
food_culture.description: Buenos Aires's historic cafes, many with long marble counters and wood panelling, are places to linger over a coffee with medialunas (small sweet croissants) rather than a quick stop.

food_culture.name: Tango
food_culture.description: Tango grew up in the port neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo and is inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list; visitors can watch a staged show or join a milonga (social dance night).

food_culture.name: Chipa and Misiones river cooking
food_culture.description: Around Iguazu, chipa (a cheesy cassava-starch bread of Guarani origin) is sold warm in bakeries and at roadside stands, alongside river-fish dishes of the Misiones province.

title: Patagonia: El Calafate, El Chalten + Bariloche, Argentina
best_time_description: The southern summer, November to March, gives the longest days and the most reliable trail and transport access in El Calafate and El Chalten. Los Glaciares National Park's Perito Moreno gate runs shorter winter hours from 1 May to 31 August (9:00 to 16:00), and the park requires trail registration at the visitor centre from May to September. In Bariloche, summer and early autumn suit the lake and mountain days; winter brings snow to the roads around Cerro Tronador.
description: Argentine Patagonia in nine days: fly to El Calafate for the Perito Moreno glacier, go north to El Chalten for the Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre trails, then head to the lakes and forests of Bariloche in Nahuel Huapi National Park. Distances and park rules are taken from the national park authority's own pages.

days.title: Fly Buenos Aires to El Calafate
activities: Domestic flight from Buenos Aires (Aeroparque, AEP) to El Calafate (FTE); if you land internationally at Ezeiza, allow a generous connection or sleep over in Buenos Aires
Walk the main street, Avenida del Libertador, in El Calafate
Dinner of Patagonian lamb at a restaurant in town

days.title: Perito Moreno Glacier
activities: Drive or take a tour to the Perito Moreno glacier, about 80 km from El Calafate along Provincial Route 11 (paved)

The Corredor Mitre-Glaciar Moreno gate is open 8:00 to 18:00 from 1 September to 30 April (you may stay until 20:00) and 9:00 to 16:00 from 1 May to 31 August (stay until 18:00); a park access fee applies, listed at ARS 50,000 for the general tariff from 1 June 2026, and you can pay at the gate by card or in pesos or online
Walk the network of walkways and viewpoints that bring you level with the glacier's front
Optional: guided trekking on the ice or a boat excursion from Puerto Bandera, both run by licensed operators; book ahead

days.title: Road to El Chalten
activities: Regular bus or private transfer from El Calafate to El Chalten: 220 km, all paved, with daily regular bus services between the two towns
Register and buy your Zona Norte park ticket online ahead of time, as the northern portals sell tickets online only and take cards, not cash
Easy afternoon walk to the Mirador de los Condores y de las Aguilas above town
days.drive_time: 220 km, all paved; check the bus operator's timetable for journey time

days.title: Laguna de los Tres (Fitz Roy)
activities: The most sought-after hike: to Laguna de los Tres under Cerro Fitz Roy, 25 km round trip, medium-high difficulty, 8 to 9 hours
Start early, carry food and water and layers, and check the forecast, as Fitz Roy is often cloud-covered
From May to September, trail registration at the park visitor centre is mandatory

days.title: Laguna Torre + Chorrillo del Salto
activities: Walk the valley of the Fitz Roy river to the Laguna Torre viewpoint of Cerro Torre: 18 km round trip, 3 to 4 hours each way
Shorter alternative or afternoon option: the Chorrillo del Salto waterfall walk
Evening in town; many bars and restaurants serve craft beer and lamb

days.title: Return to El Calafate
activities: Bus or transfer back along the same 220 km paved road to El Calafate
Free afternoon: Laguna Nimez nature reserve walk or the town's craft shops
Pack for the flight to Bariloche

days.title: Fly to Bariloche
activities: Fly El Calafate to San Carlos de Bariloche (BRC): the national park authority lists El Calafate among the cities with flights to Bariloche 'depending on the time of year'; if no nonstop is running, connect through Buenos Aires and allow a full day
Walk Bariloche's lakefront on Lago Nahuel Huapi and the civic centre
Try Bariloche's chocolate shops

days.title: Cerro Tronador + Pampa Linda
activities: Day trip into Nahuel Huapi National Park along the gravel road from Los Rapidos to Pampa Linda (about 50 km, passable with care; the road is one-way on a schedule: entry 10:30 to 14:00, exit 16:00 to 18:00, two-way from 19:30 to 9:00)
Pampa Linda trails below Cerro Tronador's glaciers; stay on marked paths and do not go down to Ventisquero Negro lake, which is prohibited
Park trails require prior registration; a number of trails in the area (Challhuaco, Ñirihuau and others) are closed from 1 March to 30 November for wildlife management

days.title: Lakes + departure
activities: Morning loop along the lake shore toward Llao Llao peninsula
Local brewery or chocolate stop
Fly Bariloche (BRC) to Buenos Aires for your onward flight

food_culture.name: Patagonian lamb (cordero patagonico)
food_culture.description: Whole lamb split and roasted slowly beside open flames is a signature of Patagonian steppe cooking and is served in restaurants in El Calafate and Bariloche.

food_culture.name: Calafate berry
food_culture.description: The calafate is a thorny shrub with dark berries that gives El Calafate its name, and local lore says anyone who eats one will return to Patagonia; the berries appear in jams and desserts.

food_culture.name: Bariloche chocolate
food_culture.description: Bariloche is known across Argentina for its chocolate shops, with specialities such as filled chocolates and hot chocolate served in cafes on the town's main streets.

food_culture.name: Patagonian craft beer
food_culture.description: Bariloche and El Chalten have small breweries and brewpubs, and many mountain towns serve local beer alongside lamb and trout.

food_culture.name: Mate
food_culture.description: Mate, a bitter herbal infusion sipped through a metal straw from a shared gourd, accompanies hikers and drivers in Patagonia as it does the rest of Argentina.

food_culture.name: Estancia and gaucho heritage
food_culture.description: Patagonian sheep ranches called estancias carry on gaucho horse and ranching traditions, and some offer day visits that finish with a lamb asado and tortas fritas.

title: Santiago, Valparaiso + Atacama Desert, Chile
best_time_description: September to November and March to May are the comfortable windows for this mix: mild in Santiago and the coast, and the Atacama stays dry year-round, though nights at San Pedro (about 2,400 m) are cold in every season and much colder in winter. Summer (December to February) is hot in Santiago and busy in San Pedro, so book tours and lodging ahead.
description: A first-timer's Chile: two days in Santiago, a night in hill-and-harbour Valparaiso, then a two-hour flight north to San Pedro de Atacama for salt-flat lagoons, high-altitude lakes, flamingos, sunrise geysers and some of the planet's clearest night skies.

days.title: Arrive Santiago
activities: Land at Santiago airport and transfer to the city
Evening walk and dinner in the Bellavista district, the neighbourhood Chile's tourism board suggests for an evening meal

days.title: Santiago: Plaza de Armas to Cerro San Cristobal
activities: Walk Plaza de Armas, the Metropolitan Cathedral and the exterior of La Moneda Palace (the seat of government)
Go up Cerro San Cristobal for the view over the city and, on a clear day, the Andes
Dinner in Bellavista or Vitacura

days.title: Santiago to Valparaiso
activities: Take an intercity bus west along Route 68 (about 120 km; Chile's tourism board puts bus travel from Santiago at almost 2 hours)
Wander Cerro Alegre and Cerro Concepcion, known for cobbled lanes, colourful houses and galleries
Ride a historic ascensor (hillside lift) such as Reina Victoria or El Peral for views over the bay
Valparaiso is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; evening in the old port quarter
days.lodging_suggestion: Cerro Alegre or Cerro Concepcion, Valparaiso

days.title: Valparaiso and Vina del Mar, back to Santiago
activities: Visit La Sebastiana, poet Pablo Neruda's house museum in Valparaiso (check opening days before you go)
Short hop to neighbouring Vina del Mar for the Flower Clock and Quinta Vergara
Return to Santiago by bus along Route 68 (almost 2 hours) in the late afternoon
days.lodging_suggestion: Providencia, Santiago (near the airport route for the next morning's flight)

days.title: Fly to Calama, transfer to San Pedro de Atacama
activities: Morning flight Santiago to Calama (El Loa Airport, CJC), about 2 hours, direct flights are available
Road transfer Calama to San Pedro de Atacama, about 100 km on Route 23, roughly 1.5 hours
Take it easy on arrival: San Pedro is at altitude, and Chile's tourism board advises hydrating and resting

Sunset at Valle de la Luna in Los Flamencos National Reserve; entry for Valle de la Luna is bought online at least a day ahead through the community that runs the sector (the sector was closed on some Tuesdays in October 2026, so check the date)

days.title: Salt flat lagoons and flamingos
activities: Laguna Chaxa in Los Flamencos National Reserve, a flamingo-watching site on the Atacama salt flat; the sector sets its own opening hours and last entry by season, and entry is bought through the community-run ticket page
Visit the village of Toconao and a community-run experience with the Lickanantay people
Optional: Laguna Tebenquiche and Ojos del Salar around sunset, then a stargazing session with a local astronomy operator

days.title: High-altitude lakes
activities: Day tour to the altiplanic lagoons Miscanti and Miniques (Los Flamencos National Reserve), reserved in advance via the Socaire community, with check-in in Socaire village
Piedras Rojas (Red Stones), above 4,000 m, on the same route according to Chile's tourism board; go slowly and drink water at this altitude
Lunch in Socaire

days.title: El Tatio geysers at sunrise
activities: Pre-dawn departure (around 5:00 am) for the Tatio geysers to see the steam fields at sunrise; bring warm layers, nights and early mornings are very cold
Watch for vicunas and altiplanic birds on the drive back
Afternoon rest; optional Puritama hot springs

days.title: Return to Santiago
activities: Transfer San Pedro to Calama airport (about 1.5 hours; leave generous buffer)
Fly Calama to Santiago (about 2 hours); Chile's tourism board suggests booking a flight in the afternoon or evening so the morning is not rushed
Onward international flight or an extra night in Santiago

food_culture.name: Pisco sour
food_culture.description: Chile's national cocktail, made with pisco, a grape brandy produced in the Atacama and Coquimbo regions, lime juice and sugar. Try it in Santiago's Bellavista or in the bars of Valparaiso's hill neighbourhoods.

food_culture.name: Empanada de pino
food_culture.description: A baked pastry stuffed with minced beef, onion, egg and olive, a staple of Chilean fiestas and bakeries and an easy lunch in Santiago.

food_culture.name: Caldillo de congrio
food_culture.description: A conger-eel and potato soup that Pablo Neruda wrote an ode to; it is a coastal classic, and a natural order in Valparaiso after a visit to La Sebastiana.

food_culture.name: Pablo Neruda's house museums
food_culture.description: Pablo Neruda, Chile's Nobel-winning poet, left several house museums; La Sebastiana overlooks Valparaiso's bay and is open to visitors as a house museum.

food_culture.name: Lickanantay (Atacamenian) community tourism
food_culture.description: Several sights around San Pedro, including Laguna Chaxa, Valle de la Luna and the Miscanti lagoons, are co-managed by communities of the Atacameno-Lickanantay people, who sell the entry tickets and offer guided experiences.

food_culture.name: Atacama stargazing
food_culture.description: San Pedro's dry, high-altitude air gives some of the clearest night skies on the planet according to Chile's tourism board, and astronomy sessions with local guides are a staple evening activity.

title: Punta Arenas, Puerto Natales + Torres del Paine, Chilean Patagonia
best_time_description: Late spring to early autumn (November to March) is the practical window: longer days, penguin colonies at Isla Magdalena (the tourism board lists spring to summer), the Lago Grey catamaran and full park access. Wind and fast weather changes happen in every month. Winter (May to September) brings snow and ice on park trails, special winter rules, and shorter hours. Torres del Paine entry quotas are limited, so buy early in summer.
description: A flight south, then a loop through the Strait of Magellan and Ultima Esperanza: Magellanic penguins at Isla Magdalena, a long bus ride to Puerto Natales, Milodon Cave, and three days in Torres del Paine for the lakes, the Grey Glacier boat and the Base Torres hike.

days.title: Fly Santiago to Punta Arenas
activities: Direct flight from Santiago to Punta Arenas (Presidente Carlos Ibanez del Campo Airport, PUQ); Chile's tourism board gives domestic flights as 2 to 3.5 hours depending on the destination
Stroll the waterfront of the Strait of Magellan and the city centre
Evening in town

days.title: Penguins at Isla Magdalena
activities: Boat from the Arturo Prat or Tres Puentes pier to Los Pinguinos Natural Monument (Isla Magdalena): about 2 hours each way, 4 to 6 hours for the whole excursion; this is the only way to land and see the colony, and it must be booked in advance with a Sernatur-registered operator
Spring-summer season only; the boat also passes Isla Marta's sea lions
Afternoon: Punta Arenas Municipal Cemetery and the Nao Victoria museum

days.title: Bus to Puerto Natales
activities: Intercity bus Punta Arenas to Puerto Natales, 250 km along Route 9, about 3 hours
Walk the Costanera Pedro Montt for views over the Ultima Esperanza Sound
Buy snacks, water and cash for the park and confirm your park tickets and lodging; try Patagonian lamb, southern king crab or southern hake for dinner

days.title: Milodon Cave and Cerro Dorotea
activities: Visit the Milodon Cave, a few kilometres from Puerto Natales, with interpretive trails across the Magellanic steppe where guanacos, foxes and rheas can be seen
Optional: Cerro Dorotea, the hill just outside town
Check weather and the park's daily report; pack for rain, wind and snow in any season

days.title: Into Torres del Paine: lakes and Salto Grande
activities: Drive from Puerto Natales to the park via Route Y-290: 115 km, about 1.5 hours per Chile's tourism board (up to 2 hours to some sectors); there is no public transport to the trailheads, so use a rental car or a tour

Your entry ticket must be bought online at pasesparques.cl at least 24 hours before entering; tickets are personal and tied to a date (changes allowed up to 24 hours before, refunds only if the park closes)

Foreign-adult entry is priced in CLP: the park's 2026 tariff page lists CLP 32,400 (day pass) and CLP 48,500 (more than 2 days), but CONAF introduced a one-day / 2+-day structure (2+ day ticket valid up to 10 consecutive days) on 1 May 2026, so confirm the current price on pasesparques.cl before paying
Easy stops: Salto Grande waterfall, Lago Pehoe, and the beach at Lago Grey where icebergs drift ashore
Sleep inside or beside the park (book lodging early, especially November to March)
days.lodging_suggestion: Lodge or hotel in or beside Torres del Paine

days.title: Lago Grey and Grey Glacier
activities: Catamaran trip on Lago Grey toward the Grey Glacier, about 3 hours on the water, past icebergs; book the boat well ahead in summer
Chile's tourism board gives an 80 km drive from the Torres-side lodgings to the western (Lago Grey) sector, so plan for the transfer
Short viewpoint walks near Lago Grey if time allows
days.lodging_suggestion: Lodge or hotel in or beside Torres del Paine

days.title: Base Torres day hike
activities: Hike to the Base Torres lookout under the granite towers; the park lists it as a medium/high difficulty day trail that needs no reservation, with entry to the trail only until 9:00 am and exit by 3:00 pm (check the park's tarifas y horarios page for the current rules)
Chile's tourism board estimates 7 to 10 hours depending on route; the park's notice says microspikes and trekking poles are required as safety gear on this trail
Register at ranger stations as required; do not cross rivers above knee height
Return to Puerto Natales in the evening

days.title: Back to Punta Arenas and Santiago
activities: Bus Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas, 3 hours; leave generous buffer for the flight
Evening flight Punta Arenas to Santiago (2 to 3.5 hours)
If you want the full multi-day W trek instead (3 to 5 days), lodging inside the park must be reserved in advance; without a reservation you will not be allowed into the mountain area

food_culture.name: Cordero patagonico
food_culture.description: Patagonian lamb is a regional staple, and Chile's tourism board lists it among the dishes to try in Puerto Natales.

food_culture.name: Centolla (southern king crab)
food_culture.description: Chilean tourism lists southern king crab among the Puerto Natales seafood to try, along with southern hake (merluza austral).

food_culture.name: Calafate sour
food_culture.description: A pisco sour made with calafate, a dark berry of the Patagonian steppe; local legend says that whoever eats calafate will return to Patagonia.

food_culture.name: Estancia culture
food_culture.description: Patagonia grew up around sheep estancias, and several, like Estancia Cerro Guido and Estancia Cerro Negro, offer visits and guided trekking, according to Chile's tourism board.

food_culture.name: Milodon Cave
food_culture.description: Named after the giant extinct ground sloth whose remains were found in the cave near Puerto Natales; the site is a reminder of the Ultima Esperanza region's deep natural history.

food_culture.name: Penguin colony at Isla Magdalena
food_culture.description: Los Pinguinos Natural Monument protects a colony of thousands of Magellanic penguins and their chicks; landing is only possible on a booked boat tour in the spring-summer season.

title: Quito, Cotopaxi, Baños + Cuenca, Ecuador
best_time_description: Ecuador's tourism site labels June to August the mountain season, the usual window for clearer skies on the Andean legs; it is high-altitude travel in any month, with Quito and several attractions above 2,700 m, so weather on Cotopaxi and in Cajas can turn quickly.
description: Ecuador's classic Andean first-timer line: Quito's UNESCO historic centre and the TelefériQo, a day in Cotopaxi National Park beneath the glaciated volcano, the waterfalls and hot springs of Baños, then Cuenca's colonial centre and Cajas National Park. Quito is high, so the first days are deliberately gentle.

days.title: Arrive Quito
activities: Arrive at Quito's Mariscal Sucre airport and go straight to the hotel; Global Affairs Canada warns that some Ecuadorian cities and attractions sit above 2,700 m, so keep the first evening easy and drink water
Short evening stroll in the La Floresta or Old Town area, with no strenuous climbs
Passport must be valid at least 6 months; visa-free visitors get a stay permit at the airport migration desk

days.title: Quito historic centre
activities: Walk Plaza Grande, the Cathedral and the Iglesia de la Compañía de Jesús in the UNESCO-listed historic centre, which Ecuador's tourism site calls the best preserved in the region
Visit the Basilica del Voto Nacional and Plaza de San Francisco
Dinner of locro de papa in the Old Town

days.title: TelefériQo and the middle of the world
activities: Ride the TelefériQo cable car (an 18-minute ride per the operator) up the slope of Pichincha to the Cruz Loma station at 4,050 m (UK FCDO figure); go up slowly, bring warm and rain layers, and turn back if altitude symptoms appear
Afternoon at the Mitad del Mundo monument complex north of Quito, where the equator is marked
Check the cable car's current opening hours on its own site before going

days.title: Cotopaxi National Park
activities: Travel by road from Quito into Cotopaxi National Park with a licensed local guide or an agency; the UK FCDO says high mountaineering on Cotopaxi is restricted and individual climbs are only allowed under the park's mandatory rules since November 2023, so plan a high-altitude walk, not a summit
Walk at Laguna Limpiopungo and the lower slopes with the glaciated cone in view; bring sun protection, layers, food and water
The FCDO notes a high risk of mixed flows of water, mud and debris around glaciated volcanoes including Cotopaxi: check current park and volcano status with the park or your operator the day before

days.title: Latacunga to Baños
activities: Continue by road through Latacunga toward Baños de Agua Santa, dropping from the high páramo to the subtropical valley; confirm the current bus or private-transfer time with the operator, as no official timetable was found
Soak in Baños's natural volcanic thermal waters, which Ecuador's tourism site names as a highlight
Evening in the town centre

days.title: Baños waterfalls and adventure
activities: See the Pailón del Diablo waterfall, which Ecuador's tourism site names among the area's spectacular cascades
Choose from rafting, canopy lines, or the Columpio del Fin del Mundo swing, all listed by the tourism site; book with a licensed operator
Check river levels and operator safety briefing before rafting

days.title: Baños to Cuenca
activities: Long overland day south to Cuenca by bus or private transfer; no official transit time was found, so check the operator's schedule and plan to travel in daylight, and consider a domestic flight from Quito or Guayaquil as an alternative if time is short
Evening on arrival in Cuenca's historic centre

days.title: Cuenca's historic centre
activities: Explore the UNESCO-listed colonial and republican centre, including Parque Calderón and the Catedral Nueva
Visit a toquilla-straw (Panama) hat workshop or shop; Ecuador's tourism site calls Cuenca a major centre for these hats
Visit the Pumapungo museum and its archaeological park, one of the archaeological points of interest inside the city

days.title: Cajas National Park and departure
activities: Morning trip to Cajas National Park, the high-altitude páramo reserve west of Cuenca: bring layers, rain gear and water, and expect the same altitude cautions as the rest of the Andes
Return to Cuenca for onward travel; allow time for the airport and check the flight status
Passport and any onward ticket should be at hand for departure

food_culture.name: Locro de papa
food_culture.description: A thick Andean potato soup, usually served with cheese and avocado, that is a staple in Quito and the highlands and an easy first meal at altitude.

food_culture.name: Hornado
food_culture.description: Slow-roasted pork served with potato and mote, a popular highland meal sold in markets and sit-down restaurants in Andean cities such as Quito and Cuenca.

food_culture.name: Mote pillo
food_culture.description: Hominy (mote) scrambled with egg and onion, a breakfast and snack associated with Cuenca and the southern highlands.

food_culture.name: Canelazo
food_culture.description: A hot drink of cinnamon, sugar and aguardiente, served in Andean towns on cold evenings.

food_culture.name: Cuy (guinea pig)
food_culture.description: Roasted guinea pig is a long-standing Andean festive dish in the highlands; it is served whole and is optional for visitors.

food_culture.name: Toquilla straw hats
food_culture.description: Ecuador's hats, popularly called Panama hats, are woven from toquilla straw and sold in Cuenca, which Ecuador's tourism site names as a major centre for them.

title: Galápagos: Santa Cruz, Isabela + San Cristóbal, Ecuador
best_time_description: The Galápagos Governing Council's inter-island boat page says seas are calmer from January to June and rougher from July to December, which matters on the two-to-three-hour boat legs between islands. Check each island's wildlife season with a licensed guide before choosing dates.
description: A land-based island-hop through three inhabited islands: Santa Cruz for the Charles Darwin Research Station and tortoises, Isabela for volcanoes and penguins, San Cristóbal for sea lions and snorkelling. Moves between islands use the daily small passenger boats; protected-area fees and the Transit Control Card apply.

days.title: Fly to Santa Cruz
activities: Before leaving the mainland: pay the USD 20 Transit Control Card (TCT) at the Quito or Guayaquil airport counter and present it at check-in; the Governing Council also requires a round-trip air ticket between the mainland and Galápagos, and arrival at the airport 3 hours before the flight

Foreign tourists must hold private health insurance before entering the province (ecuador.travel) and pay the conservation entry fee: USD 200 for adults, USD 100 for under-12s (CAN and Mercosur nationals USD 100 and USD 50)
Fly to Baltra's Seymour Airport and continue by road to Puerto Ayora; flight schedules are on the airport and airline websites

days.title: Puerto Ayora and the Darwin Station
activities: Visit the Charles Darwin Research Station and its giant tortoises, named on Ecuador's tourism site as a Santa Cruz highlight
Walk to Tortuga Bay for the beach and marine iguanas
Rules: visitor sites in the national park are visited with the park's rules; check the visitor-rules page of the Galápagos National Park Directorate

days.title: Highlands tortoise ranch, then boat to Isabela
activities: Morning at a giant tortoise ranch in Santa Cruz's highlands, which Ecuador's tourism site lists among the island's attractions

Afternoon boat Santa Cruz to Isabela: the Governing Council's permitted navigation window is 13:45 to 16:00 and the passage takes about 2 to 3 hours; the fare listed is USD 30 per person per route, tickets sold at agencies near the pier
Boats leave daily from the main pier; seas are rougher July to December

days.title: Isabela's volcanoes
activities: Take a guided day around Isabela, the largest island, with its chain of intermittently active volcanoes (ecuador.travel); book the guided visit with a licensed operator
Walk or cycle near the town: ecuador.travel lists cycling on Isabela and a tortoise breeding centre
Follow the park's visitor rules at all sites

days.title: Penguins and snorkelling off Isabela
activities: Snorkel or boat tour from Puerto Villamil; ecuador.travel notes Isabela is home to the only penguin species living in the tropics
Choose a licensed operator; the UK FCDO warns of several serious accidents involving Galápagos tour boats, so confirm life vests and safety gear before boarding
Return to town for a relaxed evening

days.title: Isabela to San Cristóbal via Santa Cruz
activities: Morning boat Isabela to Santa Cruz: permitted window 06:00 to 08:30, about 2 to 3 hours
Afternoon boat Santa Cruz to San Cristóbal: permitted window 13:45 to 16:00, about 2 to 3 hours, USD 30 per person per route
Both are small boats of up to 20 passengers; the connection is tight, so confirm both tickets in advance

days.title: San Cristóbal sea lions and coral reefs
activities: Spend the day on San Cristóbal, which ecuador.travel describes for its sea lions, tropical birds, giant tortoises and coral reefs for diving and snorkelling
Book snorkel or dive trips with licensed operators
Keep to marked trails and visitor sites

days.title: Departure from San Cristóbal
activities: Fly out of San Cristóbal Airport to the mainland on your round-trip ticket; the Governing Council advises arriving 3 hours before the flight
Confirm your total days in Galápagos: tourists are allowed up to 60 days a year, and a new TCT is paid for each trip
Keep passport and return documents ready

food_culture.name: Ceviche
food_culture.description: Ecuadorian ceviche is seafood marinated in citrus with tomato and onion, and fish dishes are a natural order in the Galápagos port towns.

food_culture.name: Fresh fish with patacones
food_culture.description: Local fish is typically served with fried green plantain (patacones) and rice; ask what the day's catch is.

food_culture.name: Galápagos coffee
food_culture.description: Coffee is grown in the highlands of San Cristóbal and is sold in cafes in the main town.

food_culture.name: Almuerzo set lunch
food_culture.description: The fixed-price midday set meal of soup, a main course and juice is the usual lunch across Ecuador and is common in Puerto Ayora and Puerto Villamil.

food_culture.name: Darwin and the conservation tradition
food_culture.description: The Charles Darwin Research Station on Santa Cruz, with its giant tortoise programme, frames the islands' tradition of conservation that visitors see in the entry fee, guides and visitor rules.

food_culture.name: Visitor rules as local etiquette
food_culture.description: Visitors keep to marked trails, do not touch or feed wildlife and go to protected visitor sites only with the park's authorisation; the national park's visitor rules are the baseline etiquette.

title: Santo Domingo, La Romana + Punta Cana, Dominican Republic
best_time_description: December to April is the driest, most comfortable window on both the capital and the east coast (the Dominican tourism board calls December to early March the most pleasant, with the highest hotel prices). Summer is the warmest and rainiest season and the Atlantic hurricane season runs 1 June to 30 November, with September the most active month; the board says a direct hit is unlikely but to expect to adjust plans if a storm is forecast.
description: The Americas' first colonial city on foot, then the Autopista del Coral east to the Altos de Chavon village, Saona Island and the beaches of Punta Cana. A classic first-timer arc: one city, one coast, one transfer of about two and a half hours.

days.title: Arrive Santo Domingo
activities: Land at Las Americas International Airport (SDQ), about 30 minutes from the capital according to the Dominican tourism board. Complete the free E-ticket entry/exit form at eticket.migracion.gob.do before you check in for the flight; airlines must see a round-trip air ticket to and from the Dominican Republic, so if you fly into SDQ and out of Punta Cana (PUJ), confirm with your airline that an open-jaw booking is accepted
Evening on the Malecon (George Washington Avenue), which the tourism board says comes alive at sunset and into the night
days.drive_time: About 30 minutes, airport to the capital

days.title: Colonial Zone
activities: Calle Las Damas, the first paved street in the Americas, and Fortaleza Ozama, the oldest European military structure in the New World
Alcazar de Colon and Plaza Espana, then the Primada de America Cathedral
Ruins of San Francisco monastery, then Calle El Conde and Parque Colon for lunch and an evening stroll

days.title: Beyond the old city
activities: Los Tres Ojos National Park, a cave park with underground lakes
Faro a Colon (Columbus Lighthouse)
National Botanical Garden or Mirador Sur park, then dinner back in the Colonial Zone

days.title: Santo Domingo to Punta Cana via La Romana
activities: Drive east on the Autopista del Coral (Route 3). The tourism board puts Punta Cana at about two and a half hours from Santo Domingo, and says the highway is under three hours end to end. Expect several toll booths (the board quotes RD$60 to RD$100 each); carry small Dominican pesos

Stop in La Romana for Altos de Chavon, a Mediterranean-style artists' village built as a replica, with museums and an amphitheater, above the Rio Chavon gorge. Speedboat, kayak and canoe trips on the river run year round according to the board
La Romana is 45 minutes from Punta Cana; check in and spend the evening on Playa Bavaro
days.drive_time: About 2.5 hours (under 3 hours on the Autopista del Coral)

days.title: Saona Island
activities: Full-day catamaran or boat excursion to Isla Saona, known for its beaches and natural pools; book it through a tour operator. Bayahibe, the gateway for the island boats, is about an hour from Punta Cana per the tourism board
Alternative: snorkel or dive off Isla Catalina
days.drive_time: About 1 hour, Punta Cana to Bayahibe

days.title: Scape Park and Macao Beach
activities: Scape Park in Cap Cana: Hoyo Azul, a cenote about 14 m deep reached across a suspension bridge and past an orchid garden, plus ziplines and other park activities (ask the park about entry and booking)
Afternoon at Playa Macao, which the board describes as a more natural setting with surfing, or Playa Juanillo's calm water

days.title: Depart Punta Cana
activities: Punta Cana International Airport (PUJ) is 15 minutes from Punta Cana and Cap Cana, 30 minutes from Bavaro and El Cortecito, and 45 minutes from Macao and Uvero Alto according to the tourism board. Leave time for the airline check-in; the E-ticket form also covers departure
days.drive_time: 15 to 45 minutes depending on the resort area

food_culture.name: La Bandera Dominicana
food_culture.description: The everyday Dominican lunch: white rice, stewed red beans and a stewed meat (often chicken or beef), usually with a side salad and fried plantain. Look for it as the plato del dia at comedores in the Colonial Zone and along Calle El Conde.

food_culture.name: Mangu
food_culture.description: Boiled, mashed green plantain topped with sauteed red onion, the classic Dominican breakfast, commonly served with fried eggs, fried cheese and salami (the 'tres golpes').

food_culture.name: Mamajuana
food_culture.description: A Dominican drink made by steeping rum, red wine and honey with tree bark and herbs in a bottle. Sold in bars and souvenir shops in Santo Domingo and the resort areas; treat it as a strong digestif.

food_culture.name: Merengue and bachata
food_culture.description: Both are Dominican music-and-dance forms that UNESCO has inscribed on its Intangible Cultural Heritage list (merengue in 2016, bachata in 2019). You will hear them in colmados, bars and on the Malecon at night.

food_culture.name: Colonial City of Santo Domingo
food_culture.description: The Colonial Zone is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 1990) and, per the Dominican tourism board, holds the first paved street, the first cathedral and the first monastery of the Americas. Santo Domingo was Culture Capital of the Americas in 2010.

food_culture.name: Habichuelas con dulce at Easter
food_culture.description: The Dominican tourism board notes that during Semana Santa Dominicans mark Holy Week with church on Good Friday and Holy Saturday and bowls of habichuelas con dulce, a sweet bean dessert. If you travel in Holy Week, expect closures, crowded beaches and very busy roads.

title: Puerto Plata, Jarabacoa + Samana, Dominican Republic
best_time_description: January to March is the prime window: humpback whale watching in Samana Bay is a January to March activity, and the mountain nights around Jarabacoa and Constanza are cold in those months (the tourism board says some Constanza mornings fall below freezing from November to March, so bring warm layers). Summer is the warmest and rainiest season and the Atlantic hurricane season runs 1 June to 30 November, with September the most active month.
description: The north coast's fortress, amber museum and kitesurfing beaches, up into the cool Cibao mountains for rafting, waterfalls and Valle Nuevo, then across to the Samana Peninsula for beaches and, in season, whales. A nature-first route that flies in and out of two different airports.

days.title: Arrive Puerto Plata
activities: Land at Gregorio Luperon International Airport (POP), 15 to 20 minutes from Puerto Plata city (the Dominican tourism board gives both figures on different pages). Complete the free E-ticket form at eticket.migracion.gob.do before check-in; airlines must see a round-trip air ticket to and from the country, so for a POP-in, El Catey-out plan confirm with your airline that an open-jaw booking is accepted
Evening walk on the Malecon of Puerto Plata and Independence Square
days.drive_time: About 15 to 20 minutes, airport to Puerto Plata

days.title: Puerto Plata old town and Isabel de Torres
activities: Fortaleza San Felipe, a 16th-century fortress turned museum overlooking the Atlantic
Amber Museum in a neo-classical house in the city centre, with amber pieces holding fossil animals
Cable car up Mount Isabel de Torres for views over the city and ocean
Paseo de Dona Blanca and the Umbrella Street for dinner

days.title: Sosua and Cabarete
activities: Sosua is about 15 minutes from POP airport per the tourism board: swim and snorkel at Sosua Beach, or at quieter Playa Alicia
Cabarete is just minutes beyond Sosua and is known as the kitesurfing capital; watch the kites or book a lesson
Alternative: a boat trip to Cayo Arena (Paradise Island), a sandbank off the northwest coast with shallow snorkelling

days.title: North coast to Jarabacoa
activities: Overland to Jarabacoa through Santiago. No official end-to-end time for Puerto Plata to Jarabacoa was found; the tourism board states Santiago to Jarabacoa is about 1 hour, so check a live map and leave margin, especially if you hire a car. The board also lists Caribe Tours coaches serving Puerto Plata, Santiago and Jarabacoa
La Confluencia, a riverside park about 10 minutes from downtown Jarabacoa where the Jimenoa and Yaque del Norte rivers meet; bring a picnic
days.drive_time: Santiago to Jarabacoa: about 1 hour (Puerto Plata to Santiago not verified)

days.title: Jarabacoa waterfalls, rafting and coffee
activities: Salto de Baiguate, a 25 m waterfall reached by wooden steps, about 20 minutes from town; a canyoning-and-rappelling excursion also ends here
Rafting the level-two rapids of the Yaque del Norte: organised trips run daily with certified guides, minimum age 14, and the tourism board says to reserve at least a day in advance
Cafe Monte Alto, a family coffee operation since the 1940s a few minutes from downtown, offers a tour of its factory (phone +1-809-574-2618 on the tourism board listing)

days.title: Constanza and Valle Nuevo
activities: Day trip to Constanza. No official Jarabacoa to Constanza time was found; the tourism board gives Constanza at about 2.5 hours from Santiago and 3.5 hours from Santo Domingo, so budget a long day and an early start
Salto de Aguas Blancas, an 83 m waterfall on a mountaintop mesa: the roughly 10 km ride up needs an all-terrain vehicle, and the pool is very cold (hypothermia warning from the board)
Las Piramides monument in Valle Nuevo National Park at about 2,300 m, with a small museum; early mornings can drop below freezing, so bring warm clothing

days.title: Cibao mountains to Samana
activities: Long transfer to the Samana Peninsula. No official Jarabacoa to Samana time was found. For scale, the tourism board gives Santo Domingo to Samana as 2.5 to 3 hours on Route 7 and Santo Domingo to Jarabacoa as about 2 hours on the Autopista Duarte; check a live map and plan for most of a day

Continue to Las Terrenas (about 2.5 hours from Santo Domingo per the board), take the Boulevard Turistico del Atlantico toll road if driving from Route 7 for the coastal views over the Bay of Coson, and watch the sunset on Playa Las Terrenas, a roughly 5 km stretch

days.title: Samana Bay and departure
activities: Pick one morning excursion. January to March: humpback whale watching in Samana Bay, the tourism board's headline attraction of the season. Other months: boat taxi from the Samana port on Avenida Marina to Cayo Levantado (visits can be restricted on days when large cruise ships dock off the island), or El Limon waterfall on horseback or on foot

Depart from El Catey International Airport (AZS), 30 minutes from Samana city and 30 minutes from Las Terrenas per the board, on a flight late enough to follow your excursion; or go by road to Santo Domingo (SDQ), 2.5 to 3 hours
days.drive_time: About 30 minutes to El Catey airport; 2.5 to 3 hours to SDQ

food_culture.name: Pescado con coco
food_culture.description: Fish simmered in a coconut sauce, the signature dish of the Samana peninsula and Las Terrenas, usually served with tostones (fried green plantain) and rice. Order it at beachfront restaurants in Las Terrenas and Samana town.

food_culture.name: La Bandera Dominicana
food_culture.description: The everyday Dominican lunch: white rice, stewed red beans and a stewed meat (often chicken or beef), usually with salad and fried plantain; the standard plate in the comedores of Puerto Plata and Jarabacoa.

food_culture.name: Jarabacoa mountain coffee
food_culture.description: Coffee grown in the high Cibao mountains; the tourism board names Cafe Monte Alto, produced by a local family in the coffee business since the 1940s, as one of Jarabacoa's best-known products and offers factory tours.

food_culture.name: Dominican amber of Puerto Plata
food_culture.description: Puerto Plata's Amber Museum displays Dominican amber, including pieces that hold insects, a lizard and plant material 15 to 20 million years old according to the tourism board; one mosquito-bearing stone was used in Jurassic Park. Amber jewellery is sold across the old town.

food_culture.name: Constanza's immigrant colonies
food_culture.description: The tourism board says Constanza's town centre reflects Japanese, Spanish and Hungarian colonies, and the cool highland farms around it grow strawberries, potatoes and carrots; Fresas Ariyama lets visitors pick strawberries on the farm.

food_culture.name: Carnival in February
food_culture.description: The tourism board describes Carnival in February as one of the biggest celebrations of the year, with Bonao and La Vega among the towns known for it. If your dates fall in February, expect crowds and plan accommodation early.

food_culture.name: Taino heritage of Samana
food_culture.description: The tourism board notes the Taino left pictographs and petroglyphs in caves, mainly in Samana, Bayahibe, San Cristobal and Enriquillo, and that Cacique Caonabo, from the Samana region, led the first revolt against Spanish colonisation.

title: Amman, Jerash, Petra, Wadi Rum + Dead Sea, Jordan
best_time_description: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are the usual windows for combining Petra and Wadi Rum on foot and by jeep. Midsummer is the hottest period in the desert south and at the Dead Sea, which lies about 427 m below sea level, so plan early starts then; check the Jordan Meteorological Department forecast before booking. The Jerash Festival usually runs from the end of July to the beginning of August.
description: Jordan's classic first-timer arc: Amman's hilltop Citadel and Roman Theatre, the Roman city of Jerash, a float in the Dead Sea, two days around the rose-red city of Petra and a night in a Wadi Rum desert camp, finishing in Aqaba on the Red Sea. A Jordan Pass bought before arrival bundles the visa fee, Jerash, Petra and Wadi Rum entry.

days.title: Arrive Amman
activities: Land at Queen Alia International Airport and get the visa on arrival (or the Jordan Pass visa waiver if you bought it before arrival and will stay the minimum nights)
Evening in downtown Amman: the Grand Husseini Mosque area and the souqs
Hummus and falafel at Hashem, one of the country's oldest restaurants

days.title: Jerash and Amman Citadel
activities: Jerash Archaeological City, about 45 km north of Amman: Hadrian's Arch, the Hippodrome, the Oval Plaza, the 800 m Cardo Maximus colonnaded street and the South Theatre (built 90-92 AD); entry is included in the Jordan Pass
The Roman Army and Chariot Experience (RACE) is held in the Hippodrome; check the current show schedule before planning around it
Late afternoon at the Amman Citadel (Temple of Hercules, Umayyad Palace) and the Roman Theatre, which seats about 6,000
Dinner and kunafa on or near Rainbow Street
days.drive_time: Amman to Jerash is about 45 km each way; your operator or driver should confirm the journey time on the day

days.title: Dead Sea float
activities: Transfer from Amman to the Dead Sea shore (the Amman-to-Dead Sea Ultra Marathon course is 42 km)
Float at a public beach or resort beach; the sea surface is about 427 m below sea level and the water is roughly ten times saltier than the ocean

Optional: Ma'in Hot Springs, 109 hot and cold springs with water up to 63 degrees C, or the Baptism Site (Bethany Beyond the Jordan, 12 JOD for non-Jordanians including shuttle and guide; add it to a Jordan Pass for 8 JOD)
Sunset over the Dead Sea; keep the water out of your eyes
days.drive_time: Amman to the Dead Sea is about 42 km (distance of the official Dead Sea Ultra Marathon course)
days.lodging_suggestion: Dead Sea resort area or return to Amman

days.title: Dead Sea or Amman to Petra
activities: Travel south to Wadi Musa, the town beside Petra; this is a full travel day, so start early and arrange a private driver or check JETT's schedule (jett.com.jo, customer service +962 6 566 4141, 24 hours)

Evening in Wadi Musa and, on Sunday to Thursday, Petra by Night: 8:30 pm to about 10:30 pm, 30 JOD per person, children under 10 free; it needs a daytime ticket or pass and is not included in the Jordan Pass

Petra ticket rules: overnight visitors pay 50 JOD for 1 day, 55 JOD for 2 days and 60 JOD for 3 days (Visit Jordan, January 2026); multi-day tickets must be used on consecutive days; a Jordan Pass (70/75/80 JOD for 1/2/3 days at Petra, bought online in advance at jordanpass.jo) covers daytime entry 6:00 am to 6:00 pm and is scanned only at the Petra Visitor Centre, not at the gates.
days.drive_time: Allow most of the day; confirm the exact road time with your driver or JETT

days.title: Petra: Siq, Treasury and Monastery
activities: Walk the Siq to the Treasury (Al-Khazneh) early in the day, then the Street of Facades and the Royal Tombs
Climb the ancient rock-cut steps to the Monastery (Ad-Deir) on the moderate main trail, which can be done without a guide; the Ad-Deir back route is rated hard and guided only, about 4-5 hours
Petra Museum is open daily 8:30 am to 7:30 pm
Children under 12 enter Petra free in daylight hours; bring your passport to the ticket office

days.title: Petra to Wadi Rum
activities: Morning at Petra if you hold a 2- or 3-day ticket or pass, or leave for Wadi Rum
Transfer to Wadi Rum village and the visitor centre; book your 4x4 jeep tour through your camp or at the visitor centre (Wadi Rum entry is included in the Jordan Pass)
Sunset jeep tour over the sand dunes and rock bridges, then dinner and a night in a desert camp
days.drive_time: Petra to Wadi Rum: confirm the road time with your camp or driver when booking; JETT lists Wadi Rum as a route

days.title: Wadi Rum to Aqaba
activities: Sunrise in the desert, then morning jeep or camel route if time allows
Transfer to Aqaba and a swim or snorkel on the Red Sea
Evening on the Aqaba waterfront
days.drive_time: Confirm Wadi Rum to Aqaba road time with your camp or driver

days.title: Aqaba to Amman and depart
activities: JETT coach or transfer from Aqaba to Amman; Aqaba is approximately 4 hours from Amman by road (Visit Jordan); the JETT Aqaba terminal on King Hussein Street is open 6:30 am to 1:00 am
Fly home from Queen Alia International Airport, or from Aqaba's King Hussein International Airport to skip the drive
days.drive_time: Aqaba to Amman is approximately 4 hours by road

food_culture.name: Hummus and falafel
food_culture.description: Amman's breakfast and lunch staple; Hashem in downtown Amman is described by Visit Jordan as one of the oldest restaurants in the country, famous for hummus and falafel.

food_culture.name: Mansaf
food_culture.description: Jordan's national dish of lamb served over rice with a fermented dried-yogurt (jameed) sauce, traditionally eaten from a shared platter at celebrations and family gatherings.

food_culture.name: Nabulsi kunafa
food_culture.description: A hot cheese pastry soaked in syrup. Habiba Sweets in Amman is named by Visit Jordan as one of the most famous places for kunafa, with queues for its Nabulsi version.

food_culture.name: Bedouin tea and coffee
food_culture.description: At Wadi Rum desert camps, sweet tea and cardamom-spiced coffee are poured as a welcome and repeated throughout the visit; accepting a cup is part of the hospitality.

food_culture.name: Zarb
food_culture.description: A Bedouin feast of meat and vegetables cooked in a pit oven buried in the sand, served at many Wadi Rum camps in the evening; ask your camp if it is on the menu.

food_culture.name: Roman and Nabataean heritage
food_culture.description: Jerash's Roman streets and theatres and Petra's Nabataean rock-cut tombs sit in one country; Jerash's Hippodrome stages Roman Army and chariot re-enactments, and the Jerash Festival of music, theatre and folklore usually runs from late July into August.

title: Madaba, Karak, Dana + Aqaba, Jordan
best_time_description: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) suit Dana's walking trails and the Red Sea; midsummer is hot in Aqaba, so plan snorkelling early in the day. Karak's museum keeps shorter winter hours (8:00 am to 3:00 pm) than its summer hours (8:00 am to 6:00 pm). Check Dana's trail and lodge availability with the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature before you go.
description: A quieter route down the King's Highway: Madaba's Byzantine mosaics and Mount Nebo, the Ma'in hot springs, Karak's Crusader castle, a night in the Dana Biosphere Reserve with its walking trails, and snorkelling in the Red Sea at Aqaba. It covers the northern end of the Jordan Trail corridor without needing to hike the whole thing.

days.title: Arrive Amman, transfer to Madaba
activities: Land at Queen Alia International Airport and clear the visa on arrival (or the Jordan Pass visa waiver)
Transfer to Madaba, described by Visit Jordan as a short distance from the capital; confirm the transfer time with your hotel or driver
Evening walk in Madaba's old town

days.title: Madaba, Mount Nebo + Ma'in Hot Springs
activities: Madaba's St George's Church and its 6th-century mosaic map of the Holy Land, now 10.5 m by 5 m with some 700,000 to 800,000 tesserae
Mount Nebo, the highest point of the ancient Kingdom of Moab
Ma'in Hot Springs, 37 km from Madaba, about 264 m below sea level with water up to 63 degrees C
Optional: Umm ar-Rasas, UNESCO-listed in 2004, or Machaerus (Mukawir) in the hills south-west of Madaba
days.drive_time: Madaba to Ma'in Hot Springs is 37 km

days.title: Karak Castle and on to Dana
activities: Karak Castle, 900 m above sea level, with stone-vaulted halls; the best-preserved are underground, reached through a large door (ask at the ticket desk); on clear days you can see across the Dead Sea to the Mount of Olives
Karak Archaeological Museum is open 8:00 am to 6:00 pm in summer and 8:00 am to 3:00 pm in winter; the Mazar Islamic Museum is open 8:30 am to 3:30 pm except Tuesday
Continue south to Dana Biosphere Reserve; book your stay in advance through the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature (rscn.org.jo/reserve/1)
days.drive_time: Karak to Dana is the Jordan Trail's Karak to Dana section, 84.5 km on foot over 5 hiking days; by road, confirm the time with your driver
days.lodging_suggestion: Dana Biosphere Reserve (guesthouse or Rummana campsite, booked via RSCN)

days.title: Dana Biosphere Reserve
activities: Walking trails in Jordan's largest and first biosphere reserve, set up in 1989, 292 km2, from over 1,500 m down to Wadi Araba; the trail map and 2026 trail rates are on the RSCN reserve page
Check with RSCN whether a guide is required for your chosen trail before you set out
Evening at the guesthouse or Rummana campsite

days.title: Dana to Aqaba
activities: Travel to Aqaba, about 4 hours from Amman and on the Red Sea
Waterfront walk and dinner in Aqaba

If you entered Jordan at Aqaba, the ASEZA free-visa rule applies; if you arrived elsewhere, register at the ASEZA visa office in Aqaba within 48 hours of arrival to claim it, or pay the usual 40 JOD visa
days.drive_time: Confirm Dana to Aqaba road time with your driver; Aqaba is approximately 4 hours from Amman

days.title: Red Sea snorkelling and diving
activities: Snorkelling or diving in the Gulf of Aqaba, whose sites include sunken boats, a tank and a C-130 Hercules aircraft scuttled on 16 November 2017 (the Cedar Pride was scuttled on 16 November 1985)
Book a licensed dive centre or boat in advance; bring your own certification card if diving
Sunset on the Aqaba waterfront

days.title: Depart Aqaba or return to Amman
activities: Fly from Aqaba's King Hussein International Airport, or take a JETT coach from the Aqaba terminal on King Hussein Street (open 6:30 am to 1:00 am) to Amman, about 4 hours by road, for a Queen Alia departure
Exit fee: an exit service fee applies at sea and land borders (8 JOD per passenger according to Aqaba authority sources)
days.drive_time: Aqaba to Amman is approximately 4 hours by road

food_culture.name: Mansaf
food_culture.description: The national dish: lamb in a sauce of jameed (dried fermented yogurt) over rice, served for celebrations and shared hospitality; Visit Jordan's Karak page lists a mansaf cooking experience as worth the time it takes.

food_culture.name: Maqluba
food_culture.description: A 'flipped over' pot of rice, vegetables and meat or chicken turned out onto a platter at the table; common in family kitchens and local restaurants across the King's Highway towns.

food_culture.name: Arabic coffee
food_culture.description: Cardamom-scented coffee poured in small cups as a sign of welcome; taking a cup and shaking the cup to signal 'enough' is part of the custom.

food_culture.name: Biosphere hospitality
food_culture.description: Dana's guesthouse and campsite are run by the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature, which also manages the reserve's trails, so a night there supports the reserve itself.

food_culture.name: Madaba mosaics
food_culture.description: Madaba is known for Byzantine-era floor mosaics, above all the 6th-century map of the Holy Land in St George's Church, one of the oldest surviving maps of the region.

title: Nairobi, Maasai Mara + Lake Nakuru, Kenya
best_time_description: The Maasai Mara is busiest during the wildebeest migration, whose river-crossing window is usually put at roughly July to October (timing shifts year to year with the rains, so no date is guaranteed). January and February are the other dry, easier-travel months; the long rains (roughly April to May) are the quiet, muddy low season. Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers vary with water levels and are not reliable in any given month.
description: Kenya's classic first safari: a day or two in Nairobi, the Rift Valley lakes at Naivasha and Nakuru (a walk or cycle among zebra and giraffe at Hell's Gate, rhino at Nakuru), then the Maasai Mara for game drives, returning to Nairobi by air. Fees: park and reserve entry fees are set by the managing authority (Kenya Wildlife Service for the national parks, Narok County Government for the Maasai Mara National Reserve), change by season and by residency, and could not be confirmed from an official page when this was researched, so none are quoted: check the current tariff and pay online in advance where required.

days.title: Arrive Nairobi
activities: Land at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO) and complete your approved eTA arrival checks; carry the eTA confirmation and the Kenyan government travel health insurance confirmation that applicants buy during the eTA process from 5 October 2026
Transfer to your hotel by a pre-arranged transfer; avoid driving at night (FCDO advice) and use a reputable operator rather than touts
Rest; no activities planned

days.title: Nairobi National Park + Karen
activities: Morning game drive in Nairobi National Park, a national park on the city's edge managed by Kenya Wildlife Service (rhino, lion, giraffe with the skyline behind; pay the KWS entry fee online in advance where required)
Visit the Giraffe Centre or the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage in Karen; Sheldrick visits are limited and need to be booked ahead through the Trust
Afternoon at the Karen Blixen Museum or Kazuri bead centre

days.title: Nairobi to Lake Naivasha + Hell's Gate
activities: Road transfer from Nairobi to Lake Naivasha in the Rift Valley with a driver-guide; confirm the travel time with your operator at booking, and avoid travelling after dark
Boat trip on Lake Naivasha among hippos and birdlife; you may not swim in the lake (swimming in Kenyan park lakes and rivers is illegal per FCDO)
Optional late afternoon at Hell's Gate National Park, where walking and cycling among zebra, giraffe and buffalo is permitted (KWS entry fee applies); guides are available at the gate

days.title: Hell's Gate gorge + Lake Nakuru National Park
activities: Morning walk into Hell's Gate gorge with a guide if you did not go yesterday (KWS park)
Transfer on to Nakuru and game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park (KWS entry fee applies): white and black rhino, Rothschild's giraffe, buffalo, and flamingos when water conditions favour them
Sunset at Baboon Cliff viewpoint above the lake

days.title: Transfer to the Maasai Mara
activities: Travel from Nakuru to the Maasai Mara by road via Narok (a long transfer; confirm the time with your operator, and the final stretch is unpaved), arriving in time for an evening game drive
Alternatively, return to Nairobi's Wilson Airport and take a scheduled light-aircraft flight to a Mara airstrip; flight times and baggage limits are set by the airline you book
Reserve entry is paid to Narok County Government; the county's site says tickets can be purchased online, so book ahead where you can
days.drive_time: Road via Narok, long transfer (confirm with operator) or scheduled flight from Wilson Airport

days.title: Maasai Mara game drives
activities: Dawn game drive for big cats; Mara is known for lion, cheetah, leopard, elephant and hippo
Picnic breakfast or lunch in the reserve, then an afternoon drive
If your dates fall in the roughly July to October window, ask your guide for the Mara River crossing points; sightings are not guaranteed, and crossings depend on the herds
Optional Maasai village visit arranged through your camp; ask what the fee covers and where it goes

days.title: Maasai Mara full day
activities: Full-day game drive with packed lunch, covering a different part of the reserve (Musiara, Mara Triangle or Talek areas, as your camp operates)
Optional dawn hot-air balloon flight over the reserve, which has to be booked in advance with an operator
Evening at camp; keep to camp rules about walking at night

days.title: Return to Nairobi + departure
activities: Morning drive, then fly from the Mara airstrip to Wilson Airport in Nairobi (booked in advance), or return by road with your operator
Connect to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your onward flight; leave a generous buffer between a Mara flight and an international departure
days.drive_time: Scheduled flight Mara airstrip to Wilson Airport (confirm times with the airline)

food_culture.name: Nyama choma
food_culture.description: Grilled goat or beef roasted over coals and eaten with kachumbari (a fresh tomato and onion salad) and ugali, at roadside butcheries and bars across Nairobi and the Rift Valley towns.

food_culture.name: Ugali with sukuma wiki
food_culture.description: Ugali is a stiff maize-meal staple eaten by hand; sukuma wiki is braised collard greens, the usual side to nearly every Kenyan meal.

food_culture.name: Kenyan chai
food_culture.description: Black tea boiled together with milk and sugar (often spiced), served at roadside kiosks and in lodges; Kenya is a major tea-growing country.

food_culture.name: Maasai culture
food_culture.description: The Maasai are pastoralists around the Mara, known for beadwork and red shukas (wraps); camps arrange village visits, and travellers should ask how the fee is shared with the community.

food_culture.name: Rift Valley and Mara wildlife conservation
food_culture.description: Nairobi National Park, Lake Nakuru and the Mara sit under different managers (Kenya Wildlife Service and Narok County), and visitors are expected to follow park rules on staying in vehicles and on tracks.

title: Amboseli, Tsavo + the Diani Coast, Kenya
best_time_description: The dry months, January to February and June to October, are easiest for game drives in Amboseli and Tsavo, and Amboseli's views of Mount Kilimanjaro (across the border in Tanzania) are usually clearest early in the morning. The migration is a Maasai Mara event and does not reach this route. The coast is hot and humid year round, with the long rains (roughly April to May) the wettest and quietest period.
description: A different Kenya from the Mara: elephants under Kilimanjaro at Amboseli, the big open landscapes of Tsavo West and Tsavo East, then Swahili Mombasa and Diani Beach on the Indian Ocean, with the option of the Madaraka Express SGR train. Fees: park and reserve entry fees are set by the managing authority (Kenya Wildlife Service for the national parks, Narok County Government for the Maasai Mara National Reserve), change by season and by residency, and could not be confirmed from an official page when this was researched, so none are quoted: check the current tariff and pay online in advance where required.

days.title: Arrive Nairobi
activities: Land at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO); carry your approved eTA and the Kenyan government travel health insurance confirmation that applicants buy during the eTA process from 5 October 2026
Transfer to your hotel by pre-arranged transport; avoid driving at night (FCDO advice) and use a reputable operator rather than touts

days.title: Nairobi to Amboseli National Park
activities: Road transfer south to Amboseli with a driver-guide (confirm the travel time with your operator), arriving for an afternoon game drive
Amboseli is a Kenya Wildlife Service park known for large elephant herds and, in clear weather, views of Mount Kilimanjaro across the Tanzanian border

days.title: Amboseli game drives
activities: Dawn drive when Kilimanjaro is usually clearest
Visit the swamp areas where elephants and hippos gather, with a mid-day rest at the lodge
Optional visit to a Maasai community arranged by your lodge; ask how the fee is shared

days.title: Amboseli to Tsavo West
activities: Transfer from Amboseli to Tsavo West National Park (KWS park) by road with your operator; confirm the travel time with them
Afternoon game drive; Tsavo West is rugged, with volcanic scenery

days.title: Tsavo West: Mzima Springs + Shetani lava
activities: Visit Mzima Springs, where hippos and fish can be seen from a viewing area (do not swim; swimming in park waters is illegal per FCDO)
Walk around the Shetani lava flow and caves with a ranger, as permitted
Afternoon game drive

days.title: Tsavo West to Tsavo East
activities: Transfer to Tsavo East National Park, entering by a gate your operator chooses (KWS entry fee applies)
Game drive along the Galana River, where Tsavo's elephants are often seen coated in red dust

days.title: Tsavo East to Mombasa
activities: Morning drive; then head to Mombasa by road with your operator

Alternative: take the Madaraka Express SGR train to the Mombasa Terminus (Miritini) from the station nearest your park exit; the schedule and which stations are served must be checked on the Kenya Railways ticketing site (metickets.krc.co.ke) because the timetable could not be verified when this was researched
Evening in Mombasa Old Town
days.drive_time: Road or SGR (confirm times on the operator or Kenya Railways site)

days.title: Mombasa Old Town + Fort Jesus to Diani
activities: Fort Jesus, the 16th-century Portuguese fort and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with its museum; check opening hours before you go
Walk through Old Town's lanes; FCDO notes crime risk is higher in Old Town and around the Likoni Ferry, so keep valuables hidden and travel in daylight
Cross by the Likoni Ferry (or drive the long way) to the south coast and settle at Diani Beach
days.drive_time: Likoni Ferry and road (confirm with your operator)

days.title: Diani Beach + departure
activities: Morning on Diani Beach and in the Indian Ocean; snorkelling or dhow trips arranged through your hotel
Depart from Moi International Airport in Mombasa or from Ukunda airstrip near Diani; confirm which airport your flight uses and leave a generous buffer for the ferry

food_culture.name: Swahili pilau
food_culture.description: Spiced rice cooked with meat and cumin, cardamom and cloves, a coastal staple shaped by centuries of Indian Ocean trade.

food_culture.name: Mahamri with coconut beans
food_culture.description: Cardamom-scented fried bread served with coconut-stewed beans, a typical coastal breakfast in Mombasa and Diani.

food_culture.name: Madafu (fresh coconut)
food_culture.description: Young coconuts opened with a machete and sold on the beach and by the roadside along Diani and the Mombasa coast.

food_culture.name: Swahili hospitality and dress
food_culture.description: Coastal Kenya is predominantly Muslim, so away from resorts dress modestly, especially in Mombasa; FCDO gives this advice for the coast.

food_culture.name: Fort Jesus and Old Town Mombasa
food_culture.description: Fort Jesus, built by the Portuguese in the 1590s, anchors an Old Town that blends Swahili, Arab, Portuguese and Indian influences.

title: Tarangire, Ngorongoro Crater + Serengeti, Tanzania
best_time_description: The dry season suits Tarangire: TANAPA says the Tarangire River draws large herds of elephants and other animals to its banks then. For the Serengeti, an operator-published account puts the wildebeest in the southern Serengeti and Ngorongoro area from January to March (calving), moving back south from early November with the short rains. Rain falls roughly March to May and in October-November (Coastal Aviation's Serengeti page), so June to September and January-February are the picks here. That month list is an editorial judgement, not a met-service measurement, and the herds' exact position changes year to year.
description: The classic northern safari circuit in seven days: Arusha, Tarangire's elephants and baobabs, the Ngorongoro Crater, then the Serengeti, with a scheduled light-aircraft flight back to Arusha. Costs and rules to know before booking: TANAPA park fees and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area (NCAA) entry and crater service permits are charged per person and the TANAPA fee covers 24 hours from entry, so each night inside Serengeti or Tarangire adds a fee day; children under 5 enter TANAPA parks free. TANAPA's online tariff page is labelled financial year 2023/2024, so confirm current fees with your operator, who pays them at the gate. Vehicles for hire in the NCA must be registered company vehicles with a valid TALA licence, and the crater floor is 4x4 only, so book a licensed operator (TTB publishes a list of blacklisted operators). Foreign visitors also need Tanzania's mandatory inbound travel insurance from 1 October 2026 (see the visa rules).

days.title: Arrive Kilimanjaro or Arusha
activities: Arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) or transfer from Arusha
Rest and settle in Arusha; Arusha is the base for the northern parks
Before you travel: apply for your e-visa at visa.immigration.go.tz (or buy on arrival), keep your return ticket and, if you are arriving from a yellow-fever-risk country, your vaccination certificate
Buy the mandatory inbound travel insurance for your first point of entry (mainland: National Insurance Corporation, inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz) and keep the QR code

days.title: Arusha to Tarangire National Park
activities: Road transfer into Tarangire National Park (TANAPA)
Game drive along the Tarangire River; TANAPA describes large elephant herds, baobab trees and over 550 bird species
TANAPA lists walking safaris, night game drives and sunrise balloon flights as activities in Tarangire; these are booked through an operator and not all lodges offer them
Park fee applies per person for each 24 hours from entry
days.drive_time: Road transfer; no park authority publishes a drive time, so ask your licensed operator to quote it before you book

days.title: Tarangire to the Ngorongoro highlands
activities: Morning game drive in Tarangire before leaving the park
Road transfer to the Ngorongoro Conservation Area rim or the nearby town of Karatu
Afternoon at leisure; the NCA is a World Heritage area and plastic bags are not allowed inside it per NCAA guidelines
Pay attention to driving hours in the NCA: NCAA says driving is permitted between 06:00 and 18:00 unless you obtain permission
days.drive_time: Road transfer; no park authority publishes a drive time, so ask your licensed operator to quote it before you book

days.title: Ngorongoro Crater floor
activities: Early descent into Ngorongoro Crater with a licensed guide; NCAA requires a licensed or official NCAA guide to accompany all crater visitors and only 4x4 vehicles up to 3,500 kg are allowed on the crater floor

NCAA says the crater descent gates close at 16:00, speed limit on the crater is 25 km/h, visitors must stay in the vehicle outside designated areas, and no more than 5 vehicles may gather at a sighting
The crater service permit is single entry, so you cannot re-enter the same day after leaving
Return to the rim for the night; picnics are allowed only at designated public areas

days.title: Ngorongoro to the central Serengeti
activities: Road transfer from the NCA highlands to Serengeti National Park, with game viewing across the plains
Optional stop at Olduvai Gorge and its new museum, which NCAA lists as an attraction; confirm museum opening times locally
Enter Serengeti National Park (TANAPA fee applies; TANAPA's tariff page puts Serengeti in a higher fee band than Tarangire)
Evening game drive around Seronera, the central Serengeti where Coastal Aviation lists an airstrip
days.drive_time: Road transfer; no park authority publishes a drive time, so ask your licensed operator to quote it before you book

days.title: Full day in the Serengeti
activities: Dawn game drive; TANAPA calls the Serengeti home to the highest concentration of large carnivores and the annual wildebeest migration
Optional sunrise hot air balloon ride, a TANAPA-listed activity that needs advance booking through an operator
Mid-day bush meal or rest at the lodge
Afternoon game drive; the migration's exact position depends on the season and changes every year, so ask your operator where the herds are

days.title: Fly Serengeti to Arusha
activities: Morning game drive
Coastal Aviation's published timetable lists a Serengeti to Arusha flight departing 10:45 and arriving 11:45; times can change, so confirm with reservations@coastal.co.tz
Connect to your onward flight from Kilimanjaro (JRO) or stay a night in Arusha
If you prefer the road back, ask your operator for the full-day drive option instead
days.drive_time: Coastal Aviation scheduled flight, 10:45 to 11:45 (1 hr) per its published timetable; confirm before booking

food_culture.name: Nyama choma
food_culture.description: Grilled meat, usually goat or beef, cooked over charcoal and shared at roadside grills and local bars across the Arusha region; ask for it with ugali and kachumbari salad.

food_culture.name: Ugali and sukuma-style greens
food_culture.description: Ugali is a stiff maize porridge eaten with the hand, the everyday staple served alongside stews, greens and grilled fish or meat across mainland Tanzania.

food_culture.name: Maasai, Hadzabe and Datoga peoples
food_culture.description: NCAA's own cultural heritage pages name the Maasai, Hadzabe and Datoga as the peoples of the conservation area. NCAA says photographing local people is prohibited except in designated cultural bomas, so ask before taking any photo.

food_culture.name: Olduvai Gorge and the human-origins story
food_culture.description: NCAA presents Olduvai Gorge and the Laetoli footprints as major archaeological sites of the conservation area, a reminder that the same landscape holds some of the oldest traces of early humans.

food_culture.name: Chai and Tanzanian coffee
food_culture.description: Spiced milk tea (chai) is served at most lodges and roadside stops, and coffee is grown on the slopes around Arusha and Kilimanjaro; both are easy first-morning drinks before a dawn game drive.

title: Nyerere Safari + Zanzibar Stone Town and Beaches, Tanzania
best_time_description: This route avoids the northern circuit and Mount Kilimanjaro altogether: one safari park in the south, then the coast. Tanzania's rains fall roughly March to May and in the short-rains months of October to December (an operator-published Serengeti and Mafia season note; the national met service TMA publishes a yearly Vuli short-rains outlook). The suggested months, January-February and June-September, sit outside those rains but are an editorial judgement, not a measured recommendation. Note that Coastal Aviation says tourism on the nearby island of Mafia largely closes during the long rains, so check lodge opening dates for March to May.
description: A southern safari in Nyerere National Park (formerly the Selous Game Reserve, now Africa's largest national park according to TANAPA) followed by Zanzibar's Stone Town and beaches, all by short scheduled flights. No Kilimanjaro or Serengeti involved. Fees and rules: Nyerere is in the same higher TANAPA fee band as Serengeti, charged per person for each 24 hours, with children under 5 free; TANAPA's online tariff page is labelled financial year 2023/2024 so confirm today's amount with your lodge. Coastal Aviation's timetable lists Dar es Salaam to Selous flights and Selous to Zanzibar flights, with each flight landing at the airstrip of your lodge (Beho Beho, Kiba, Matambwe, Mbuyu, Mtemere, Siwandu, Sumbazi or Stiegler's Gorge). Inbound travel insurance is mandatory: if you land in Dar es Salaam first, a National Insurance Corporation policy is enough for the mainland and Zanzibar for 92 days, according to a Zanzibar Insurance Corporation notice dated 7 October 2026.

days.title: Arrive Dar es Salaam
activities: Arrive at Dar es Salaam (DAR); the city is the starting point for scheduled flights into Nyerere

Before you travel: Tanzania e-visa at visa.immigration.go.tz (or a visa on arrival), a return ticket, six months' passport validity, and a yellow-fever certificate if you are coming from a risk country
Buy the mandatory inbound travel insurance for your first point of entry (mainland: National Insurance Corporation at inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz) and keep the QR code for scanning

days.title: Fly to Nyerere, boat safari on the Rufiji
activities: Coastal Aviation's published timetable lists Dar es Salaam to Selous flights at 08:30 (arriving 09:15), 10:45 (arriving 11:30) and 16:30 (arriving 17:35); times change by airstrip, so confirm with your lodge
Transfer to your lodge or camp at one of the park's airstrips
Afternoon boat safari on the Rufiji River; TANAPA notes Nyerere's sandbanks, oxbow lakes and river channels shelter over 440 bird species and Nile crocodiles
days.drive_time: Coastal Aviation scheduled flight, 08:30 to 09:15 (45 min) per its published timetable; confirm before booking
days.lodging_suggestion: Nyerere National Park lodge or camp

days.title: Game drive and walking safari in Nyerere
activities: Morning game drive; TANAPA says Nyerere has most of the Big Five except rhinos and a high concentration of wildlife
Walking safaris with armed rangers are described by Coastal Aviation as one of the park's most exciting activities, offered by some lodges and booked in advance
Afternoon rest or a second boat safari on the Rufiji
TANAPA fee applies per person for each 24 hours from entry
days.lodging_suggestion: Nyerere National Park lodge or camp

days.title: Nyerere to Zanzibar
activities: Last morning game drive or boat safari at the lodge
Coastal Aviation's timetable lists two Selous to Zanzibar flights, 09:15 to 11:20 and 13:15 to 14:20; the later one allows a full morning in the park (confirm before booking)
Arrive at Abeid Amani Karume International Airport (ZNZ) and transfer to Stone Town
Evening stroll in Stone Town's coral-stone lanes
days.drive_time: Coastal Aviation scheduled flight, 13:15 to 14:20 (about 1 hr 5 min) per its published timetable; confirm before booking

days.title: Stone Town on foot
activities: Walk Stone Town, once the trading port of the Sultans of Oman and known for its carved wooden doors and coral-stone houses (Coastal Aviation's Zanzibar page)
Visit the Old Fort (Ngome Kongwe) and the Darajani market area; opening hours and any entry fees were not verified, so check locally
Evening at Forodhani Gardens waterfront, where street-food stalls set up after dark; eat only freshly cooked food

days.title: Spice farm and Jozani Forest, or Prison Island
activities: Half-day spice farm tour near Stone Town, booked through a licensed Zanzibar operator
Jozani Chwaka Bay National Park to see Zanzibar red colobus monkeys; confirm entry fee and guide rules locally
Alternative: boat trip to Changuu (Prison Island) from Stone Town to see the giant tortoises
Return to Stone Town or move to the coast
days.lodging_suggestion: Stone Town or east coast, Zanzibar

days.title: Beach day on Zanzibar's coast
activities: Beach day on the east coast (Paje or Jambiani) or the north coast (Nungwi or Kendwa); the east-coast sea level changes noticeably with the tide, so check tide times before planning a swim
Snorkelling or a dhow trip arranged through your hotel with a licensed operator
Sunset dinner at a beachfront restaurant

days.title: Depart Zanzibar
activities: Transfer to Abeid Amani Karume International Airport (ZNZ); keep your inbound insurance QR code handy
Coastal Aviation lists hourly Zanzibar to Dar es Salaam flights (per its timetable), useful for an international connection at DAR; leave generous time for the connection
Check your return ticket and passport validity before departure

food_culture.name: Zanzibar mix (urojo)
food_culture.description: A tangy street-food soup of potato, bhajia fritters, cassava and chutney, a local favourite in Stone Town; ask what the stall's broth contains if you are avoiding any ingredient.

food_culture.name: Pilau and seafood curry
food_culture.description: Spiced pilau rice and coconut-based fish or octopus curries reflect the island's Swahili, Arab and Indian trading history; widely served in Stone Town restaurants.

food_culture.name: Swahili spice trade
food_culture.description: Zanzibar is known as the Spice Island; cloves, cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla grow on farms near Stone Town and can be seen on guided farm tours.

food_culture.name: Stone Town's carved doors and sultanate history
food_culture.description: Coastal Aviation's Zanzibar page highlights Stone Town's carved doors, coral-stone houses and the trading port of the Sultans of Oman as the heart of Swahili and Arab culture on the island.

food_culture.name: Forodhani waterfront food market
food_culture.description: After dark, stalls line the Forodhani Gardens waterfront in Stone Town grilling seafood and skewers and serving sugarcane juice; the evening market is a long-running local tradition.
